items.subject: The Escapardenne Eisleck Trail, Kautenbach to La Roche
items.text: A seven-day thru-walk on the Escapardenne Eisleck Trail from Kautenbach to La Roche-en-Ardenne, plus a Lee Trail sampler from Vianden.

trip_data.title: The Escapardenne Eisleck Trail, Kautenbach to La Roche
trip_data.gateway: Luxembourg (LUX)

itinerary.title: Kautenbach and the trailhead
itinerary.morning: Train from Luxembourg City to Kautenbach, a small station on the main Luxembourg-Liège line that doubles as the Eisleck Trail's start point. Drop bags at the guesthouse.
itinerary.afternoon: Short orientation walk along the Wiltz river below the village, checking the trail's stylised waymark (a white-and-orange "É" on green background) before the real distance begins tomorrow.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner; the week's longest stage is next.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km, 150 m ascent, 150 m descent. Grade easy forest and riverside path, no exposure.

itinerary.title: Stage 1: Kautenbach to Wiltz
itinerary.morning: Climb out of the Wiltz valley onto open plateau farmland, the trail alternating between hedgerowed fields and beech forest.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend into Wiltz, the Éislek's largest town, known for its open-air festival amphitheatre and its château.
itinerary.evening: Wiltz has the week's best choice of restaurants; a good night to eat properly.
itinerary.dayStats: 22 km, 480 m ascent, 460 m descent. Waymark: white-and-orange Escapardenne blaze on green post, standard forest and field track.

itinerary.title: Stage 2: Wiltz to Boulaide
itinerary.morning: The trail leaves Wiltz through the Wiltz forest, one of the larger continuous woodland blocks on the route, before opening onto the plateau again.
itinerary.afternoon: Rolling farmland to Boulaide, a small village near the Luxembourg-Belgium border, with the plateau's characteristic long sightlines over hedgerowed pasture.
itinerary.evening: Boulaide's single guesthouse is the only overnight option, confirmed ahead is essential.
itinerary.dayStats: 24 km, 420 m ascent, 400 m descent. Grade easy, gravel and forest track throughout.

itinerary.title: Stage 3: Boulaide to Insenborn
itinerary.morning: The trail turns toward the Lac de la Haute-Sûre, Luxembourg's largest reservoir, through forest that thickens as the ground drops toward the water.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive at Insenborn on the lake's southern shore, with an afternoon free to walk the lakeside path or simply sit by the water, the only substantial lake on the whole route.
itinerary.evening: Fish features on every local menu here; the lake is stocked and actively fished.
itinerary.dayStats: 19 km, 380 m ascent, 420 m descent. Grade easy, lakeside and forest track.

itinerary.title: Stage 4: Insenborn to Nadrin, crossing into Belgium
itinerary.morning: The trail follows the lake shore before climbing away from the water and crossing the unmarked Luxembourg-Belgium border into the southern Ardennes.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue through Belgian forest to Nadrin, a small village on a bend of the Ourthe, with a viewpoint over the river's horseshoe loop at nearby Le Hérou.
itinerary.evening: First night in Belgium; note the transport pattern changes here, Belgian regional buses are not part of Luxembourg's free network.
itinerary.dayStats: 23 km, 500 m ascent, 480 m descent. Grade easy to moderate, more forest track, occasional root and stone underfoot.

itinerary.title: Stage 5: Nadrin to La Roche-en-Ardenne
itinerary.morning: The final stage follows the Ourthe valley's forested flank, with repeated views down to the river's meanders.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend into La Roche-en-Ardenne, the trail's terminus, a small town below a ruined medieval castle at the river's most dramatic bend.
itinerary.evening: A proper finish-line dinner; La Roche has more restaurant choice than anywhere since Wiltz.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km, 380 m ascent, 460 m descent. Grade easy, forest track, one steady climb out of Nadrin.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Vianden and the Lee Trail
itinerary.morning: Bus from La Roche to Bastogne, then train back into Luxembourg and up to Vianden, gateway to the Escapardenne Lee Trail, the Eisleck Trail's northern sister route.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Lee Trail's opening stretch from Vianden along the Our valley toward Stolzembourg, a shorter sampler day that shows the second trail's character, tighter valley, more river, less open plateau, before looping back to Vianden.
itinerary.evening: Depart from Vianden or return to Luxembourg City for the flight home.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km, 320 m ascent, 320 m descent. Grade easy to moderate, valley path with one climb above Stolzembourg.

items.subject: San Marino & the Montefeltro: Towers, Truffles and Block-Printed Linen
items.text: Two nights on a limestone crag that has been an independent republic since the fourth century, then four in the Malatesta hill country that surrounds it. San Marino is best understood as a strange, steep, self-governing village rather than a curiosity, and it is transformed the moment the last day-tripper takes the cable car down. Below it, the Montefeltro gives you San Leo's cliff fortress, Pennabilli's poet's gardens, Verucchio's Iron Age museum and Santarcangelo's tufa caves and printing workshop, all within a 40 km radius. One move, two open afternoons, and, if you time it for October, four Sundays of white truffle in Sant'Agata Feltria. It suits people who like small, dense places and don't need a coastline.

source.verified: Borgo Maggiore market confirmed as Thursday, 06:00-14:00, Piazza Grande, with a monthly antiques market on the third Sunday, March-December. Sant'Agata Feltria's Fiera Nazionale del Tartufo Bianco Pregiato 2026 confirmed for Sundays 4, 11, 18 and 25 October plus 1 November 2026. San Marino's use of the euro outside EU membership confirmed.

trip_data.title: San Marino & the Montefeltro: Towers, Truffles and Block-Printed Linen
trip_data.best_period: Late April-June & September-early November (October for the truffle fair)
trip_data.avoid: Mid July-August, when Rimini's coastal traffic clogs every approach road and Monte Titano bakes; also February, when Montefeltro fog sits all day and hill restaurants close
trip_data.budget: €1,100 to €1,700 per person, excl. international flights
trip_data.difficulty: 2, the Titano ridge path between the towers and San Leo's approach are steep but short; nothing longer than 4 km
trip_data.gateway: RMI, Rimini Federico Fellini, 30 min to San Marino; BLQ Bologna is the bigger hub, 1 h 40 by car or 1 h by train to Rimini plus a 50 min bus

itinerary.title: Up Monte Titano
itinerary.morning: Land at Rimini and take the Bonelli bus or a car up to San Marino, the road climbs 700 m in 20 km and the republic appears as a wall of rock with buildings on top of it. Leave the car in the multi-storey car parks below the walls.
itinerary.afternoon: Check in inside the walls, then walk the ridge: Guaita first, then the Passo delle Streghe to Cesta, where the museum of ancient weapons sits at the republic's high point.
itinerary.evening: The town after 18:00 is a different place. Aperitivo on Piazza della Libertà, then dinner at Ristorante Righi or a smaller osteria off Contrada Omerelli, try the nidi di rondine, Romagna's baked rolled pasta.
itinerary.dayStats: RMI-San Marino 27 km / 35 min; Bonelli bus roughly 50 min, about €5 each way, 10-12 daily. Cesta at 755 m. Two-tower ticket roughly €7 to €10.

itinerary.title: Market morning below the crag
itinerary.morning: Take the cable car down to Borgo Maggiore, 90 seconds, and the best two euros in the republic, for the Thursday market on Piazza Grande from 06:00. Cheese, cured meat, plants, cheap clothes and locals doing their weekly shop.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk back up the old path rather than riding, then the State Museum and the Basilica del Santo Marino. Late in the day, the terrace outside Cesta faces the Adriatic and, on clear days, shows the Croatian coast.
itinerary.evening: Second night on the crag, and the only night it makes sense to eat late in the upper town. Piadina and Sangiovese if you want the honest version.
itinerary.dayStats: Cable car 1.5 min, roughly €2.80 single / €4.50 return, every 15 min. Market 06:00-14:00 Thursday. Uphill path 1.8 km / 200 m.

itinerary.title: San Leo's cliff, then down to Santarcangelo
itinerary.morning: Drive south-west to San Leo, where a fortress sits on a sheer sandstone block above a village of 300 people. Cagliostro died in a cell here in 1795 with no door, food was lowered through the ceiling. The Romanesque Pieve and Duomo below are the best of their kind in the region.
itinerary.afternoon: North to Santarcangelo di Romagna, on the flat, and check in. Walk the tufa grotte beneath the hill, a network of tunnels of contested purpose, and then Piazza Ganganelli.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Osteria La Sangiovesa in the Palazzo Nadiani, a Romagnolo institution of piadina, tagliatelle and a great deal of Sangiovese.
itinerary.dayStats: San Marino-San Leo 25 km / 40 min; San Leo-Santarcangelo 35 km / 45 min. San Leo at 601 m, fortress entry roughly €10. Grotte tour about 45 min, €4 to €6.

itinerary.title: Printing linen, then nothing at all
itinerary.morning: Stamperia Marchi for the block-printing session: choose a pear-wood block, ink it in rust dye, press it onto linen, and watch the mangano, a stone-weighted wooden press from the 1700s, finish the cloth.
itinerary.afternoon: Blank. Santarcangelo is a town made for sitting: the arcades of Via Cesare Battisti, a bar table, a book. If you must move, the Rocca Malatestiana is a ten-minute walk up.
itinerary.evening: Piazza Ganganelli fills from 18:30. Eat where the queue is, and order the cappelletti in brodo if it's autumn.
itinerary.dayStats: Workshop 60-90 min, roughly €25 to €45 depending on the cloth. Santarcangelo at 42 m, the only flat night of the week. Rocca walk 700 m / 45 m.

itinerary.title: Verucchio and the Marecchia valley
itinerary.morning: Verucchio, 15 km up the valley, for the Museo Civico Archeologico, the Villanovan princely burials found here are among the richest Iron Age finds in Italy, with 8th-century BC textiles and a wooden throne. Then the Rocca Malatestiana on the ridge.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue up the Marecchia to Pennabilli for Tonino Guerra's gardens: the Orto dei Frutti Dimenticati with its forgotten fruit varieties and hand-painted ceramics, and the Giardino Pietrificato's mosaics.
itinerary.evening: Back down the valley. Dinner in Santarcangelo again, the advantage of a four-night base.
itinerary.dayStats: Santarcangelo-Verucchio 15 km / 20 min; Verucchio-Pennabilli 35 km / 50 min. Verucchio at 333 m, Pennabilli at 629 m. Museum entry roughly €6 to €8; Guerra's gardens free.

itinerary.title: Sant'Agata Feltria, truffles and an idle afternoon
itinerary.morning: Sant'Agata Feltria for the Sunday truffle fair if you are here in October, the whole village turns into a market, with the Rocca Fregoso above and the 1605 Teatro Angelo Mariani open. Out of season, come anyway for the theatre and a quiet lunch.
itinerary.afternoon: Nothing scheduled. Drive back over the ridge slowly, stop where the view is good, and be back in Santarcangelo by mid-afternoon.
itinerary.evening: Last dinner. If it's truffle season, this is the night to spend money on a plate of tagliolini al tartufo bianco.
itinerary.dayStats: Santarcangelo-Sant'Agata Feltria 45 km / 1 h. Sant'Agata at 607 m. Fair Sundays: 4, 11, 18, 25 October and 1 November 2026. White truffle at fair prices roughly €200 to €400 per 100 g depending on the season.

itinerary.title: Rimini, and out
itinerary.morning: Drive or train down to Rimini. The Tempio Malatestiano, Alberti's unfinished 15th-century masterpiece, and the Roman Ponte di Tiberio are both a short walk from the station.
itinerary.afternoon: Return the car at Rimini airport, or take the Adriatic line north to Bologna in about an hour for a wider choice of flights.
itinerary.evening: Flight home.
itinerary.dayStats: Santarcangelo-RMI 15 km / 20 min. Santarcangelo-Rimini by regional train 8 min, 1-2 hourly. Rimini-Bologna 1 h by Frecciarossa, 1 h 20 by Regionale.

items.subject: Kungsleden North: Abisko to Nikkaluokta
items.text: A seven-day hiking & alpine trekking itinerary in Lapland, Norrbotten, Abisko and Kebnekaise massif, Sweden.

trip_data.title: Kungsleden North: Abisko to Nikkaluokta
trip_data.best_period: Late June to mid-September, matching the STF staffed-hut season and the boat services. July has mosquitoes and midnight sun; the first half of September has autumn colour, no insects and the first frosts
trip_data.budget: €865 to €1,410 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.
trip_data.difficulty: Moderate-hard. About 105 km over 6 walking days on a well-marked, bridged trail; one pass at 1,150 m; the difficulty is distance, weather and remoteness rather than technicality

itinerary.title: Abisko: arrival and the Abisko canyon
itinerary.morning: Arrive by the Stockholm-Narvik night train to Abisko Turiststation (about 17 h, and one of Europe's best rail journeys), or fly to Kiruna and take the bus.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Abisko canyon where the Abiskojåkka river cuts a gorge through red rock, and see the Lapporten, the U-shaped glacial gate that is the symbol of Swedish Lapland. Weigh your pack, buy last gas canisters at the station shop.
itinerary.evening: Abisko Turiststation. Brief yourself on the route board and register your plan.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km

itinerary.title: Abisko to Abiskojaure
itinerary.morning: The trailhead arch at Abisko is the northern terminus of the Kungsleden, the King's Trail. Birch forest, boardwalk over wet ground, the river always to your left.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive Abiskojaure hut on the lake, a group of red-painted cabins with a sauna by the water.
itinerary.evening: Sauna and a lake swim at 8 °C. Water: the river and its tributaries the entire way; Swedish mountain water is drinkable untreated above the treeline and generally safe here.

itinerary.title: Abiskojaure to Alesjaure
itinerary.morning: Climb out of the birch into open fell. The valley widens; the trail is stony but clear, marked with cairns and red-painted rocks.
itinerary.afternoon: Alesjaure sits above a lake chain with Sámi settlements nearby, this is a working reindeer-herding landscape, not a wilderness in the empty sense. The hut has one of the best saunas on the trail, on a hill with a view down the valley.
itinerary.evening: Sámi-operated boat services run on the Alesjaure lakes in season and can shorten this stage significantly if weather or blisters demand it. `verify: true`

itinerary.title: Alesjaure to Tjäktja and over the pass to Sälka
itinerary.morning: Gentle climb up the Tjäktjavagge valley, a classic glacial trough, wide, treeless and enormous.
itinerary.afternoon: The Tjäktja pass at about 1,150 m is the highest point of the Kungsleden and the watershed of the trip. There is an emergency shelter at the top. Descend into the long valley to Sälka.
itinerary.evening: Sälka hut, with a shop and a sauna. If the day is too long, break it at Tjäktja hut before the pass. Water: streams throughout; the pass itself is dry for about 4 km.

itinerary.title: Sälka to Singi and Kebnekaise Fjällstation
itinerary.morning: Down the valley to Singi, where the Kungsleden continues south and our route turns east into the Kebnekaise massif.
itinerary.afternoon: The Ladtjovagge valley approach to Kebnekaise Fjällstation, with the massif rising ahead. The station is a full mountain centre, restaurant, shop, sauna, guides.
itinerary.evening: Proper food and a bed. Book the guided summit day now if you want it.

itinerary.title: Kebnekaise south summit
itinerary.morning: Sweden's highest mountain. The eastern route is the standard non-glaciated ascent, long, steep, rocky, and hard but unguided-feasible for fit, experienced walkers. The western route crosses the Björling glacier and requires a guide, rope and crampons.
itinerary.afternoon: The south summit is a glacier-capped peak whose height changes measurably from year to year as the ice cap melts, it has now dropped to roughly the same height as the ice-free north peak, which is itself a lesson in what is happening up here.
itinerary.evening: Back at the station. Sauna. This is the hardest day of the week by a wide margin, treat the weather forecast as a veto, not a suggestion. Water: streams to about 1,400 m only; carry 2 litres.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km return, 1,700 m, 10-14 h

itinerary.title: Kebnekaise to Nikkaluokta and out
itinerary.morning: The exit valley to Nikkaluokta, a Sámi village and the road head. A boat across Ladtjojaure lake cuts about 6 km off the walk when it is running.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus Nikkaluokta-Kiruna (about 1 h 20), then flight or the night train south. Eat a reindeer burger at the Nikkaluokta café; it is a tradition and it is earned.
itinerary.dayStats: 19 km, mostly descending

items.subject: The Balaton Ring: Seven Days Around Hungary's Inland Sea
items.text: Balaton is shallow, jade-green and 77 km long, and the ring around it is flat enough that all the climbing is voluntary. This week rides the paved Balatoni Bringakör anticlockwise, then leaves it twice, over the…

trip_data.title: The Balaton Ring: Seven Days Around Hungary's Inland Sea
trip_data.best_period: mid-May to mid-June, then the first three weeks of September
trip_data.avoid: late July-August (heat, Balaton crowds, and a path that jams solid between Siófok and Zamárdi)
trip_data.difficulty: Moderate
trip_data.gateway: Budapest Ferenc Liszt (BUD), then MÁV line 26 (Kelenföld → Balatonfüred → Tapolca, 2 h 10) north shore, or line 29 (Székesfehérvár → Siófok → Nagykanizsa) south. Hévíz-Balaton (SOB) has limited seasonal traffic.

itinerary.title: Arrival, Csopak and a shakedown
itinerary.morning: Train in, collect the bike, set it up properly, saddle height, brake reach, rack bolts. Coffee on the Tagore sétány, the lime-shaded Balatonfüred promenade where Tagore planted a tree in 1926.
itinerary.afternoon: East on the separated path to Csopak, then inland to Jásdi Pince or Figula Pincészet for Csopaki Olaszrizling, flinty and high-acid off Permian red sandstone. On to Alsóörs and its red-sandstone Turkish House, then back.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Kisfaludy Ház on the hillside, terrace looking straight down the peninsula, or cheaper and better at Baricska Csárda below it. Mákos guba at Bergmann Cukrászda. Early night: tomorrow has the best climb.

itinerary.title: Tihany, the abbey, and the volcanic west
itinerary.morning: Flat path to Tihany-rév, then the climb in the small ring. At the top, the twin-towered Tihanyi Bencés Apátság, founded 1055, whose charter holds the oldest written Hungarian words. Walk Echo Hill for the Belső-tó, the crater lake sitting 25 m above Balaton.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to Aszófő, through Örvényes, Balatonudvari and Balatonakali, where the path fails and road 71 begins, take the parallel village streets at Zánka and Balatonszepezd. Fogas lunch at Révfülöp, then 12 km under the Badacsony basalt.
itinerary.evening: Base in Badacsony. Climb the vineyard road to Laposa Birtok for Kéknyelű and Juhfark facing the water, or to Szent Orbán Borház higher up for dinner over the whole lake.

itinerary.title: Káli basin: gravel, basalt organs, stone seas
itinerary.morning: Off the ring. Climb through Káptalantóti to Kővágóörs, then gravel into the Káli-medence, hayfields, dry-stone walls, volcanic buttes. Stop at the Szentbékkálla kőtenger, a field of wind-carved sandstone blocks you can scramble on.
itinerary.afternoon: Farm track to Salföld Major and its grey cattle, racka sheep and buffalo, then Kékkút, the spring behind every Theodora bottle in Hungary. Finish at the Hegyestű Geológiai Bemutatóhely above Monoszló: a quarried cone whose sheared face is a wall of hexagonal basalt columns.
itinerary.evening: Eat at Káli Art Inn in Köveskál, or taste at Villa Sandahl in Kővágóörs. Descend to Badacsony with Szent György-hegy (415 m) and Csobánc (376 m) black against the sky.

itinerary.title: Szigliget, Kis-Balaton and the Festetics
itinerary.morning: Leave the bikes below Szigliget and walk 20 minutes to Szigligeti Vár, the 13th-century castle that never fell to the Ottomans and owns the western basin view. Down for the flat run to Balatonederics.
itinerary.afternoon: Packed limestone past Fenékpuszta, where the Zala leaves the Kis-Balaton marshes, spoonbills, purple herons, hundreds of great white egrets in September. Into Keszthely on the lakefront path.
itinerary.evening: The Festetics-kastély, 101 rooms and a 90,000-volume Helikon Library, is the best interior on the lake. Dinner at Bacchus Étterem. If legs allow, spin 5 km to Hévíz and float on the 33-36 °C thermal lake.

itinerary.title: South shore, sphere lookout, and Kistücsök
itinerary.morning: South to Balatonberény, where the path leaves road 71 for good and runs flat behind the reeds. Balatonmáriafürdő, Balatonfenyves and the kisvasút crossings, the fastest 25 km of the week, and a tailwind leg in the usual north-westerly.
itinerary.afternoon: Ramp up to Fonyód's Bélatelep villa terrace for the postcard of Badacsony and Szigliget across the water, then Balatonboglár and the 1960s concrete Gömbkilátó on Várdomb, before dropping to Balatonlelle and Konyári Pincészet for the south shore's most serious red.
itinerary.evening: Sleep in Balatonszemes and eat at Kistücsök, thirty years the best restaurant on Balaton, built around the lake's own fish and Somogy's growers, book ahead. Natural wine afterwards at Bakos Bar, a few doors along.

itinerary.title: Szántód, the ferry, back to the north
itinerary.morning: Easy path through Balatonszárszó, pause at the József Attila memorial, where the poet died in 1937, then Balatonföldvár and Zamárdi, with the Szamárkő boulder above the village for one more climb.
itinerary.afternoon: The Szántód-Tihany car ferry, BAHART's crossing of the lake's narrowest point (~1.5 km), takes seven minutes, runs year-round and carries bikes without fuss, 1,000 HUF for the passenger and 400 HUF for the bike, so about €3.50 (1,400 HUF) all in, with under-14s free and a car at 3,100 HUF (BAHART tariff from 1 June 2026). It trades the dull 40 km Siófok arm for the best short boat ride in Hungary.
itinerary.evening: Climb from Tihany-rév to the village once more in evening light, then coast to Balatonfüred. Dinner at Vitorlás Étterem by the Round Church, then out along the pier as the yacht club boats come in.

itinerary.title: The eastern arm, and out
itinerary.morning: East to Alsóörs, then the short inland ramp to Felsőörs and its 13th-century Romanesque provost's church, the finest small church on the lake and almost always empty.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to Balatonalmádi, up to the Óvári kilátó for the last panorama, then the Wesselényi beach for a swim: still around 20 °C in September.
itinerary.evening: Return the bike, then the train from Balatonalmádi or Balatonfüred. With three spare hours, ride the extra 12 km to Balatonkenese and Balatonfűzfő and close the ring by wheel rather than by ferry.

items.subject: Vranec & Stanušina: The Tikveš Basin and the Vardar Road
items.text: Tikveš is the largest continuous vineyard region in the Balkans and almost nobody visits it. The basin sits between the Vardar and the Kožuf mountains, gets around 270 sunny days a year, and grows Vranec, the black, tannic national grape, alongside Stanušina, a pale indigenous red found nowhere else. The week runs south from Skopje through Negotino, Kavadarci and Demir Kapija, staying in wineries that built their own rooms because there were no hotels, then east to Štip for pastrmajlija. Come in September and the whole country is outdoors making ajvar over open fires.

source.verified: Popova Kula operating as a winery with hotel rooms, restaurant and structured tastings at Demir Kapija, with bookable tasting and dinner-plus-accommodation formats; Tikveš Winery at Kavadarci as a visitable estate founded 1885 and the largest in south-east Europe; Tikveš's position within the Povardarie/Vardar Valley wine region; the endemic status of Stanušina to the Tikveš basin.

trip_data.title: Vranec & Stanušina: The Tikveš Basin and the Vardar Road
trip_data.best_period: Late April-mid-June & September-late October
trip_data.avoid: July-mid-August, the Tikveš basin is the hottest place in the country at 38-42°C with almost no shade
trip_data.budget: €850 to €1,435 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.
trip_data.difficulty: 2/5, vineyard walking, the Stobi site on gravel, a short climb at Marko's Towers
trip_data.gateway: SKP Skopje, 1 h 20 min drive to Negotino, 1 h 35 min to Kavadarci; OHD Ohrid 2 h 30 min

itinerary.title: Skopje: Bit Pazar and the Old Bazaar
itinerary.morning: Land at SKP, 20 minutes from the centre. Walk the Stone Bridge into the Old Bazaar, the largest surviving Ottoman bazaar in the Balkans outside Istanbul.
itinerary.afternoon: Bit Pazar, pepper mountains in September, ajvar pots, dried beans for tavče gravče, sheep cheese, rakija sold by the funnel.
itinerary.evening: Pivnica An in a restored caravanserai for kebapi and tavče gravče, or Stara Kuća for the fuller spread.
itinerary.dayStats: SKP 20 min / bazaar meal MKD 400-800 (€7 to €13) / market ajvar 1 kg jar MKD 300-500 (€5 to €8) / no driving today

itinerary.title: South to Stobi and Negotino
itinerary.morning: The A1 down the Vardar to Stobi, the Roman and early Byzantine city at the Crna-Vardar confluence, mosaics, a theatre, the Episcopal basilica, and effectively empty midweek.
itinerary.afternoon: Stobi Winery next door for a first Vranec and a Temjanika, then on to Bovin at Negotino, the country's first private winery.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Popova Kula on arrival at Demir Kapija; the kitchen pairs the winery's own range.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km Skopje-Stobi, 1 h 10 m / Stobi entry MKD 120-300 (€2 to €5) / 2 wineries / tastings MKD 600-1,500 (€10 to €24) each

itinerary.title: Demir Kapija and the Stanušina question
itinerary.morning: Popova Kula's own tasting, working through Vranec, Kratošija, Temjanika and, the reason to be here, Stanušina as both a light red and a rosé.
itinerary.afternoon: The Demir Kapija gorge, the "iron gate" where the Vardar cuts through the mountains, then the winery's collection of dozens of local varieties grown side by side.
itinerary.evening: Stay in; Demir Kapija has little else, which is exactly why the winery built rooms.
itinerary.dayStats: 1 winery / Keif-style tasting MKD 900-1,800 (€15 to €29) / Stanušina bottle MKD 500-900 (€8 to €15) / no driving

itinerary.title: Kavadarci, Tikveš Winery and Lake Tikveš
itinerary.morning: Driver day. Tikveš Winery at Kavadarci, founded 1885, the largest in south-east Europe, and its Barovo and Lepovo single-vineyard programme.
itinerary.afternoon: Out to Lake Tikveš, the reservoir on the Crna, for a boat hour and the vineyard slopes above it.
itinerary.evening: A Kavadarci kafana for tavče gravče baked to order in its earthenware dish, and a carafe of house Vranec.
itinerary.dayStats: 32 km / 1 winery / tasting MKD 700-1,600 (€11 to €26) / driver day €150 to €280 per car / Vranec Reserve MKD 700-1,400 (€11 to €23)

itinerary.title: Ajvar over the fire, and rakija
itinerary.morning: In September, the hands-on morning: an ajvar session, crates of red peppers roasted over an open grill, peeled hot, minced and slow-cooked in oil for hours. Arranged through your host, not sold as a tour.
itinerary.afternoon: A rakija distillation visit in a Tikveš village if you are here in October or November; otherwise a cellar visit at Lazar Winery or Château Sopot.
itinerary.evening: Eat what you made. Ajvar with sheep cheese, bread and grilled meat is the correct end to the day.
itinerary.dayStats: Ajvar session 4-6 h / ~10 kg peppers yields ~3 kg ajvar / rakija 40-50% abv / visit fees MKD 500-1,200 (€8 to €20)

itinerary.title: East to Štip for pastrmajlija
itinerary.morning: Drive north-east to Štip, the textile city on the Bregalnica, and climb to the Isar fortress above it.
itinerary.afternoon: Pastrmajlija from a dedicated pastrmajlijarnica, the oval bread with cubed pork and a cracked egg, ordered by size and eaten with a hot pepper and a beer.
itinerary.evening: Back west toward Skopje, or a night in Štip. Stop at Chateau Kamnik on the Skopje approach for a last serious tasting.
itinerary.dayStats: 105 km Demir Kapija-Štip, 1 h 30 m / pastrmajlija MKD 200-400 (€3 to €7) / Kamnik tasting MKD 900-1,800 (€15 to €29)

itinerary.title: Matka, last market, and out
itinerary.morning: Matka Canyon, 30 minutes from Skopje, a gorge, a reservoir and Vrelo cave, and the country's easiest morning off.
itinerary.afternoon: Last buys at Bit Pazar: ajvar, dried peppers, sheep cheese and a bottle of Stanušina that will be almost impossible to find at home.
itinerary.evening: SKP is 25 minutes from the centre. Wine over one litre goes in the hold; there are duty limits leaving for the EU.
itinerary.dayStats: Matka 30 min each way / boat to Vrelo MKD 300-600 (€5 to €10) / SKP 25 min / EU duty allowance 4 l still wine per adult

items.subject: Златни мостове - Алеко
items.text: An 8 km walk with 521 m of climbing, about 2 h 43 min of walking. It tops out at 1,856 m, mostly on footpaths. On the way: the huts hizha Aleko and Gorski dom Tintyava, and the peak Kamen del (1,860 m). Usually clear of snow from June to October.

items.subject: Klaipeda, Lithuania
items.text: Lithuania's port city of Prussian timber houses, gateway to the Curonian Spit

source.text: Klaipėda is a city in Lithuania Minor, the narrow northwest coastal region of Lithuania. It's the country's third-largest city. The city has historic sights but isn't pretty-pretty like Vilnius Old Town, and draws mostly local tourism.

items.subject: Lucerne in a day
items.text: Lucerne in a day is a one day city sightseeing walk between the city's main sights in Switzerland. The day is anchored in Lucerne and features 9 sightseeing stops.

items.subject: Fredrikstad, Norway
items.text: Scandinavia's best-preserved fortress town, moats and cobbled lanes still fully intact

source.text: Fredrikstad is a city and municipality in Østfold county in Norway, home to around 85,000 people (2023). Its old town is Northern Europe's best preserved fortified town.

items.subject: Camino Lituano Žemaitija
items.text: Camino Lituano Zemaitija is a waymarked hiking route located in LT. The route spans a distance of 215.6 km within the national waymarked hiking network.

items.subject: Tallinn: Limestone, Bastions & Telliskivi
items.text: A seven-day city trip itinerary in Harju County, Gulf of Finland, Estonia.

trip_data.title: Tallinn: Limestone, Bastions & Telliskivi
trip_data.best_period: May to September for terraces and white nights; December for the Town Hall Square Christmas market; January-February is bitter, beautiful and half price
trip_data.budget: €785 to €1,560 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.

itinerary.title: Lower Old Town: the Hanseatic block
itinerary.morning: Tram 4 from the airport, 15 minutes. Start at Town Hall Square (Raekoja plats) with the only surviving Gothic town hall in Northern Europe, and the pharmacy on its corner, trading since 1422 and claiming to be Europe's oldest continuously operating one.
itinerary.afternoon: The merchant streets: Pikk with its guild halls, the Great Guild, the House of the Blackheads, and the Three Sisters merchant houses. Climb St Olaf's Church tower, briefly the tallest building in the world in the 16th century, for the best rooftop view in the Baltics.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in the Old Town but off Viru, Rataskaevu 16 and its neighbours are where Estonians actually eat inside the walls. Book ahead; it is small.

itinerary.title: Toompea and the bastion tunnels
itinerary.morning: Up the Lühike jalg passage to Toompea, the upper town of nobility and power: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, the Riigikogu parliament in its pink Baroque castle, and the Kohtuotsa and Patkuli viewing platforms.
itinerary.afternoon: Kiek in de Kök and the Bastion Passages, 17th-century Swedish tunnels under the earthworks, later used as Soviet bomb shelters and, in the 1980s, by the city's punks. Guided entry only, and genuinely cold; take a jacket.
itinerary.evening: Walk the surviving town wall towers, then down to the Rotermann Quarter for dinner in the converted mill and factory buildings between the Old Town and the port.

itinerary.title: Kalamaja and Telliskivi
itinerary.morning: Kalamaja, the wooden district: pastel 1920s-30s "Lender houses" with limestone bases, once fishermen's and factory workers' homes and now the most desirable address in the city. Balti Jaam Market for breakfast, three floors of produce, street food and secondhand.
itinerary.afternoon: Telliskivi Creative City, a former railway repair complex: Fotografiska Tallinn, independent design shops, and a rotating wall of street art. Then walk the Kultuurikilomeeter seafront path.
itinerary.evening: Noblessner, the old submarine shipyard turned waterfront quarter, a brewery taproom, a seafront promenade, and the city's most ambitious restaurants. This is where to spend your one big dinner.

itinerary.title: Kadriorg and KUMU
itinerary.morning: Tram 1 or 3 to Kadriorg: Peter the Great's Baroque palace and gardens, built after the Great Northern War, with the Kadriorg Art Museum inside.
itinerary.afternoon: KUMU, the Estonian national art museum, a copper-and-limestone building cut into the escarpment. Its 20th-century floors, covering the occupation years and Soviet-era nonconformist art, are the most affecting museum experience in the Baltics.
itinerary.evening: Walk to Pirita along the sea, past the Song Festival Grounds where 300,000 people sang during the 1988 Singing Revolution. Eat at the Pirita marina.

itinerary.title: Seaplane Harbour and the Soviet edge
itinerary.morning: Lennusadam (Seaplane Harbour), a 1917 seaplane hangar of pioneering thin-shell concrete, now a maritime museum with the submarine Lembit sitting inside it. Excellent for all ages.
itinerary.afternoon: Patarei, a Tsarist sea fortress that became a Soviet prison, now partly open as a memorial to the victims of communism and Nazism. Sobering and essential; check the current opening status. `verify: true` Then Linnahall, the crumbling 1980 Olympic concrete monument on the shore, best seen from outside.
itinerary.evening: Kalamaja neighbourhood dinner, then a sauna, Estonian sauna culture is as serious here as in Finland and several public saunas operate in the city.

itinerary.title: Helsinki day trip or Lahemaa
itinerary.morning: Option A: the fast ferry to Helsinki, roughly 2 hours each way, giving five hours in the Finnish capital, enough for the Design District and a market lunch. Option B: drive or take a tour to Lahemaa National Park for manor houses, bog boardwalks and the Baltic coast.
itinerary.afternoon: Whichever you chose, be back for the evening; the last ferries fill in summer.
itinerary.evening: Old Town cellar bars, or a folk-music evening if one is on.

itinerary.title: Markets and departure
itinerary.morning: Balti Jaam Market or the Sunday flea section for last purchases; coffee in Kalamaja.
itinerary.afternoon: Tram 4 to the airport, or the ferry terminal for the Helsinki connection. Tallinn Airport is 4 km from the centre, the shortest airport transfer in this dataset.

items.subject: Saas-Fee, Switzerland
items.text: Car-free 'Pearl of the Alps' ringed by thirteen 4,000 m peaks, with the world's highest revolving restaurant

source.text: Saas-Fee is the biggest town in the Saas valley in the Swiss canton of Valais. The valley is a destination for winter sport, with the slopes in Saas fee being one of the few places in the region where skiing in summer is possible.

items.subject: Kraków in Seven Days: Planty Ring, Kazimierz Nights, Nowa Huta Mornings
items.text: Most people give Kraków a weekend and see the Cloth Hall, a dragon and a queue. Seven days is the length at which the city stops performing. You get the hejnał at 07:00 with nobody watching, a whole grey morning in…

trip_data.title: Kraków in Seven Days: Planty Ring, Kazimierz Nights, Nowa Huta Mornings
trip_data.best_period: late April to mid-June, then the second half of September
trip_data.avoid: July-August (Rynek Główny gridlock, Wieliczka queues, Kazimierz stag noise) and the first fortnight of December
trip_data.difficulty: Easy
trip_data.gateway: Kraków-Balice (KRK), 11 km west. The Kraków Lotnisko-Kraków Główny train runs every 30 min, ~20 min, ~€4.65 (20 PLN, 2026 Koleje Małopolskie fare, luggage free). Rail from Warsaw Centralna 2h20 on EIP/IC; from Berlin via Warsaw or the direct night train.

itinerary.title: The Planty Ring and the First Hejnał
itinerary.morning: Arrive, drop bags, and walk the Planty clockwise from Barbakan to Wawel, 4 km, about an hour, and the fastest way to internalise the city's shape. It replaced the walls after 1820; the surviving fragment at Brama Floriańska tells you how thick they were.
itinerary.afternoon: Rynek Główny, then the Sukiennice gallery of 19th-century Polish painting upstairs in the Cloth Hall. Stand under St Mary's on the hour for the hejnał, played to four windows, cut off mid-phrase.
itinerary.evening: Miód Malina, ul. Grodzka 40, pierogi and duck; touristed and still good. Nightcap at Café Camelot, ul. św. Tomasza 17.
itinerary.dayStats: 5 km on foot

itinerary.title: Wawel and the Renaissance Courtyard
itinerary.morning: Be at the Wawel ticket office when it opens; take the State Rooms first, then the Crown Treasury & Armoury. Timed slots mean a 09:30 entry and a 12:00 entry can be two hours apart.
itinerary.afternoon: Wawel Cathedral on its separate ticket: the Sigismund Chapel from the nave, the Royal Tombs below, then the timber climb to the Sigismund Bell. Descend through ul. Kanonicza, the city's best-preserved street.
itinerary.evening: Starka, ul. Józefa 14 in Kazimierz, house-aged rye vodkas and Galician cooking. Reserve; the back room fills by 19:30.
itinerary.dayStats: 4 km

itinerary.title: Under the Square, and Kazimierz After Dark
itinerary.morning: Rynek Underground, four metres below the square, the medieval market level with cloth stalls, cart ruts and a lead-smelting hearth. Ninety minutes is right.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to Kazimierz. Szeroka's synagogue rectangle: the Old Synagogue (municipal museum), the Remuh with its 16th-century cemetery, then Izaak. Coffee and pistachio cake somewhere on ul. Józefa.
itinerary.evening: Hamsa, Szeroka 2, for hummus and mezze, the argument for Israeli food on this square is deliberate. Then a zapiekanka at the Okrąglak, the round former butchers' rotunda in the middle of Plac Nowy, roughly €4 (16-20 PLN) and open absurdly late.
itinerary.dayStats: 5 km

itinerary.title: Oświęcim
itinerary.morning: Train from Kraków Główny to Oświęcim, then the shuttle or a 2 km walk to the Auschwitz I gate. Your booked English-language guided tour covers Auschwitz I and the bus transfer to Birkenau; allow 3.5 hours minimum.
itinerary.afternoon: Birkenau's scale is the point, the ramp, the wooden barracks, the distance from the gate to the ruins of Crematoria II and III. Do not schedule anything after it.
itinerary.evening: Back in Kraków, eat quietly and early. Café Camelot or a bowl of żurek near your flat. No nightlife tonight; nobody wants it.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km each way, ~1h40 by train

itinerary.title: Podgórze, Zabłocie and the Ghetto Ground
itinerary.morning: Cross Kładka Bernatka to Plac Bohaterów Getta and its 70 empty bronze-and-steel chairs (Lewicki & Latak, 2005), one per thousand deported. Apteka pod Orłem, the pharmacy on the square that stayed open through the ghetto, is a small, exact museum.
itinerary.afternoon: East into Zabłocie: Schindler's Factory on ul. Lipowa, a Kraków-under-occupation museum more than a Schindler shrine, then MOCAK next door.
itinerary.evening: Bottiglieria 1881, ul. Bocheńska 5, tasting menu, Michelin-starred, book three to six weeks ahead; expect €90 to €130 (380-550 PLN) per head with pairing.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km

itinerary.title: Nowa Huta and the Socialist City
itinerary.morning: Tram 4 or 22 from Teatr Bagatela to Plac Centralny im. Ronalda Reagana, 25-35 minutes. Walk the arcades, then out along Aleja Róż, a parade axis turned quiet rose-bed, with a hole where Lenin stood until 1989.
itinerary.afternoon: The Nowa Huta Museum branch and the Nowa Huta Underground shelters, then the concrete ark of Arka Pana church in Bieńczyce, built 1967-77 after a decade of refused permits.
itinerary.evening: Back to Kazimierz for a slower night, wine on ul. Józefa, then Plac Nowy's bars, which are at their best on a Friday around 22:00.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km east by tram

itinerary.title: Wieliczka, Hala Targowa and the Mound
itinerary.morning: If it is a Sunday, start at Hala Targowa on ul. Grzegórzecka, the flea market runs early and thins out by 11:00; enamel signs, Cepelia textiles, and the grilled-sausage van under the viaduct.
itinerary.afternoon: Train from Kraków Główny to Wieliczka Rynek-Kopalnia (24 min) for the Tourist Route: about 800 steps down, 3 km of the mine's 245 km walked, two hours underground, ending at the Chapel of St Kinga carved entirely from salt. Guided groups only; the mine now prices the Tourist Route seasonally from 93 PLN (~€22) per person, with a normal Polish-language ticket running roughly 100-130 PLN (~€23 to €30) depending on the month.
itinerary.evening: Tram 1 to Salwator, up ul. Kościuszki past the Norbertine convent to Kopiec Kościuszki for the last light over the Vistula bend, then a final supper back in Stare Miasto.
itinerary.dayStats: 30 km round trip

items.subject: Sankt Peter-Ording, Germany
items.text: A 12 km North Sea beach so vast it hosts stilt-house restaurants, kite buggies and Germany's best kitesurfing

source.text: Sankt Peter-Ording is in Schleswig Holstein. Owing in part to its exposed position, it is one of Germany's prime destinations for surfing and kite-surfing but also popular with people who enjoy bathing or the unique climate of the North Sea, that is said to be a cure for many ailments, especially respiratory diseases.

items.subject: Vallée Heureuse - Château d'Ultrera
items.text: An 11 km loop with 665 m of climbing, about 4 h 55 min of walking. It tops out at 676 m. On the way: the peak Puig Nalt (561 m) and the castle Château d'Ultrera. Usually walkable all year.

facts.name: Vallée Heureuse - Château d'Ultrera

items.subject: Mount Olympus Refuges: Petrostrouga, the Muses Plateau and Mytikas
items.text: Olympus is far more mountain than its mythology suggests: a limestone massif rising from a beach to 2,918 m in 18 kilometres, with a summit that is a genuine scramble rather than a walk. This week climbs it the sensible way, up the forested Gortsia ridge to Petrostrouga, onto the Plateau of the Muses, over Mytikas and Skolio, and then a long descent through the Enipeas gorge to Litochoro and the sea. The refuges are cheap, sociable and Greek in character, meaning enormous dinners and no nonsense about check-in times. It suits fit hikers with scrambling experience; the summit ridge is the crux and not everyone should attempt it.

source.verified: Refuge altitudes, capacities and seasons, Spilios Agapitos (Refuge A) at 2,060 m with 110 places, open early May to end of October; Giosos Apostolidis at 2,697 m with 80 places, open early June to end of October and year-round by arrangement with the manager; Petrostrouga at 1,920 m with 72 places, operating throughout the year; Christos Kakalos at 2,648 m with 17 places, open late May to early November plus a March-April winter window. All three main refuges require booking before arrival and none is served by a central portal.

trip_data.title: Mount Olympus Refuges: Petrostrouga, the Muses Plateau and Mytikas
trip_data.best_period: Mid-June-early October, with mid-September the best mix of stable rock and empty refuges
trip_data.avoid: November-May, Mytikas becomes a winter mountaineering route, refuges close and the Kaki Skala ices
trip_data.budget: €650 to €1,050 per person, excl. international flights
trip_data.difficulty: 4/5, spiking to 5/5 on the Mytikas day, an exposed Grade II/III scramble on loose rock at 2,900 m
trip_data.gateway: SKG Thessaloniki Makedonia, 1 h 10 min to Litochoro; ATH Athens 4 h 30 min by car or 4 h by train to Litochoro station

itinerary.title: Litochoro, the lower Enipeas and the sea
itinerary.morning: Arrive from Thessaloniki to Litochoro, 300 m, a stone town wedged at the gorge mouth with the massif filling the whole western sky. Register your route at the Olympus National Park information office and confirm the refuge bookings by phone.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the lower Enipeas gorge from the town's Mylos to the Agios Dionysios monastery ruins and back, wooden footbridges, river crossings, plane trees, and a cold pool at the Enipeas springs.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Gastrodromio En Olympo on the main square, the best kitchen in Pieria, wild greens, Olympus mushrooms, goat, and a Rapsani red from the mountain's own vineyards.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km round trip / 350 m ascent / Litochoro 300 m / 3 h 30 min realistic / national park registration completed

itinerary.title: Gortsia to the Petrostrouga refuge
itinerary.morning: Taxi 40 minutes to the Gortsia trailhead at 1,100 m (€25 to €40). Start the E4 through beech and black pine, past the Barba clearing, on a broad ridge that gains height steadily rather than steeply.
itinerary.afternoon: Reach Petrostrouga refuge, 1,920 m, sitting on a shoulder with the tree line just above and the whole Thermaic Gulf below. Afternoon here is deliberate acclimatisation, you have gained 800 m and will gain 800 more tomorrow.
itinerary.evening: Refuge dinner, bean soup, pasta, plenty of it, and an early night. The refuge is the friendliest on the mountain and often has climbers coming down off Stefani.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km / 820 m ascent / Gortsia 1,100 m / Petrostrouga 1,920 m / 3 h 30 min-4 h realistic / bed €18 to €22 cash

itinerary.title: Skourta and the Plateau of the Muses
itinerary.morning: Above Petrostrouga the forest ends within an hour. Climb the Skourta ridge to 2,475 m, then traverse the exposed Lemos ridge with the Stefani north face, the Throne of Zeus, the most dramatic thing on the mountain, appearing across the Kazania cirque.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross onto the Plateau of the Muses at about 2,650 m and check into Giosos Apostolidis, 2,697 m, the highest refuge in Greece, with Christos Kakalos a few hundred metres away.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from the plateau over the Kazania. Nights up here drop to 3-6 °C in August; the refuge has blankets but the dorm is not heated. Buy water now, there is none on the plateau.
itinerary.dayStats: 7 km / 900 m ascent / 150 m descent / Skourta 2,475 m / refuge 2,697 m / 4-5 h realistic / no water source above the tree line

itinerary.title: Mytikas, 2,918 m, and down to Refuge A
itinerary.morning: Leave at 06:00 with helmets on. Traverse the Zonaria below Stefani to Skala, 2,866 m, then the Kaki Skala, 30-45 minutes of exposed Grade II/III scrambling on loose limestone to the summit of Mytikas, 2,918 m and its metal box of a summit register. The direct Louki couloir from the plateau is shorter and considerably more dangerous.
itinerary.afternoon: Reverse to Skala, add the easy 20-minute ridge to Skolio, 2,911 m for the view down the 500 m Kazania wall, then take the long zigzagging descent to Spilios Agapitos (Refuge A), 2,060 m, in its stand of Bosnian pine.
itinerary.evening: Refuge A is the busiest and best-run hut on the mountain: dinner at 18:00, lights out at 22:00, and a warden's briefing on tomorrow's weather. Ouzo on the terrace as the Thermaic Gulf turns pink.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km / 450 m ascent / 1,100 m descent / summit 2,918 m / Kaki Skala 30-45 min each way at Grade II/III / 7-8 h realistic

itinerary.title: Prionia and the full Enipeas gorge
itinerary.morning: Descend the classic mule path through beech and Bosnian pine to Prionia, 1,100 m, where a taverna sells bean soup, grilled sausage and the coldest spring water on the mountain.
itinerary.afternoon: Instead of taking the road, walk the full Enipeas gorge, 12 km and roughly 800 m of descent past the monastery of Agios Dionysios, the cave chapel, and a dozen plank bridges and cable-assisted river crossings, all the way back down to Litochoro at 300 m. It is the finest gorge walk in northern Greece and almost nobody does it in this direction.
itinerary.evening: Swim at Plaka Litochorou, five minutes from town, then dinner at To Pazari for grilled octopus and tsipouro.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km / 150 m ascent / 1,760 m descent / Prionia 1,100 m / gorge 12 km / 7-8 h realistic, the longest day of the week

itinerary.title: Dion, Platamonas and Palaios Panteleimonas
itinerary.morning: Drive 15 minutes to the archaeological park of Dion, the Macedonian sanctuary city at the mountain's foot where Alexander sacrificed before crossing into Asia, mosaics, a submerged sanctuary of Isis and an excellent museum (€8).
itinerary.afternoon: South to the Platamonas castle, a 13th-century Crusader fortress on a bluff above the sea, and up to the restored stone village of Palaios Panteleimonas at 500 m for the best view back at the whole Olympus escarpment.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Palaios Panteleimonas's plane-shaded square, grilled lamb, local wine, and the massif you walked over silhouetted opposite.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km driving / Dion €8 / Platamonas €3 to €4 / Palaios Panteleimonas 500 m / 3 km of village walking

itinerary.title: Rapsani, the Tembi gorge and out
itinerary.morning: Drive the mountain's south flank to Rapsani, the PDO wine village at 700 m, for a tasting of xinomavro-krassato-stavroto blends at Dougos or the Rapsani co-operative.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue through the Vale of Tembi, the gorge between Olympus and Ossa where the Pineios cuts to the sea, then north to Thessaloniki (1 h 10 min from Litochoro) or south to catch the Athens train from Litochoro station.
itinerary.evening: Thessaloniki's Ladadika or Modiano market for bougatsa, mezedes and the flight out.
itinerary.dayStats: Rapsani 700 m / Tembi gorge 10 km / Litochoro-SKG 1 h 10 min / Litochoro-Athens 4 h by train

items.subject: Two Rivers: The Váh Cycle Trunk and the Danube Dyke from Žilina to Štúrovo
items.text: Slovakia has one finished long-distance cycle route and one that is half-built, and this week rides both honestly. The Danube dyke below Bratislava is flat, smooth asphalt across Europe's largest river island, with a…

trip_data.title: Two Rivers: The Váh Cycle Trunk and the Danube Dyke from Žilina to Štúrovo
trip_data.best_period: the first three weeks of September, warm, dry, the Danube dyke empty of Austrian weekend traffic
trip_data.avoid: late July-August (35 °C on the shadeless dyke) and March-April, when the Danube floodplain paths can be under water
trip_data.difficulty: Easy-Moderate
trip_data.gateway: Fly Bratislava (BTS) or Vienna (VIE); ZSSK train Bratislava → Žilina, 2 h 20, bikes carried. Return from Štúrovo by train to Bratislava (~2 h 15) or cross the Mária Valéria bridge for Esztergom and Budapest.

itinerary.title: Through the Strečno gorge
itinerary.morning: From Žilina's Mariánske námestie, pick up the Váh downstream. The Strečno gorge comes at 12 km: the castle on its limestone crag above the river, and the route's worst infrastructure, short shared stretches on road I/18. Ride it early, before the truck traffic.
itinerary.afternoon: Past Vrútky, a spur into Martin for the Slovak National Museum's open-air Museum of the Slovak Village at Jahodnícke háje, then back onto the valley route through Považská Bystrica.
itinerary.evening: Reach Trenčín under its castle rock. Eat on Mierové námestie and look up: the castle is floodlit and vertical.

itinerary.title: The Roman inscription
itinerary.morning: Climb into Trenčín Castle first. Behind the Hotel Elizabeth, cut into the rock, is the Roman inscription of 179 AD recording the victory of Legio II Adiutrix at Laugaricio, the only Roman inscription north of the Danube limes, and viewable through a window in the hotel.
itinerary.afternoon: An easy 48 km on the finished cycleway south to Piešťany. This is the best-surfaced stretch of the whole Váh strand.
itinerary.evening: Cross the Kolonádový most, the 1933 covered colonnade bridge, to the spa island. Eat on the Winterova pedestrian street.

itinerary.title: Spa island to the Váh dams
itinerary.morning: A thermal soak or a walk round the spa island, the mud here has treated rheumatism since the 18th century.
itinerary.afternoon: South to Hlohovec on levee and quiet road, past the Empire château above the town. The Hlohovec-Sereď section is the second unfinished gap: signed, partly unsurfaced, and with two short stretches on a busy road.
itinerary.evening: Sereď is unremarkable and that is fine, it is a bed, a supper and 62 km done. The Holocaust museum in the former labour camp is worth an hour if it is open.

itinerary.title: Onto the Danube
itinerary.morning: West through the Trnava lowlands on quiet farm roads to Senec, then down into Bratislava. If the wind is against you, take the regional train from Sereď, it is a legitimate shortcut and costs a few euros.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the Bratislava riverfront under the Nový most and out to Devín, where the Morava joins the Danube under the castle ruin. Then back into the Old Town.
itinerary.evening: Change bikes if you are switching rental, and sleep in Bratislava. Tomorrow is the flat river.

itinerary.title: Žitný ostrov and the barrage
itinerary.morning: Leave on EuroVelo 6 along the left-bank dyke into the Žitný ostrov (Csallóköz), at roughly 1,600 km², Europe's largest river island, formed between the Danube and the Little Danube, flat, agricultural and Hungarian-speaking.
itinerary.afternoon: Smooth asphalt all the way to Šamorín and on to the Gabčíkovo barrage, the vast, contested hydroelectric works on the Danube, whose locks you can ride across and watch from above.
itinerary.evening: Stay in Gabčíkovo or Vojka nad Dunajom. Fish soup, and an early night.

itinerary.title: The dyke to the fortress town
itinerary.morning: Pure dyke riding: asphalt, no traffic, no gradient, the Danube on your right and the Hungarian bank beyond it. The Vojka-Kyselica ferry and the Šamorín-area crossings operate seasonally if you want the right bank.
itinerary.afternoon: Into Komárno, where the Váh finally meets the Danube. The Komárno fortress system is one of the largest surviving 19th-century bastion complexes in central Europe, the Old and New Fortress plus the Monostor works across the river.
itinerary.evening: Komárno is a bilingual Slovak-Hungarian town; eat halászlé or kapustnica depending on which side of the menu you read.

itinerary.title: To the basilica
itinerary.morning: Continue east on EuroVelo 6, still on the dyke, through Iža, where the Roman fort of Kelemantia, a bridgehead of the Danube limes, sits in a field, and Radvaň nad Dunajom.
itinerary.afternoon: Roll into Štúrovo, with Esztergom's basilica, the largest church in Hungary, filling the far bank. Cross the Mária Valéria bridge, destroyed in 1944 and not rebuilt until 2001; it is open to cyclists and pedestrians, there is no border check inside Schengen, and the crossing takes four minutes.
itinerary.evening: Climb to the basilica dome for the view back over Slovakia, then take the train from Štúrovo to Bratislava, or from Esztergom to Budapest, which is the better ending.

items.subject: West Cork Larder: Ballymaloe to Skibbereen
items.text: A seven-day culinary & wine tour itinerary in County Cork, East Cork, Kinsale and West Cork, Ireland.

trip_data.title: West Cork Larder: Ballymaloe to Skibbereen
trip_data.best_period: May to October. June for the first of the season's produce and long evenings; September-October for shellfish, apples and the West Cork food festivals
trip_data.budget: €1,790 to €3,330 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.

itinerary.title: Cork city and the English Market
itinerary.morning: Land at Cork. Straight to the English Market, a covered Victorian food market trading since 1788, with tripe and drisheen butchers, spiced beef, buttered eggs and On the Pig's Back's charcuterie counter.
itinerary.afternoon: Lunch upstairs at the Farmgate Café overlooking the market floor, the single best introduction to Cork food culture. Then the Butter Museum in Shandon, which sounds like a joke and is actually the history of Ireland's export economy.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Cork city. The city has developed real depth in recent years, including internationally recognised kitchens. `verify: true`

itinerary.title: East Cork: Ballymaloe and Midleton
itinerary.morning: Drive east to Shanagarry. Ballymaloe House is where modern Irish food began, Myrtle Allen opened the dining room in 1964 on the family farm and turned local, seasonal cooking into a national argument. Lunch here, or better, book a one-day course at the Ballymaloe Cookery School at Kinoith, with its organic farm and gardens.
itinerary.afternoon: Midleton and the Jameson distillery for the whiskey story, or the smaller producers around Ballycotton for fish landed that morning.
itinerary.evening: Ballymaloe's dinner is a set five-course menu built from the farm and the garden. Book far ahead.

itinerary.title: Kinsale
itinerary.morning: Kinsale, Ireland's self-declared gourmet capital since the 1970s, in a harbour of painted houses. Charles Fort on the headland gives you the walk before lunch.
itinerary.afternoon: The town's restaurant density is real, everything from a Michelin-recognised small room to fish shacks on the pier. Blacks of Kinsale brews and distils in the town.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Kinsale, then the harbour walk. This is the last "town" night before the west gets rural.

itinerary.title: Clonakilty, Timoleague and the pudding belt
itinerary.morning: Clonakilty black pudding has been made by the same family butchers since the 1880s and is the Irish benchmark. The town also has a Friday market and Deasy's out at Ring for lunch on the water.
itinerary.afternoon: Ummera Smokehouse at Timoleague, cold-smoked salmon, chicken and bacon over oak, in tiny batches, by arrangement. Then Inchydoney beach.
itinerary.evening: Stay in Clonakilty or move on to Skibbereen. Traditional music in Clonakilty's pubs is unforced and excellent.

itinerary.title: Skibbereen, Drimoleague and the cheese run
itinerary.morning: Skibbereen's Saturday market is one of the best food markets in Ireland, cheese, vegetables, bread, oysters, and the producers themselves behind the tables. Time your week to land here on a Saturday.
itinerary.afternoon: The farmhouse cheese circuit: Durrus on the Sheep's Head road, Gubbeen at Schull with Fingal Ferguson's smokehouse and salami operation next to Giana's cheese room, and Glenilen Farm at Drimoleague for butter and cream. Visits are by arrangement and worth every email.
itinerary.evening: West Cork Distillers in Skibbereen, then dinner in town.

itinerary.title: Schull, Baltimore and the sea
itinerary.morning: Schull's Sunday market and the harbour. Sally Barnes's Woodcock Smokery near Castletownshend smokes only wild fish, over beech, with salt, one of the most uncompromising food producers in Europe.
itinerary.afternoon: Baltimore, and the ferry to Sherkin Island or Cape Clear, Cape Clear has a goat farm making ice cream and a bird observatory, and the crossing is 45 minutes of Atlantic.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Baltimore, where the standard is startlingly high for a village of a few hundred people. `verify: true`

itinerary.title: Bantry, the Beara edge and out
itinerary.morning: Bantry's Friday market if the day fits; otherwise the drive around Bantry Bay with Whiddy Island offshore, and Milleens cheese country on the Beara peninsula, where Veronica Steele made the cheese in 1976 that started Irish farmhouse cheesemaking.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive back to Cork Airport (about 2 h from Bantry). Buy vacuum-packed cheese and smoked fish at the last market you pass; almost all of it travels well.

items.subject: Kopaonik: Pančićev Vrh, the Karaman Ridge and a Week on Serbia's Roof
items.text: Kopaonik is the mountain Serbia built its winter around, and it is odd and likeable in ways the brochures do not capture: a broad, rounded massif rising to Pančićev vrh at 2,017 m, treeless on top, sun-drenched to a degree that has given it the nickname Sunčana planina, and equipped with an unusually good modern lift fleet including heated six-seaters and, since the Brzeće gondola opened, a genuine 1,000-metre vertical descent. The week is built as an inside-out exploration, two days learning the Suvo Rudište core around Karaman Greben, Malo Jezero and Krst, then out to the flanks at Gobelja and Duboka, then the full ride down the gondola to Brzeće and back, with the summit of Pančićev vrh saved for a clear morning. Kopaonik sits inside a national park, so the terrain is protected forest and open alpine meadow rather than a building site, and the après scene at Konaci is loud, cheap and entirely unlike anything in the Alps. It suits intermediates who want a lot of well-groomed red mileage, families who want night skiing and short lift lines mid-week, and travellers who like the idea of finishing the week in a 78°C thermal spring and a twelfth-century UNESCO monastery.

source.verified: The Skijališta Srbije published Kopaonik ski-pass tariff in RSD (day adult 5,600 / child 3,900 / senior 5,000; 6-day 24,900 / 16,400 / 20,900; 7-day 27,900 / 18,000 / 22,400), the 500 RSD ChipCard deposit, night-track ticket pricing in the 1,950-2,400 RSD region, the "day + night" category including a minimum of one floodlit run, and the published 30% discount on single, half-day, daily and two- to four-day tickets during ski-track and season openings. The three published season bands (Low 15 Nov-16 Dec and from 24 Mar; Mid 17-24 Dec, 8 Jan-10 Feb, 18-23 Mar; High 25 Dec-7 Jan, 11-17 Feb). Kopaonik's resort profile: 1,060-2,017 m with 957 m vertical, roughly 55 km of piste at 30 km easy / 19 km intermediate / 6 km difficult, 26 lifts including heated four- and six-seaters, an early-December to early-April operating season, and the resort's position inside Kopaonik National Park. The existence and operation of the Brzeće-Mali Karaman gondola.

trip_data.title: Kopaonik: Pančićev Vrh, the Karaman Ridge and a Week on Serbia's Roof
trip_data.best_period: Late January-early March; the second half of February combines the deepest base with the famous Kopaonik sun
trip_data.avoid: 25 December-7 January, when high-season pricing bites and every Belgrade family is on Malo Jezero, and after 20 March when the sun that makes this mountain pleasant destroys it by noon
trip_data.budget: €950 to €1,700 per person, excl. international flights
trip_data.difficulty: 3/5, six lift-served days on a mountain with 950 m of vertical and long, sustained reds; nothing technical, but altitude, cold and a 200 km transfer make day one hard
trip_data.gateway: BEG Belgrade Nikola Tesla, 285 km / 4 h 30-6 h by road; INI Niš Constantine the Great, 200 km / 3 h 30-4 h 30 and usually the smarter arrival

itinerary.title: Fly to Niš or Belgrade, drive south, arrive on the mountain
itinerary.morning: Land at INI Niš if you can, it is 200 km and 3 h 30-4 h 30 away against Belgrade's 285 km and up to six hours in winter traffic. Collect a hire car or a pre-booked transfer; the last 30 km up from Raška or Brzeće is a serious mountain road and needs winter tyres.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive at Suvo Rudište, roughly 1,770 m, and settle. Buy the six-day pass and pay the 500 RSD ChipCard deposit; collect rental gear at Konaci. If there is light left, ride one lap of Malo Jezero just to open the legs at altitude.
itinerary.evening: Eat at your hotel, the half-board convention here is strong, or walk to Konaci for the après strip, which starts loud at about 16:30 and does not pretend to be sophisticated.
itinerary.dayStats: Niš-Kopaonik 200 km / 3 h 30-4 h 30 / base altitude 1,770 m / ChipCard 500 RSD / 6-day adult pass 24,900 RSD (≈ €213)

itinerary.title: Karaman Greben end to end
itinerary.morning: Ride the Karaman Greben chair and ski the ridge run top to bottom. This is Kopaonik's signature descent, a long, sustained, beautifully graded red along the crest with the whole Raška valley on your left. Lap it three times before the mountain fills.
itinerary.afternoon: Work down through Mali Karaman and Veliki Karaman, then across to Krst on the northern side, which is steeper and quieter. Lunch at the Marine Vode mountain restaurant on the sunny flank.
itinerary.evening: Night skiing on Malo Jezero. The floodlit run is short but the refrozen surface is fast, the ticket is roughly 1,950-2,400 RSD, and at −10°C under lights it is the most memorable hour of the week. Dinner afterwards at Restoran Kraljevi Čardaci.
itinerary.dayStats: Kopaonik 1,060-2,017 m / 55 km over 25 runs, 26 lifts / Karaman Greben the resort's signature red / night ticket ≈ 1,950-2,400 RSD (€17 to €21) / lifts 09:00-16:00

itinerary.title: Gobelja and Duboka: the cold flanks
itinerary.morning: Traverse northwest to Gobelja, the shoulder that holds the coldest, driest snow on the massif and sees a fraction of the traffic. On a hard-frozen morning it is worth the transit twice over; on a warm one it is the only place still skiing well after 11:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop into the Duboka chain, Duboka 1, 2 and 3, a wooded valley on the north side and the closest thing Kopaonik has to tree skiing. Watch the clock: the bottom of Duboka 3 is where people get stranded, so turn round by 15:00.
itinerary.evening: Back at Konaci, eat at Restoran Angella, then take the après strip seriously for one night, Serbian ski nightlife is a genuine cultural artefact and it runs on rakija, turbofolk and volume.
itinerary.dayStats: Gobelja north-facing, coldest snow on the mountain / Duboka chain three lifts / hard turnaround 15:00 at Duboka 3, 15:15 at Gobelja / rakija ≈ 250-400 RSD

itinerary.title: The gondola day: the full 1,000 m to Brzeće
itinerary.morning: Ski to Mali Karaman and take the Brzeće gondola down, roughly 4.4 km of cable and about 700 m of drop to the village at 1,050 m. Ride it once to see the line, then ski it: the descent from Mali Karaman to Brzeće is the longest continuous run in Serbia and the reason the gondola was built.
itinerary.afternoon: Do it twice more, then have lunch in Brzeće itself, which is 40% cheaper than the mountain top and where the local kitchens are better. Ride back up on the gondola, or take the Brzeće ski bus if the queue has grown.
itinerary.evening: Return to Suvo Rudište and eat at the Konaci complex, or stay down in Brzeće for a village dinner, grilled meat, kajmak and a Rubin red, and come up on the last cabin.
itinerary.dayStats: Brzeće gondola ≈ 4.4 km, 8-seat cabins, Brzeće 1,050 m to Mali Karaman ≈ 1,760 m / continuous descent ≈ 950-1,000 m vertical / three laps ≈ 3,000 m descent / ski bus 300-500 RSD

itinerary.title: Weather-contingency and rest day: Jošanička Banja and Studenica
itinerary.morning: This is the designed flex day; take it early if the mountain is in cloud or a košava-driven wind has stopped the upper chairs, otherwise take it here when legs are worst. Drive 25 km down the western side to Jošanička Banja and get into the hottest thermal water in Serbia, the source runs at around 78°C and the bathhouses are plain, cheap and excellent.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue 40 km north to Studenica Monastery, founded in the 1190s by Stefan Nemanja, a UNESCO World Heritage site whose marble Church of the Virgin holds the best Byzantine frescoes in the country. In winter it is close to empty and genuinely silent.
itinerary.evening: Eat in Raška on the way back for a fraction of mountain prices, then drive up in the dark with care, the last 25 km is unlit switchback.
itinerary.dayStats: Jošanička Banja 25 km, spring ≈ 78°C / Studenica ≈ 60-70 km from the resort / total driving 130-160 km round trip / zero vertical metres skied

itinerary.title: Pančićev vrh, the summit and the sunny side
itinerary.morning: Take the summit lift to Pančićev vrh, 2,017 m, the highest point in central Serbia, and walk the last few metres to the mausoleum of Josif Pančić, the botanist who catalogued this mountain. On a clear morning you can see into Kosovo and across to the Golija massif; the snow on the flanks up here is the best on the mountain.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the sunny Marine Vode and Sunčana Dolina side in the early afternoon while it is still soft rather than slushy, then finish with two more laps of Karaman Greben as the light goes flat and gold.
itinerary.evening: Last night: dinner at Restoran Milmari, then a walk out onto the snow above the hotels, Kopaonik's summit plateau under a clear February sky is worth ten minutes of cold.
itinerary.dayStats: Pančićev vrh 2,017 m / summit-to-Brzeće potential vertical ≈ 950 m / roughly 25-30 piste km on the day / national park: stay on marked ground

itinerary.title: A last morning, then the long road out
itinerary.morning: Ski Malo Jezero and Karaman until 11:00 on the last day of the six-day pass, then return rental gear and reclaim the 500 RSD ChipCard deposit. Sunday mornings are the quietest three hours of the week here.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive out. Allow 4 h 30-6 h to Belgrade and 3 h 30-4 h 30 to Niš, and add an hour in snow, the descent to Raška and the road through Brus are both slow when it is falling.
itinerary.evening: If your flight is early, sleep in Belgrade or Niš rather than trusting the mountain road at dawn. In Belgrade, eat in Skadarlija before you go.
itinerary.dayStats: Half-day skiing ≈ 1,500-2,500 m descent / ChipCard refund 500 RSD / Kopaonik-BEG 285 km / Kopaonik-INI 200 km / add 1 h in snow
