items.subject: Pristina & Prizren: Kosovo's Two Cities in Seven Days
items.text: Kosovo gives you two entirely different cities four days apart on the same €5 bus. Pristina is young, loud and architecturally strange, Yugoslav brutalism, a spiky National Library, an unfinished Orthodox cathedral, and the Newborn monument that gets repainted each February. Prizren is Ottoman: a river through the middle, a hillside fortress, a 17th-century mosque on the square, and a Serbian Orthodox cathedral rebuilt after 2004. Between and around them are the Gračanica and Visoki Dečani monasteries, still under protection, and the Rugova gorge. It is the cheapest week in this collection, and the least infrastructure-heavy: expect minibuses, cash, and conversations.

source.verified: Kosovo's use of the euro confirmed; Visoki Dečani's access regime confirmed, it remains the only site in Kosovo still guarded by KFOR, with a traffic barrier and watchtower, bag surrender and passport registration required to enter. Gračanica access confirmed as the Gjilan-bound bus from Pristina station, 20 minutes, €1 fare, departing every 30 minutes. Pristina-Peja bus confirmed at €5 and 1h30 with departures roughly every 20 minutes. Rugova gorge access from Peja confirmed as taxi or on foot, with hiking, water sports and ziplining available.

trip_data.title: Pristina & Prizren: Kosovo's Two Cities in Seven Days
trip_data.best_period: Mid-May-late June & September-mid October
trip_data.avoid: December-February (Pristina's winter inversion traps lignite smog and air quality collapses); August is hot and dusty with monasteries at their busiest.
trip_data.budget: €600 to €950 per person, excl. international flights
trip_data.difficulty: 2-6-9 km a day in the cities, plus one 8-12 km hiking option in Rugova with 350-500 m of ascent.
trip_data.gateway: PRN, Pristina International "Adem Jashari"; airport shuttle or taxi to central Pristina 20 min (€15-20 fixed); no train link

itinerary.title: Pristina: the boulevard and the library
itinerary.morning: Taxi in from PRN, drop bags, then walk Bulevardi Nënë Tereza from Skanderbeg's statue north. Macchiato at Dit' e Nat', Fazli Grajçevci 5, a bookshop-café that functions as the city's living room.
itinerary.afternoon: National Library of Kosovo (free, enter and look up at the domes from inside, it is the whole argument), the unfinished Christ the Saviour cathedral beside it, and the University campus. Then Newborn on Bill Clinton Boulevard, repainted every 17 February, and the Heroinat memorial of 20,000 pins.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Liburnia, Rr. Perandori Justinian 9, Kosovar home cooking done seriously, €12-20pp. Then rakia at Soma Book Station.
itinerary.dayStats: 6.4 km, flat; taxi PRN €15-20; library open Mon-Fri 08:00-20:00; mains €5-8.

itinerary.title: Ottoman Pristina, Gračanica monastery
itinerary.morning: The old quarter, Xhamia e Madhe (Great Mosque, 1461), the Great Hammam, the Clock Tower, and the Ethnological Museum Emin Gjiku (€2), an 18th-19th-century Ottoman family compound with the oda reception room intact and excellent guides.
itinerary.afternoon: Gjilan-bound bus from the main station to Gračanica, 20 minutes, €1. The 1321 monastery church, five domes stacked in a pyramid, holds some of the finest surviving Serbian medieval frescoes. Cover shoulders and knees; no photography inside.
itinerary.evening: Back in Pristina, Te Zoti or Renaissance 2 (Rr. Sylejman Vokshi, no menu, no prices, a set procession of dishes and wine, ~€20pp, ring the bell).
itinerary.dayStats: 5.8 km; bus €1 each way, 20 min; Emin Gjiku 10:00-17:00, closed Mondays; Gračanica daylight hours, closed midday.

itinerary.title: Kosovo Museum, Grand Hotel context, bus to Prizren
itinerary.morning: Kosovo Museum, Rr. Ali Pashë Tepelena (€2), for the Neolithic Goddess on the Throne from Tjerrtorja, and the Kosovo Art Gallery nearby. Walk past the Grand Hotel Prishtina, worth ten minutes for the lobby and the story of a five-star state hotel that lost its stars one at a time.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus from Pristina station to Prizren, ~1h45, €5, departures every 20-30 min. Check into the old town and walk Shadervan square at golden hour.
itinerary.evening: Te Syla, off Shadervan, for qebapa and suxhuk; €8-14pp. Then the riverside terraces along the Lumbardhi.
itinerary.dayStats: 5.1 km; bus 1h45 / €5; Kosovo Museum 10:00-17:00, closed Mondays.

itinerary.title: Prizren: mosques, the League, and Kalaja
itinerary.morning: Sinan Pasha Mosque (1615) on Shadervan, the single-dome hall and painted mihrab, then the Gazi Mehmed Pasha Hammam and the Stone Bridge over the Lumbardhi.
itinerary.afternoon: League of Prizren complex (€1), the reconstructed 1878 house where the Albanian national movement was founded; then the Church of Our Lady of Ljeviš (14th century, UNESCO, burnt in 2004, restored, access by arrangement) and the Catholic Cathedral of Our Lady of Perpetual Succour.
itinerary.evening: Climb to Kalaja fortress (free, 30 min, 130 m) for sunset over the roofs and the Šar mountains behind. Dinner at Ambient, Rr. Sharri, €10-18pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 6.7 km incl. 130 m fortress climb; League complex 09:00-17:00; Kalaja open, unlit, carry a torch for the descent.

itinerary.title: Visoki Dečani and Gjakova
itinerary.morning: Pre-arranged visit to Visoki Dečani Monastery near Deçan, driver from Prizren (~€40-60 return, 1h) or bus to Deçan then taxi. At the gate you pass a KFOR checkpoint, surrender bags and register with passports; the 1327-35 church holds around a thousand frescoes and the largest surviving medieval Byzantine-rite fresco programme anywhere.
itinerary.afternoon: On to Gjakova for the reconstructed Çarshia e Madhe bazaar, the longest in Kosovo, and the Hadum Mosque.
itinerary.evening: Back to Prizren. Marashi on the riverbank for trout, €12-18pp.
itinerary.dayStats: ~120 km driven; Dečani open roughly 09:00-13:00 and 15:00-17:00; passport mandatory; no photography inside the church.

itinerary.title: Rugova Gorge and Peja
itinerary.morning: Bus or driver Prizren → Peja (1h15-1h30). The Patriarchate of Peć (small entry fee, passport required, KFOR-adjacent) at the gorge mouth, four churches under one roof, 13th-14th century.
itinerary.afternoon: Into the Rugova Gorge: the Via Ferrata Ari, the zipline, or the walk toward the Drelaj villages. A hired car or driver is the only practical way; €25-40 for the half day.
itinerary.evening: Peja's bazaar and a beer at the Birra Peja brewery town it is named for, or return to Pristina by the 18:00-19:00 bus (€5, 1h30).
itinerary.dayStats: 8-12 km hiking option, 350-500 m ascent; Peja bus €5 / 1h30; driver into Rugova €25-40.

itinerary.title: Pristina coffee, Bear Sanctuary, departure
itinerary.morning: If time allows, the Bear Sanctuary Prishtina at Mramor (€2-3, 20 min by taxi), where bears rescued from restaurant cages live out their lives, a very Kosovar postscript. Otherwise, a last slow macchiato on Rr. Rexhep Luci.
itinerary.afternoon: Souvenir filigran silver from the old quarter workshops, then taxi to PRN.
itinerary.evening: Flight out.
itinerary.dayStats: 4.0 km; taxi PRN €15-20; allow 2 h at PRN for non-Schengen departure; macchiato €1-1.50.

items.subject: Umbrian Hill Towns: Spello, Bevagna & the Sagrantino Hills
items.text: A week built around two squares and the hills between them. You settle into Spello for three nights and Bevagna for four; Montefalco's Sagrantino cellars, Trevi's olive presses and Rasiglia's water channels happen as half-day loops that return you to a familiar doorway before dark. The rhythm is deliberately Umbrian, shutters down 13:30-16:00, then the whole town reappearing on the corso at 18:30. Two town moves in seven days, two written-in "do nothing" blocks.

source.verified: Infiorate di Spello 2026 confirmed as 6-7 June 2026 (Corpus Domini weekend; date moves annually with Easter, 29-30 May in 2027). Mercato delle Gaite 2026 confirmed as 18-28 June 2026, evening opening from 18:30 and 16:00 on public holidays. Continued operation of Antonelli San Marco, Scacciadiavoli and Frantoio Gaudenzi spot-checked.

trip_data.title: Umbrian Hill Towns: Spello, Bevagna & the Sagrantino Hills
trip_data.best_period: Late April-mid June & mid September-late October
trip_data.avoid: July-August (valley heat above 35°C, kitchens shut in late August) and January-February, when many hill-town restaurants close entirely
trip_data.budget: €1,150 to €1,800 per person, excl. international flights
trip_data.difficulty: 2, steep cobbled lanes and one 5.5 km valley walk; every town is crossable in under an hour
trip_data.gateway: PEG, Perugia San Francesco d'Assisi, 27 km / 30 min to Spello; FCO Rome is the fallback, 2 h 15 by car

itinerary.title: Landing softly in Spello
itinerary.morning: Land at Perugia, collect a small car (Panda-class suits these gates) and drive to Spello. Park in the lot below Porta Consolare rather than attempting the walled lanes. Check in; do nothing more ambitious than a coffee on Via Cavour.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the spine from Porta Consolare up to Porta dell'Arce. Stop in Santa Maria Maggiore for the Cappella Baglioni, Pinturicchio's 1501 cycle, majolica floor intact.
itinerary.evening: Aperitivo at Enoteca Properzio beside the church, then dinner at Il Molino on Piazza Matteotti, in the old olive-mill room: strangozzi al tartufo nero.
itinerary.dayStats: PEG-Spello 27 km / 30 min. Spine walk 1.6 km, 95 m ascent. Spello at 280 m, valley floor 220 m.

itinerary.title: Market morning, olive terraces
itinerary.morning: Tuesday market outside Porta Consolare, 08:00-13:00: Valnerina cheese, farro, chickpeas, whatever fruit is dictating the trattoria menus that week. Buy lunch rather than book it.
itinerary.afternoon: The Fonte Bulgarella loop out of Porta Montanara, CAI-marked track through terraced Moraiolo olives to the spring, back along the aqueduct line, with Assisi and Monte Subasio in view throughout.
itinerary.evening: Passeggiata peaks around 19:15 on Via Garibaldi. Dinner at La Bastiglia's terrace at the top of town; book two days ahead.
itinerary.dayStats: Loop 5.5 km / 210 m ascent / 2 h at a talking pace. Market 08:00-13:00. Monte Subasio above at 1,290 m.

itinerary.title: Trevi olive oil, then an afternoon of nothing
itinerary.morning: Drive to Trevi, spiralled on its hill above the Flaminia. The Museo della Civiltà dell'Ulivo in the San Francesco complex, then down to Bovara for the Ulivo di Sant'Emiliano, credibly over a thousand years old. Taste at Frantoio Gaudenzi in Pigge.
itinerary.afternoon: Deliberately blank. Back by 14:30, sleep, read, sit in the courtyard. The town is shuttered until 16:00 anyway, and that is the point.
itinerary.evening: Trattoria Il Pinturicchio on Via Sant'Angelo: torta al testo with sausage, grilled porcini, half last night's bill.
itinerary.dayStats: Spello-Trevi 13 km / 20 min. Trevi old town 412 m, Bovara 240 m; 2.5 km each way to the tree. Frantoio tastings €10 to €15.

itinerary.title: Move to Bevagna; Piazza Silvestri at dusk
itinerary.morning: Slow start, then the short drive down to the valley floor into Bevagna, the only genuinely flat town of the week, and the easiest to live in. Check in and leave the car parked for two full days.
itinerary.afternoon: The Botteghe delle Gaite circuit, medieval paper mill, silk workshop, candle-maker, dyer, then the 2nd-century Roman mosaic on Via Porta Guelfa: black-and-white sea creatures, ten minutes, unforgettable.
itinerary.evening: Sit in Piazza Silvestri from 18:15 and watch the town arrive. Dinner at Osteria Il Podestà, two doors off the square: pigeon, chickpea soup, a bottle of Montefalco Rosso.
itinerary.dayStats: Spello-Bevagna 13 km / 18 min. Botteghe ticket ~€8 to €10. Bevagna at 210 m. Passeggiata 18:15-20:00.

itinerary.title: Sagrantino day in Montefalco
itinerary.morning: Up to Montefalco, "the balcony of Umbria," for the circular Piazza del Comune and the Museo di San Francesco, where Benozzo Gozzoli's 1452 life of St Francis fills the apse.
itinerary.afternoon: Two cellars, no more. Antonelli San Marco for the organic, restrained house style and a vineyard walk; Scacciadiavoli at Cantinone for the 19th-century gravity-flow cellar and its Metodo Classico. Book both.
itinerary.evening: Back to Bevagna for Ristorante Redibis, built inside the curved wall of the Roman theatre, the room is the reason to go, but the food holds up.
itinerary.dayStats: Bevagna-Montefalco 7 km / 12 min; Montefalco 473 m vs Bevagna 210 m. Cellar visits €15 to €30, 75-90 min. Thursday market on Piazza del Comune.

itinerary.title: A hands-on hour, Rasiglia's water, Bettona's walls
itinerary.morning: Unstructured, with one option: the papermaking hour at the Cartiera. Pull your own sheet from the vat, press it, leave it drying while you have lunch. Otherwise the flat 8 km riverside there-and-back to Cantalupo.
itinerary.afternoon: Rasiglia, thirty houses threaded by the Menotre's channels, water running under and beside the lanes. Timed entry now applies on peak weekends; book ahead. Loop back via Bettona, Etruscan-walled, good Pinacoteca, almost no visitors.
itinerary.evening: Last night on Piazza Silvestri. Aperitivo outside, then Serpillo for a lighter, vegetable-forward dinner and a glass of Sagrantino Passito.
itinerary.dayStats: Bevagna-Rasiglia 25 km / 35 min via Foligno; Rasiglia at 648 m. Bettona 355 m, 15 km from Bevagna. Cantalupo walk 8 km, flat.

itinerary.title: Foligno, and out
itinerary.morning: With a late flight, drive to Foligno for the Saturday market and the Calamita Cosmica, Gino de Dominicis's 24-metre skeleton in the deconsecrated church of the Santissima Trinità in Annunziata. The strangest thing in Umbria and a perfect last stop.
itinerary.afternoon: Return the car at Perugia. Training out instead, Foligno station sits on the Rome-Ancona line.
itinerary.evening: Flight home, or an early dinner in Perugia with a night in hand.
itinerary.dayStats: Bevagna-Foligno 10 km / 15 min; Foligno-PEG 40 km / 45 min. Foligno-Roma Termini 1 h 50-2 h 10 by Regionale, roughly hourly.

items.subject: Baden Wine and the Black Forest Table
items.text: A week on Germany's warmest wine hills, from Kaiserstuhl cooperatives and Ortenau growers to the Black Forest kitchen and Freiburg's daily market.

trip_data.title: Baden Wine and the Black Forest Table
trip_data.gateway: EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg (EAP)

itinerary.title: Freiburg orientation
itinerary.morning: Land at EuroAirport and take the airport bus to Freiburg, about 45 minutes. Drop bags near the Altstadt.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Münsterplatz, where Freiburg's daily market runs Monday to Saturday, roughly 07:30-13:30, thickest on Wednesday and Saturday, the cathedral's red sandstone tower rises directly over the stalls. Note the Bächle, the shallow water channels threading the old town.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in the Altstadt: Bibeleskäs mit Bubespitzle, fresh herbed quark with hand-rolled potato noodles, a genuine Baden farmhouse dish, with a Freiburg Spätburgunder.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 0. Km travelled: 4 km on foot. Approx. tasting spend: €0.

itinerary.title: Into the Kaiserstuhl
itinerary.morning: Drive west into the Kaiserstuhl, about 25 minutes to Ihringen, the warmest point in Germany and the source of most of the region's Grauburgunder and Spätburgunder. Walk the terraced Winklerberg vineyard, cut into volcanic loess with dry-stone retaining walls.
itinerary.afternoon: Weingut Dr. Heger in Ihringen shows appointment-led tastings; email ahead. For a walk-in alternative, the Winzergenossenschaft Achkarren, one of Germany's oldest wine cooperatives, opened in 1929, pours a full flight with no booking needed.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at a Straußwirtschaft if the calendar allows, these seasonal taverns, licensed by Baden-Württemberg law for a few weeks a year, are the classic setting for Zwiebelkuchen mit Federweißer, onion tart with the cloudy, half-fermented new wine. Outside that window, order Flammkuchen (locally "Dünnele"), the thin-crust tart of cream, onion and bacon, instead.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 1-2. Km travelled: 45 km round trip. Approx. tasting spend: €20-30.

itinerary.title: Volcanic villages and the Franz Keller table
itinerary.morning: Drive on to Oberrotweil and Oberbergen, the Kaiserstuhl's highest villages, for a walk along the Vulkanpfad, the marked path explaining the extinct volcano's geology among the vines.
itinerary.afternoon: Weingut Salwey in Oberrotweil pours by appointment; the Winzergenossenschaft Oberbergen/Bickensohl area cooperatives are walk-in.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Schwarzer Adler in Oberbergen, the Keller family's long-established restaurant-with-rooms, built directly into its own vineyard and known for Baden classics done precisely, Schäufele, roasted pork shoulder blade with a dark gravy and Kartoffelsalat, is the dish to order.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 2. Km travelled: 55 km round trip. Approx. tasting spend: €25-35.

itinerary.title: Freiburg market day and the Umweltzone
itinerary.morning: A full morning at the Münsterplatz market: farm cheese, Schwarzwälder Schinken (Black Forest ham, smoked over fir and spruce), stone fruit in season, and bread from the surrounding villages.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Altstadt properly, the university quarter, the Augustinerplatz, the Schwabentor gate. If driving into the city, remember Freiburg's Umweltzone: only cars with a green environmental sticker (Feinstaubplakette) may enter the centre, checked at the ring boundary.
itinerary.evening: Slice of Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte, Black Forest cherry cake, made properly with Schwarzwälder Kirschwasser, the region's protected cherry brandy, at a Konditorei in the old town.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 0. Km travelled: 5 km. Approx. tasting spend: €15-20.

itinerary.title: Ortenau and Durbach
itinerary.morning: Drive north to Durbach, about an hour, where Riesling is grown under its old local name, Klingelberger, on granite rather than the Kaiserstuhl's loess.
itinerary.afternoon: The Durbacher Winzergenossenschaft is walk-in and pours the full Klingelberger range. For a private grower, the historic Schloss Staufenberg estate above the village keeps a public Vinothek with terrace views over the Rhine plain.
itinerary.evening: Return to Freiburg. A lighter dinner: Flädlesuppe, pancake-strip broth, ahead of a Winzergenossenschaft Spätburgunder.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 2. Km travelled: 110 km round trip. Approx. tasting spend: €20-25.

itinerary.title: Up into the Black Forest kitchen
itinerary.morning: Drive up into the hills above Freiburg, the Schauinsland or the villages around Kandel, for the Black Forest side of the trip: working smokehouses and farm kitchens that supply the ham and Kirschwasser tasted on Day 4.
itinerary.afternoon: A farmhouse Vesper plate (cured meats, farm bread, mountain cheese) at a Schwarzwaldhof; several of the working farms sell direct and will explain the smoking process, which takes weeks over cold fir smoke.
itinerary.evening: Back down to Freiburg. A last Kaiserstuhl bottle with dinner in the Altstadt.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 0. Km travelled: 60 km round trip. Approx. tasting spend: €15-20.

itinerary.title: Königschaffhausen and departure
itinerary.morning: A final Kaiserstuhl stop at Königschaffhausen, whose cooperative cellar is known for a particularly structured Spätburgunder from the Steingrüble vineyard. Walk-in tasting, no appointment.
itinerary.afternoon: Last errands at the Münsterplatz market if it is a market day, then the airport bus back to EuroAirport.
itinerary.evening: Departure.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 1. Km travelled: 50 km round trip plus airport transfer. Approx. tasting spend: €10-15.

items.subject: The Sherry Triangle: Solera, Tabanco & the Bajo de Guía
items.text: Three towns, twenty kilometres apart, producing wines that cannot legally be made in each other's cellars. You spend the week learning why: albariza chalk, the flor yeast veil, the fractional blending of the solera, and the sea humidity that makes Sanlúcar's manzanilla thinner and saltier than Jerez's fino from identical grapes. Between visits it is a tapas trip, tabancos where a copa costs €1.60, Cádiz's Mercado Central, langostinos at the Guadalquivir mouth, retinto beef from the Vejer marshes. Cheap for what it is, and the most technically interesting wine week in Spain.

source.verified: González Byass / Tío Pepe's own experiences page listing the Tío Pepe Experience at €25.50, Colors of Sherry at €28.50, Between Tapas at €30.50, Between Wines and Tapas at €33.50 and Premium VORS at €50, Tuesday-Sunday with advance reservation and telephone booking on +34 956 357 016; Barbadillo's public visits page for Sanlúcar; the existence and separate legal status of DO Manzanilla-Sanlúcar de Barrameda.

trip_data.title: The Sherry Triangle: Solera, Tabanco & the Bajo de Guía
trip_data.best_period: Late February-early June & late September-early November
trip_data.avoid: July-August (38-42°C inland, bodegas hot and half-staffed) and Feria del Caballo week in May, when Jerez prices double
trip_data.budget: €1,450 to €2,300 per person, excl. international flights
trip_data.difficulty: 1/5, flat towns, one beach walk, sand at Bajo de Guía

itinerary.title: Jerez: albariza, flor, first copa
itinerary.morning: Arrive at XRY, drop bags, and walk Jerez's old town to the Alcázar and the Cathedral of San Salvador, which stands above the historic bodega quarter.
itinerary.afternoon: The orientation visit at González Byass (Tío Pepe), the Gustave Eiffel-attributed La Concha bodega, the venencia demonstration, and the Colors of Sherry flight covering fino through PX.
itinerary.evening: Tabanco crawl on Calle Santa María: El Pasaje for sherry from the butt and a 22:00 flamenco set, then Tabanco Plateros for chicharrones.
itinerary.dayStats: 1 bodega / González Byass tours €25.50 to €50 / tabanco copa €1.60 to €2.60, tapa €2.50 to €4 / 15 min airport transfer

itinerary.title: Old wines and the almacenista idea
itinerary.morning: Bodegas Tradición for VOS and VORS only, amontillado and palo cortado with 30-plus years of average age, plus the Zurbarán and Goya canvases upstairs.
itinerary.afternoon: Bodegas Lustau for the almacenista range, which bottles other people's soleras under their names, the clearest lesson in how the trade actually works.
itinerary.evening: Mantúa (Michelin-starred, Jerez) if you want the modern kitchen, or Albalá for a shorter, cheaper version of the same idea.
itinerary.dayStats: 2 bodegas / Tradición €40 to €60, Lustau €18 to €30 / VORS bottle band €55 to €120 / all walking, no car

itinerary.title: El Puerto de Santa María and the river bodegas
itinerary.morning: Train from Jerez to El Puerto (12 min). Visit Gutiérrez Colosía, whose butts sit metres from the Guadalete mouth, the humidity gives a visibly thicker flor than Jerez.
itinerary.afternoon: Bodegas Osborne and the Toro bull, then fried fish from a freiduría on Calle Misericordia, eaten in a paper cone with a copa from the bar next door, which is legal and expected.
itinerary.evening: Aponiente, Ángel León's three-star in a tidal mill on the salt marsh, if you booked months ago; otherwise Romerijo for a kilo of prawns.
itinerary.dayStats: Train €4 return / 2 bodegas / Colosía €18 to €25 / freiduría cone €8 to €14 / Aponiente tasting menu €250+

itinerary.title: Sanlúcar: manzanilla and the Bajo de Guía
itinerary.morning: Transfer to Sanlúcar (35 min). Barbadillo in the Barrio Alto for Solear and the manzanilla pasada, then a walk down to the Barrio Bajo.
itinerary.afternoon: La Guita or Hidalgo-La Gitana for the second angle, then the Doñana view across the Guadalquivir from the Fábrica de Hielo.
itinerary.evening: Casa Bigote at Bajo de Guía: langostinos de Sanlúcar, acedías, and a cold half-bottle of manzanilla en rama that costs less than the starter.
itinerary.dayStats: 35 min transfer / 2 bodegas / fees €15 to €30 / langostinos €28 to €45 per ración / manzanilla bottle €7 to €14

itinerary.title: Cádiz market day
itinerary.morning: Drive or bus to Cádiz (45 min) and go straight to the Mercado Central de Abastos, the Rincón Gastronómico stalls sell erizos, tuna mojama and a plate of gambas you eat standing up.
itinerary.afternoon: The sea wall from La Caleta to the Castillo de San Sebastián, then the Torre Tavira camera obscura for the peninsula's rooftop geography.
itinerary.evening: Taberna Casa Manteca in La Viña for chicharrón especial de Cádiz on waxed paper, then El Faro de Cádiz for a proper sit-down.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 min each way / market plates €3 to €9 / Torre Tavira €8 / no bodega today, palate rest

itinerary.title: Vejer: retinto, vinegar and a kitchen
itinerary.morning: Drive inland to Vejer de la Frontera, a white hill town above the Barbate marshes, and take the cookery class at Annie B's Spanish Kitchen, tortillitas de camarones and a sherry reduction.
itinerary.afternoon: Retinto beef tasting at Venta El Toro or a visit to a sherry-vinegar solera at Bodegas Páez Morilla in Jerez on the way back, where the acetification bodega smells nothing like the wine one.
itinerary.evening: Restaurante Trafalgar on Vejer's Plaza de España, or back in Jerez at Tabanco San Pablo.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 min Sanlúcar-Vejer / class €75 to €110, 4 h / vinegar visit €12 to €20 / retinto steak €22 to €32

itinerary.title: Pagos, horses and out
itinerary.morning: A vineyard morning, not a cellar one: ask a bodega to run you into the Macharnudo or Balbaína pago to see albariza chalk, white and spongy, holding winter rain through a rainless summer.
itinerary.afternoon: The Real Escuela Andaluza del Arte Ecuestre in Jerez for the Thursday or Friday "Cómo bailan los caballos andaluces" show, then last bottles at La Casa del Jerez.
itinerary.evening: Early flight from XRY, 15 minutes away, or the 1 h 10 m train to Seville.
itinerary.dayStats: Vineyard visit €25 to €45 / equestrian show €22 to €30 / XRY 15 min / duty-free sherry travels badly in the hold, pack upright

items.subject: Monaco Sailing Week: Port Hercule to the Riviera
items.text: A Monaco-based sailing week through the Yacht Club de Monaco, coastal passages to Villefranche and Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat, and a crossing to Sanremo.

trip_data.title: Monaco Sailing Week: Port Hercule to the Riviera
trip_data.gateway: Nice Côte d'Azur (NCE)

itinerary.title: Port Hercule and the Yacht Club de Monaco
itinerary.morning: Arrive and walk Port Hercule, Monaco's main harbour, stern-to with superyachts along the Quai des États-Unis and racing dinghies tucked into the smaller basins.
itinerary.afternoon: Visit the Yacht Club de Monaco on the Quai Louis II, in its Norman Foster-designed home opened in 2014. The club runs sailing programmes across dinghies, offshore keelboats and its own Optimist and youth fleets, and can point toward its current partner schools for short-course sailing.
itinerary.evening: Dinner near the port, watching the evening arrivals from a day's racing or delivery passage.
itinerary.dayStats: 1 water hour (harbour orientation) · Calm inside the breakwater · no gear beyond a life jacket check.

itinerary.title: Sailing course inside the bay
itinerary.morning: A half-day keelboat or dinghy session within Monaco's bay and toward Cap Martin, working points of sail, tacking and reefing in the moderate conditions the sheltered bay usually offers before midday.
itinerary.afternoon: As the thermal breeze fills in from the south-east through early afternoon, extend the session to practice sailing in a proper 12-16 knots, the wind range this coast delivers most reliably in the settled season.
itinerary.evening: Easy night in Monaco; an early start tomorrow for the first real coastal passage.
itinerary.dayStats: 4 water hours · 8-16 knots, building SE thermal · keelboat or dinghy, life jacket, spray top.

itinerary.title: Passage to Villefranche-sur-Mer
itinerary.morning: Depart Port Hercule west past Cap d'Ail and Cap Ferrat's outer point for Villefranche-sur-Mer, roughly 12 nautical miles, one of the deepest natural harbours on the entire Mediterranean and historically a fleet anchorage for exactly that reason.
itinerary.afternoon: Anchor or pick up a mooring in the bay, sheltered on three sides by hills that block most of a mistral's force even when it is blowing hard further west along the coast. Row or dinghy ashore to walk the old town.
itinerary.evening: A mooring night in Villefranche if conditions and berth availability allow, otherwise a short motor back to Port Hercule.
itinerary.dayStats: 5 water hours · 10-15 knots SE, flattening inside the bay · keelboat, foul-weather layer for the passage.

itinerary.title: Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat and Beaulieu-sur-Mer
itinerary.morning: Sail the short leg around Cap Ferrat to Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat, threading past the point where the cape's own micro-thermal often accelerates the breeze noticeably.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue into Beaulieu-sur-Mer's harbour, another well-sheltered stop, then a shore break to see the Villa Kérylos before sailing back toward Monaco in the calmer late-afternoon air as the thermal starts to ease.
itinerary.evening: Return to Port Hercule for the night.
itinerary.dayStats: 4.5 water hours · 10-18 knots, gusty around the cape point · keelboat, harness for foredeck work.

itinerary.title: Crossing to Sanremo
itinerary.morning: The week's longest passage: east past Menton and across the French-Italian border toward Sanremo, roughly 25 nautical miles, best started early to use the calmer morning air before the thermal builds against the course.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive into Sanremo's Porto Vecchio in the early afternoon and moor for the night; this old fishing harbour on the Italian Riviera is a natural break point and a fair-weather crossing only.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Sanremo's old town, La Pigna, a very different register from Monaco's polish.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 water hours · 8-14 knots, wind against course by afternoon · keelboat, full offshore layer.

itinerary.title: Return passage and regatta context
itinerary.morning: Depart Sanremo early to beat the building thermal on the return leg toward Monaco, a passage best sailed on a settled forecast with the mistral and libeccio both absent.
itinerary.afternoon: Back in Port Hercule by mid-afternoon. If the calendar allows, this is the moment to see what the Yacht Club de Monaco has on the water: the club runs the Primo Cup-Trophée Credit Suisse each winter, one of the longest-established winter keelboat regattas on this coast, and Monaco Classic Week in alternating summers for classic yachts, alongside a full programme of youth and offshore racing through the year.
itinerary.evening: Rest evening in Monaco after the longer sailing days.
itinerary.dayStats: 5.5 water hours · 10-16 knots, morning favourable, afternoon on the nose · keelboat, full kit.

itinerary.title: Final sail and departure
itinerary.morning: A short final sail inside Monaco's bay, working on what the week has built, before returning gear to the club or charter operator.
itinerary.afternoon: Pack and take the coastal bus or train to Nice for the flight home.
itinerary.evening: Departure from Nice Côte d'Azur.
itinerary.dayStats: 2 water hours · Light thermal, 8-12 knots · dinghy or keelboat.

items.subject: The Rhine Alpine Triangle, Vaduz, the Silvretta and Graubünden
items.text: One base in Vaduz, six day loops into three countries, the Silvretta, the Bregenzerwald, the Ruinaulta gorge and the Graubünden passes.

trip_data.title: The Rhine Alpine Triangle, Vaduz, the Silvretta and Graubünden
trip_data.gateway: Zürich (ZRH)

itinerary.title: Zürich to the Fürstentum
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Zürich airport. A Swiss-registered rental almost always carries the Autobahnvignette already; check the windscreen or, for the e-vignette, that your plate is registered. Take the A3 along the Zürichsee and the Walensee, an hour of lake and limestone wall.
itinerary.afternoon: Leave the motorway at Sargans, cross the Rhine at Trübbach and enter Liechtenstein. No border post, no formalities, no Liechtenstein road charge, the country has no motorway to charge for. Settle in Vaduz, 455 m.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Städtle: the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein and Hilti Art Foundation share a black basalt cube, the Landesmuseum is opposite, and the castle sits on its rock above, closed to visitors but photogenic from the vineyard path. Park in the underground Städtle garage; surface bays are short-stay blue-zone.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km · 1h30 driving · no passes · max altitude 455 m.

itinerary.title: The one mountain road
itinerary.morning: Drive Liechtenstein's only alpine road: Vaduz to Triesenberg (884 m) on tight switchbacks with a 10% average, then through the Gnalp-Steg tunnel to Steg (1,300 m) and up to Malbun at 1,600 m. Fifteen kilometres, 1,150 m of climb, and a dead end, Malbun has no through route to anywhere.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the Sareis chairlift to 2,000 m for the ridge view into Austria, then drive down and south to Balzers, where Burg Gutenberg stands on a free-standing knoll above the Rhine.
itinerary.evening: Back in Vaduz, book a tasting at the Hofkellerei des Fürsten von Liechtenstein, the princely wine estate on the slope below the castle. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, and a short walk from the Städtle.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km · 1h30 driving · 1 climb (Malbun, dead end) · max altitude 1,600 m.

itinerary.title: Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse
itinerary.morning: North into Austria via Feldkirch. You need the Austrian digital Vignette for the A14 Rheintalautobahn and the S16, around €13 for ten days, bought from the ASFINAG app, valid immediately. Run the Walgau to Bludenz, then over the Arlbergpass, 1,793 m, on the free B197 rather than the tolled S16 tunnel, into Landeck.
itinerary.afternoon: South up the Paznaun through Ischgl to Galtür for the Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse: 34 hairpins, gradients to 12%. The lower Partenen ramp on the Vorarlberg side is shut for rockfall barrier works until summer 2030, so in 2026 the road is driven as a toll-free there-and-back from Galtür (open from 4 June) as far as the Vermuntsee. The Bielerhöhe at 2,032 m sits on the dam wall of the Silvretta-Stausee, with the Piz Buin behind it and a large car park that is the only easy parking on the whole road.
itinerary.evening: Retrace through Ischgl and Landeck, back over the Arlbergpass and down the Klostertal to Bludenz and home.
itinerary.dayStats: 230 km · 4h15 driving · 2 passes (Arlbergpass, Bielerhöhe) · max altitude 2,032 m.

itinerary.title: Furkajoch and the Bregenzerwald
itinerary.morning: Feldkirch, then Rankweil and up the Laternsertal to the Furkajoch, 1,761 m, a narrow, unfenced Vorarlberg pass, closed from November to May, with passing places rather than two full lanes. Not for wide vehicles. Over to Damüls, one of the highest villages in the region.
itinerary.afternoon: Down the Faschinajoch (1,486 m) or straight on to Au and the Bregenzerwald proper: Schwarzenberg, Bezau and Andelsbuch, where contemporary timber architecture sits next to 300-year-old farmhouses. The Werkraum Bregenzerwald in Andelsbuch shows what the local joiners actually make.
itinerary.evening: Over the Bödele (1,140 m) to Dornbirn, then Bregenz for the Bodensee at dusk. Back to Vaduz on the A14.
itinerary.dayStats: 210 km · 4h00 driving · 3 passes (Furkajoch, Faschinajoch, Bödele) · max altitude 1,761 m.

itinerary.title: Ruinaulta and the Viamala
itinerary.morning: South on the Swiss A13 to Chur, then up to Flims. Park at Flims Waldhaus and walk 40 minutes to Conn and the Il Spir viewing platform, a cantilevered timber spiral hanging over the Ruinaulta, the Rhine gorge cut through the debris of a prehistoric landslide.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive the gorge's southern rim through Ilanz and down the hairpins to Versam-Safien, then out at Bonaduz. Stop at Reichenau, where the Vorderrhein and Hinterrhein meet under a covered bridge and become the Rhine.
itinerary.evening: Continue to Thusis for the Viamala gorge, 359 steps down between walls 300 m high on the old road to Italy. Return north on the A13. If you have time and light, the San Bernardino pass at 2,065 m is another 40 minutes south and worth the detour.
itinerary.dayStats: 210 km · 3h40 driving · no passes on the core loop · max altitude 1,100 m.

itinerary.title: Prättigau, Wolfgangpass and Davos
itinerary.morning: A13 to Landquart and up the Prättigau through Schiers and Klosters, a long, steady valley climb with the Silvretta chain on the left.
itinerary.afternoon: Over the Wolfgangpass, 1,633 m, one of the few Graubünden passes open all year, past the Davosersee into Davos at 1,560 m, Europe's highest town of its size. Continue over the Flüelapass (2,383 m) only if it is open; it is a summer road, closed roughly November to May, and the Vereina car-train through the mountain is the winter alternative.
itinerary.evening: Loop back via Filisur and the Lenzerheide (1,549 m) to Chur, then the Rhine valley home. Detour to see the Landwasser viaduct near Filisur if the light holds.
itinerary.dayStats: 235 km · 4h10 driving · 2 passes (Wolfgangpass, Lenzerheide) · max altitude 1,633 m.

itinerary.title: Rhine valley and out
itinerary.morning: Cross to Werdenberg at Buchs, a lakeside cluster of medieval timber houses below a castle, then Bad Ragaz and the Taminaschlucht, the gorge where the thermal spring emerges. The last kilometre to the old baths is closed to private cars; a shuttle runs from the valley station.
itinerary.afternoon: North on the A3 along the Walensee to Zürich. Refuel in Liechtenstein or Austria before leaving; Swiss fuel is the most expensive of the three.
itinerary.evening: Drop the car at Zürich airport. Swiss returns want a full tank and heavy refuelling surcharges if not.
itinerary.dayStats: 145 km · 2h00 driving · no passes · max altitude 520 m.

items.subject: Julian Alps Passes: Vršič, Predel & Mangart
items.text: Slovenia packs three genuinely serious alpine roads into an area you can cross in ninety minutes, and this week drives all of them properly rather than ticking them off. Vršič is the headline, 1,611 m, fifty numbered hairpins, several of them still surfaced in the original 1915 Russian-laid cobbles, but Mangart is the one that stays with you, a 12 km toll road drilled through five unlit tunnels to the highest asphalt in the country. Between the passes you get the Soča itself, a river the colour of glacier milk running past Trenta, Bovec and Kobarid, and a Predel crossing into Italy that takes twenty minutes and feels like a different century. It suits drivers who enjoy technical roads for their own sake, and who are content to spend an entire afternoon covering 40 km.

source.verified: Vršič Pass altitude (1,611 m), ~50 hairpins, partly cobbled surface, and the 2026 traffic regime, control barriers from 15 June 2026 with no toll, free Kranjska Gora-Bovec shuttle 1 June-30 September, summit parking suspended until 31 August with a 117-space lot reopening 1 September; Mangart road 2026 €10 toll, five unlit tunnels, 12 km / 980 m ascent, mid-June to November season, and vehicles limited to the km 9 car park (90 spaces) after rockslide damage; Slovenian e-vinjeta 2026 prices (weekly €16, monthly €32, annual €117.50) and the €9 Karavanke tunnel charge.

trip_data.title: Julian Alps Passes: Vršič, Predel & Mangart
trip_data.best_period: Mid-June-early July & September-early October (all three passes reliably open)
trip_data.avoid: November-mid-May, Vršič is closed or chained-only, Mangart and Predel shut entirely; August brings Vršič shuttle-season congestion
trip_data.budget: €1,150 to €1,770 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.
trip_data.difficulty: 2, mostly driving, with a 1 h 30 Vintgar gorge boardwalk and a 40-minute walk to the Mangart Saddle
trip_data.gateway: LJU, Ljubljana Jože Pučnik; 62 km / 50 min to Kranjska Gora via A2 and Route 201

itinerary.title: Ljubljana to Kranjska Gora, and Zelenci at dusk
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at LJU. Buy the weekly e-vinjeta before you leave the airport forecourt, the A2 begins immediately and enforcement is camera-based. Run the A2 to Jesenice, then Route 201 up the Sava valley.
itinerary.afternoon: Settle in Kranjska Gora and walk or drive the 4 km to the Zelenci nature reserve, where the Sava Dolinka rises out of an emerald spring pool. There is a small paid car park at the trailhead.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Gostilna Pri Martinu in Kranjska Gora, a proper valley inn; order the ričet with smoked pork, or the beef goulash with buckwheat žganci.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km / 50 min; weekly e-vinjeta €16; A2 is fully vignette-covered; Zelenci parking €3.

itinerary.title: Vršič: fifty hairpins and the Russian Chapel
itinerary.morning: Leave by 08:00 to have the cobbles to yourself. The 24 northern hairpins are numbered on stone markers; bend 8 carries the Russian Chapel, built in 1916 by prisoners of war who died in an avalanche while constructing this road. Park in the layby just past it.
itinerary.afternoon: At the 1,611 m summit, walk ten minutes up toward the Poštarski dom for the Prisojnik "window" view. Then descend the 26 southern hairpins into Trenta, this is where cobbles alternate with new asphalt and the drop-offs are unguarded. Stop at the Trenta source of the Soča (Izvir Soče), a 20-minute scramble with fixed cables.
itinerary.evening: Down the Soča road (Route 206) to Bovec. Eat at Gostilna Sovdat for Soča trout, or Thirsty River Brewery for a post-drive beer.
itinerary.dayStats: 52 km / 4 h with stops; 50 hairpins; summit 1,611 m; max gradient 12%; no toll; ~1,100 m of descent into Trenta.

itinerary.title: Mangart, the highest asphalt in Slovenia
itinerary.morning: Drive Bovec to Log pod Mangartom, then onto the Mangartska cesta. Pay the €10 toll at the barrier. The five tunnels are unlit, unsigned and single-lane, headlights on, horn before entry, and give way to anything descending. Ascend in second gear.
itinerary.afternoon: Park at the km 9 lot (90 spaces; arrive before 10:00 in July-August or you will be turned back at the automatic barrier). Walk the 40 minutes to the Mangart Saddle at 2,055 m, with Jôf di Montasio and the Italian Julians filling the horizon. Descend using engine braking only; riding the brakes for 9 km will fade them.
itinerary.evening: Back in Bovec, walk to the Boka waterfall viewpoint layby on the road toward Žaga, Slovenia's highest falls, best in late afternoon when the west light hits the cliff face.
itinerary.dayStats: 46 km / 3 h 30; Mangart toll €10; 12 km climb, 980 m ascent; 5 unlit tunnels; saddle 2,055 m; road open mid-June to November.

itinerary.title: Predel into Italy, and back over the border
itinerary.morning: Take Route 203 up to the Predel Pass at 1,156 m, a short, well-surfaced climb past the ruined Predel fort and the Log pod Mangartom war cemetery. Cross into Italy at Cave del Predil.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop to Tarvisio on the SS54, then loop back via the SS13 and the Rateče border into Slovenia, a 90 km circuit that crosses two national borders without a single passport check. Stop at Lago del Predil for lunch on the water.
itinerary.evening: Return to Bovec via Vršič or the Soča road (choose the valley road if it has rained, the cobbles are slick). Dinner at Martinov Hram in Kobarid if you extend the loop south.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km / 2 h 45; Predel 1,156 m; Italian autostrade not used, so no Telepass needed; Slovenian vignette still required on return to A-roads.

itinerary.title: Kobarid, the Soča gorge and the Napoleon Bridge
itinerary.morning: The Kobarid Museum on the Isonzo Front is the best small war museum in the Alps, two hours, and it recontextualises every fortification you have driven past. Then walk the Kozjak waterfall loop from the Napoleon Bridge car park.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive the Route 102 south along the Soča toward Tolmin, stopping at the Tolmin gorges (Tolminska korita), the lowest point of Triglav National Park at 180 m, and a striking contrast to yesterday's 2,055 m.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Hiša Franko in Staro Selo, 3 km from Kobarid, Ana Roš's three-Michelin-star restaurant. Book months ahead, or eat superbly for a fifth of the price at Gostilna Breza in Kobarid.
itinerary.dayStats: 55 km / 1 h 20; Tolmin gorge entry €8; Kobarid Museum €8; Kozjak loop 3.5 km / 1 h.

itinerary.title: Over the Soriška planina to Bohinj
itinerary.morning: Take Route 403 from Podbrdo over the Soriška Planina saddle (1,277 m), a quiet, wide, beautifully graded road with about a dozen open bends and no traffic. It drops you into the Selška valley.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to Lake Bohinj via Bohinjska Bistrica. Drive the north shore road to Ukanc; the Savica waterfall car park is at the road's end. In peak summer Bohinj closes the Ukanc road to non-residents from mid-morning, arrive before 09:30 or use the Bohinj park-and-ride.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from the Church of St John the Baptist at the lake's eastern outlet, then dinner at Gostilna Rupa in Srednja vas for žlikrofi and Bohinj cheese.
itinerary.dayStats: 78 km / 1 h 50; Soriška Planina 1,277 m; Bohinj parking €10 to €15/day; Savica entry €4.

itinerary.title: Vintgar gorge and the run to Ljubljana
itinerary.morning: Drive to Zgornje Gorje for the Vintgar Gorge. Entry is timed-slot only and must be booked online; the 1.6 km boardwalk hangs over the Radovna river and ends at the Šum waterfall. First slot at 08:00 is the one worth having.
itinerary.afternoon: Bled for coffee at Slaščičarna Zima and a kremšnita, then the A2 south to Ljubljana. If you have time, stop at Radovljica's medieval core, the free car park sits just outside the walls.
itinerary.evening: Return the car at LJU with a full tank. Fuel at the Petrol station on the airport approach road.
itinerary.dayStats: 82 km / 1 h 30; Vintgar €20 adult, timed entry; Bled parking €3/h; A2 vignette-covered.

items.subject: Saimaa Lakeland: Linnansaari & Kolovesi Cabin Week
items.text: A seven-day nature escapes & cabin stay itinerary in Lake Saimaa, South Savo, Linnansaari and Kolovesi National Parks, Finland.

trip_data.title: Saimaa Lakeland: Linnansaari & Kolovesi Cabin Week
trip_data.best_period: Mid-June to early September for paddling and swimming; late August-September for mushrooms, berries and mist mornings; February-March for ice, snowshoeing and a frozen lake outside the sauna door
trip_data.budget: €1,100 to €2,130 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.

itinerary.title: Helsinki to the lake
itinerary.morning: Drive northeast from Helsinki, about 3 h 30, or take the train to Savonlinna. Stop for supplies at the last large supermarket, this is the trip's most important logistical act.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive at your first cabin near Oravi or Rantasalmi, between Linnansaari and Kolovesi. Unload, swim, learn the boat.
itinerary.evening: Heat the sauna. The Finnish sequence is sauna, lake, repeat, and then dinner at 21:00 in the long summer light.

itinerary.title: Linnansaari National Park by kayak
itinerary.morning: Rent kayaks or take the park boat from Oravi into Linnansaari, an archipelago national park of hundreds of rocky, pine-topped islands.
itinerary.afternoon: Paddle to Linnansaari island itself, where there is an old croft farm still worked traditionally, marked trails and a lookout over the labyrinth. This is prime Saimaa ringed seal habitat; sightings are a matter of luck and stillness.
itinerary.evening: Return to the cabin, or stay in a park hut. Seal rule: keep your distance, never approach a hauled-out seal, and observe the spring landing restrictions on nesting islets.

itinerary.title: Kolovesi: the paddling-only park
itinerary.morning: Kolovesi National Park bans motorboats, so the only way in is by paddle. The result is the quietest water in southern Finland: narrow sounds, 30 m cliffs, and prehistoric rock paintings in red ochre on the cliff faces at Ukonvuori and elsewhere.
itinerary.afternoon: Paddle the sounds, land at a designated site, and cook over a fire in a marked fireplace.
itinerary.evening: Camp at a wilderness site or return. This is the day the trip is built around.

itinerary.title: Cabin day: fishing, foraging, sauna
itinerary.morning: Slow start. Fish from the boat, pike, perch and zander are the lake's staples, under the public rod-and-line right.
itinerary.afternoon: Forage. From late July, bilberries carpet the forest floor; from August, chanterelles and ceps. Everyman's right allows this everywhere except gardens and cultivated land.
itinerary.evening: Cook what you caught and picked, then a proper long sauna. If your cabin has a smoke sauna (savusauna), it needs five hours of heating and it is worth every one of them.

itinerary.title: Savonlinna and Olavinlinna
itinerary.morning: Drive to Savonlinna. Olavinlinna is a 1475 medieval castle standing on a rock in the middle of the strait, one of the northernmost stone fortresses in the world, and it hosts an opera festival inside its courtyard in July.
itinerary.afternoon: The Kerimäki church nearby is the largest wooden church in the world, seating over 3,000 in a village of a few thousand. Then the Punkaharju esker, a narrow glacial ridge of pine forest between two lakes, a Finnish national landscape since the 19th century.
itinerary.evening: Back to the cabin. Restock food.

itinerary.title: The isolation night
itinerary.morning: Move to a second, more remote cabin: an island property reached by boat, or a rented hut with no electricity.
itinerary.afternoon: Do nothing on purpose. Swim, row, read, chop wood for the sauna.
itinerary.evening: No light pollution, and from late August the nights are dark enough for stars again, and occasionally aurora this far north.

itinerary.title: Out
itinerary.morning: Last swim, clean the cabin properly (this is expected in Finland, and the standard is high), return the boat.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive or train back to Helsinki.

items.subject: Pelicans, Beech and Bujtina: Eastern Albania Off the Grid
items.text: Eastern Albania is the country's quiet half: a high plateau of lakes at 700-900 m, walled in by 2,200 m ridges, with the Greek and Macedonian borders on three sides and almost no coach tourism. This week starts in Korçë among Ottoman bazaar streets and the painted churches of Voskopojë, drops to the Prespa lakes where a Macedonian-speaking minority farms beans on the shore of a lake full of Dalmatian pelicans, then works north through Lin and Pogradec on Lake Ohrid before finishing in the beech forest of Shebenik-Jabllanicë, a UNESCO primeval-beech site and the best-documented Albanian habitat of the Balkan lynx. You sleep almost entirely in bujtina, family homestays where dinner is not optional and the rakia is homemade. It suits people who want genuinely empty landscape, are relaxed about rough road, and accept that most of the week is cash, no signal, and a wood stove.

source.verified: Shebenik-Jabllanicë National Park area of roughly 34,500 ha, free entry, 14 glacial lakes at 1,500-1,900 m, Balkan lynx / brown bear / grey wolf presence, and the Rrajca beech forest's inscription as part of the UNESCO Ancient and Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians and Other Regions of Europe; Lesser Prespa as the world's largest Dalmatian pelican breeding colony and the catastrophic avian-influenza outbreak that struck it in early 2022; Balkan Lynx Recovery Programme monitoring in Albania run by PPNEA.

trip_data.title: Pelicans, Beech and Bujtina: Eastern Albania Off the Grid
trip_data.best_period: Mid-May-late June & September-mid-October
trip_data.avoid: December-March, the Shebenik glacial-lake tracks are snowbound, most Prespa homestays close, and the Rrajcë road ices badly
trip_data.budget: €680 to €1,100 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.
trip_data.difficulty: 3/5, walks of 8-15 km with 400-800 m ascent on shepherd paths and forest track; nothing technical, but way-marking in Shebenik is thin and a guide changes the day
trip_data.gateway: TIA Tirana, 2 h 30 to Korçë via Elbasan and 1 h 40 to Librazhd; OHD Ohrid (North Macedonia), 50 min to Pogradec via the Qafë Thanë border

itinerary.title: Into Korçë
itinerary.morning: Drive from Tirana over the Krrabë and through Elbasan and Librazhd, then up the Devoll to Korçë at 850 m, a city of low nineteenth-century houses, a serious Ottoman-era bazaar restored in the 2010s, and the country's first Albanian-language school, now a museum.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Old Bazaar, the Mirahori mosque (founded in the 1490s), and the National Museum of Medieval Art, which holds the best collection of Albanian icons in the country, including work by the Onufri school. Buy a week's supplies here, it is the last full supermarket before the mountains.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in the bazaar on Korçë staples: lakror pie, kernacka sausages, and a Birra Korça, brewed in the city since 1928.
itinerary.dayStats: 180 km drive / 2 h 30 / Korçë 850 m / last full supermarket for 3 days / museum entry roughly 700 ALL (€7)

itinerary.title: Voskopojë churches and Dardhë
itinerary.morning: Drive 21 km west to Voskopojë, which in the eighteenth century was one of the largest cities in the Balkans with a printing press and an academy, and is now a village of a few hundred among the ruins. Five post-Byzantine churches survive with extensive frescoes, St Nicholas, St Athanasius and the Prodromos among them. Several are locked; the keyholder lives nearby and is found by asking in the café.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue over to Dardhë, a stone village at 1,344 m in beech forest, then walk one of the loops above it. Slow afternoon by design; this is acclimatisation and the pleasantest air in eastern Albania.
itinerary.evening: Eat where you sleep, grilled meat, mountain trout, and the local honey and walnut everything.
itinerary.dayStats: 21 km to Voskopojë / Dardhë 1,344 m / 8 km walk, 350 m ascent / keyholder tip 300-500 ALL per church (€3 to €5) / five surviving frescoed churches

itinerary.title: Over the ridge to Prespa
itinerary.morning: Drive north-east from Korçë through Zvezdë and over the ridge into the Prespa basin, dropping to Greater Prespa at 850 m. The moment the lake appears, the character changes: the villages here, Pustec, Gollomboç, Gorica e Madhe, Zaroshkë, Cerje, are Macedonian-speaking, and the municipality is bilingual.
itinerary.afternoon: Take a boat from Gorica or Pustec to Maligrad, the small rock island in Albanian water, where the fourteenth-century cave church of Shën Maria is built into an overhang with surviving frescoes. Back on shore, walk up to the rock-cut hermitages above Zaroshkë, cut into the cliff face and reached by a steep scramble.
itinerary.evening: Homestay dinner: Prespa beans, which are the local pride, lake fish, and rakia poured by the host until you stop him.
itinerary.dayStats: 55 km drive / 1 h 15 / Prespa 850 m, Ohrid 695 m, 155 m apart and connected through karst / Maligrad boat roughly 3,000-5,000 ALL (€30 to €50) per boat / homestay 2,500-4,000 ALL per person with dinner

itinerary.title: A slow day on the lake
itinerary.morning: Be on the shore at first light with binoculars. Dalmatian pelicans move between Lesser and Greater Prespa and are most reliably seen on the water early; from the northern shore near Gorica you also look straight across at Golem Grad, the Macedonian island in the middle of the lake, notorious for its tortoises and water snakes and closed to Albanian-side boats.
itinerary.afternoon: Deliberately nothing. Swim, Prespa is warm and clean by August. Walk the shore path between two villages. Watch the bean harvest if it is September. There is no attraction to tick here and that is the point.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from the Zaroshkë cliffs, then back for dinner. Ask your host about the winter, when the lake sometimes freezes at the edges and the village halves.
itinerary.dayStats: 0-8 km walking / Prespa NP Albania roughly 27,750 ha, declared 1999 / Lesser Prespa holds the world's largest Dalmatian pelican colony / no entry fee / power cuts common, charge everything when you can

itinerary.title: Lin, Pogradec and the Ohrid shore
itinerary.morning: Drive north around the lakes and over to Lake Ohrid's Albanian shore. Stop at Lin, a peninsula village of steep lanes where a hilltop early-Christian basilica keeps sixth-century floor mosaics, and where excavation from 2023 revealed a Neolithic pile-dwelling settlement in the shallows dated to around 6000 BC, among the oldest lakeside villages known in Europe.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Pogradec and Tushemisht, where the Drilon springs feed a channel of clear water under plane trees. This is a resort strip by Albanian standards; treat it as the week's shower-and-laundry day.
itinerary.evening: Grilled koran, the Ohrid trout, subject to catch restrictions, so ask what is actually on the plate, on the lakefront.
itinerary.dayStats: 75 km drive / 1 h 40 / Lin basilica mosaics 6th c., pile dwellings dated to roughly 6000 BC / Ohrid 695 m / Qafë Thanë border 20 min from Pogradec

itinerary.title: Rrajcë, the primeval beech, and up into Shebenik
itinerary.morning: Drive north on the SH3 to Rrajcë in Librazhd municipality. The beech forest above the village is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list as part of the transnational Ancient and Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians and Other Regions of Europe, old, structurally complex, full of deadwood, and completely unlike the grazed hillsides around it. Walk it slowly with a park guide.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrange the 4x4 up from Fushë-Studë towards the glacial lakes. Shebenik-Jabllanicë covers about 34,500 hectares and holds fourteen glacial lakes between roughly 1,500 and 1,900 m, most of them shallow, cold and completely silent. Walk in from wherever the track gives up.
itinerary.evening: Back down to a Rrajcë or Fushë-Studë bujtina. Wood stove, spring water, no signal, dinner from the garden and the flock.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km drive / 4x4 track 9-12 km from Fushë-Studë / lakes at 1,500-1,900 m / park roughly 34,500 ha, free entry / 14 glacial lakes / Shebenik peak 2,262 m

itinerary.title: Jabllanica ridge, çaj mali, and out
itinerary.morning: A last walk on the Jabllanica side towards Stëblevë, the border village, on slopes where çaj mali grows in dry limestone grassland. In July and August you will meet people cutting it; watch how they do it, knife, above the wood, never the root, before you touch any yourself.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend and choose an exit. Qafë Thanë into North Macedonia puts you at Ohrid airport in under an hour; the SH3 west takes you to Tirana in two and a half. Clear the rental agency's cross-border paperwork in advance if you are leaving through Macedonia.
itinerary.evening: Last dinner in Librazhd or Elbasan, or on the Ohrid lakefront if you have crossed.
itinerary.dayStats: 8-12 km walk, 400-600 m ascent / çaj mali harvest July-August / Qafë Thanë border 55 min to OHD / Tirana 2 h 30 from Librazhd / green card and written permission needed for a border crossing in a rental

items.subject: Skûtsjes and Open Boats on the Frisian Lakes
items.text: A week chartering an open boat through the Frisian lake district, Sneek, Heeg, Stavoren, Makkum, with a taste of skûtsjesilen and the IJsselmeer's short steep chop.

trip_data.title: Skûtsjes and Open Boats on the Frisian Lakes
trip_data.gateway: Amsterdam Schiphol (AMS)

itinerary.title: Sneek and boat handover
itinerary.morning: Arrive in Sneek, home of the annual Sneekweek regatta and the natural hub of this lake district. Settle in and walk the Waterpoort, the 17th-century water gate that is the town's defining landmark.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus or taxi the short distance to Heeg, one of Friesland's main charter hubs, for boat handover with an established local charter operator such as Ottenhome Heeg. Boats under 15 m and below the inland speed threshold need no formal licence in the Netherlands, though a briefing on the boat's handling and the area's buoyage is standard practice and worth taking seriously.
itinerary.evening: First night aboard or back in Sneek, depending on the charter's mooring arrangement; either way, a short shakedown sail on the Heegermeer to get the feel of the boat before the open lakes tomorrow.
itinerary.dayStats: 1.5 water hours · Heegermeer, sheltered, 8-12 knots SW · open sailing boat, life jackets, no wetsuit required.

itinerary.title: Heeg and the Fluessen
itinerary.morning: Sail from Heeg onto the Fluessen, one of the larger open lakes in the district and a genuine test of open-water boat handling without the exposure of the IJsselmeer itself.
itinerary.afternoon: Work points of sail across the Fluessen's open stretch, then duck into the sheltered channels around Elahuizen and Oudega for a calmer finish to the day.
itinerary.evening: Moor at Heeg or continue back toward Sneek depending on the plan; both towns have well-serviced visitor moorings.
itinerary.dayStats: 4 water hours · Fluessen, 10-16 knots SW, moderate lake chop · open sailing boat, spray jacket.

itinerary.title: South to Stavoren
itinerary.morning: Sail south-west through the connecting waters toward Stavoren, the oldest town in Friesland and historically its main Zuiderzee trading port before the IJsselmeer's closure changed the coast's character entirely.
itinerary.afternoon: Moor in Stavoren's harbour and walk the small town centre, including the Vrouwe van Stavoren statue commemorating the local legend of a merchant's wife whose greed supposedly sank the harbour's fortune.
itinerary.evening: Stavoren's harbourside for dinner, with a clear view out toward the open IJsselmeer beyond the breakwater.
itinerary.dayStats: 3.5 water hours · Sheltered lakes and canals, 8-14 knots SW · open sailing boat.

itinerary.title: A careful look at the IJsselmeer
itinerary.morning: Check the forecast seriously before committing. The IJsselmeer is shallow, averaging only 5-6 m, and with roughly 50 km of open fetch it builds short, steep waves fast once the wind passes force 4, genuinely different water from the sheltered lakes and not to be underestimated in an open boat.
itinerary.afternoon: On a settled, moderate forecast, take a short exposure out from Stavoren's harbour mouth to feel that chop firsthand before turning back into sheltered water; on anything stronger, stay inside the harbour and use the day for the town and the small maritime museum instead.
itinerary.evening: Depart Stavoren back into the lake network, heading north toward Workum.
itinerary.dayStats: 2.5 water hours · IJsselmeer exposure (conditions-dependent) and sheltered return · open sailing boat, full waterproofs on deck.

itinerary.title: Workum and Hindeloopen
itinerary.morning: Sail to Workum, a handsome former Zuiderzee town with a long Waag and a well-preserved historic waterfront.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue a short hop to Hindeloopen, famous for its own distinct decorative painted-furniture tradition and for the Hindeloopen style of speed skating that gave the sport several of its early techniques. The Hidde Nijland Museum covers both.
itinerary.evening: Moor at Hindeloopen's small, picturesque harbour for the night.
itinerary.dayStats: 3 water hours · Sheltered lakes and connecting canals, 8-13 knots SW · open sailing boat.

itinerary.title: Makkum and the ceramics workshop
itinerary.morning: Sail north to Makkum, another former Zuiderzee port, now known above all for Koninklijke Tichelaar Makkum, the royal ceramics and tile workshop operating continuously since 1572, genuinely one of the oldest companies in the Netherlands.
itinerary.afternoon: Visit the workshop, then sail back south-east into the lake network, retracing part of the Elfstedentocht's summer-sailable route toward Sneek.
itinerary.evening: Overnight on the water or back into Sneek, depending on how the week's schedule has run.
itinerary.dayStats: 4 water hours · Sheltered lakes and canals, 8-14 knots SW · open sailing boat.

itinerary.title: Sneekermeer and handover
itinerary.morning: Finish on the Sneekermeer itself, the lake that hosts Sneekweek each August and, in season, carries skûtsjesilen races between the SKS's competing towns, traditional Frisian sailing barges, some over a century old, raced under enormous sail area by teams drawn from the towns they represent.
itinerary.afternoon: Return the boat at Heeg and take a taxi or bus back to Sneek.
itinerary.evening: Train to Schiphol for the evening flight, or an extra night in Sneek before an early departure.
itinerary.dayStats: 2 water hours · Sneekermeer, 10-15 knots SW · open sailing boat.

items.subject: Hvitløypa
items.text: Hvitløypa is a waymarked hiking route in Norway with a distance of 11.5 km. The route starts and finishes at the same place, featuring 251 m of ascent and 252 m of descent.

items.subject: Lisbon on Foot: Seven Hills, Seven Days
items.text: Lisbon rewards people who accept that the city is a staircase. This week trades the tram-28 conveyor belt for a neighbourhood sequence: the Moorish tangle of Alfama and Mouraria, then the Pombaline grid and the literary hills of Chiado and Bairro Alto, then Príncipe Real, then the river, Belém's Manueline stonework west, Marvila's warehouse breweries east. Distances are short, gradients are not. A Sintra day breaks the week open with fog and Romantic follies. It suits travellers who want architecture and food weighted equally.

source.verified: Navegante Ocasional card cost (€0.50), 24h Carris/Metro pass (€7.25), zapping versus on-board single fares, and the airport Red Line routing were checked against 2026 Lisbon fare summaries; the €4 per person per night city tax was confirmed for 2026.

trip_data.title: Lisbon on Foot: Seven Hills, Seven Days
trip_data.best_period: Mid-March-early June & mid-September-end October
trip_data.avoid: July-August, 35°C on the calçada, Alfama unwalkable by noon, peak prices.
trip_data.budget: €1,025 to €1,675 per person, excl. international flights
trip_data.difficulty: 2-8-12 km a day on steep basalt cobbles, 150-250 m cumulative ascent; hard on ankles, not on lungs.
trip_data.gateway: LIS, Humberto Delgado; Metro Red Line to Alameda 20 min, taxi to Baixa 20-25 min (€15-20)

itinerary.title: Landing on the Grid: Baixa and Chiado
itinerary.morning: Metro to Baixa-Chiado, drop bags, walk the Pombaline grid from Praça do Comércio up Rua Augusta, note the standardised window bays, Manuel da Maia's prefab logic in stone. A bica standing at Confeitaria Nacional on Praça da Figueira, open since 1829.
itinerary.afternoon: The roofless Convento do Carmo (€7) is the truest surviving image of 1 November 1755. Then Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea-Chiado on Rua Serpa Pinto, and up via the Elevador da Glória to Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara.
itinerary.evening: Taberna da Rua das Flores (no. 103), no reservations, arrive 19:00, chalkboard menu, €25-35pp. Ginjinha at A Ginjinha, Largo de São Domingos, €1.60.
itinerary.dayStats: 5.5 km, 130 m ascent; Metro Red + Green; Navegante €0.50 + 24h pass €7.25; Carmo 10:00-19:00.

itinerary.title: Alfama and Mouraria end to end
itinerary.morning: Bus 737 from Praça da Figueira to Castelo de São Jorge (€15) for the 09:00 opening and empty ramparts, then walk down through Largo do Contador Mor.
itinerary.afternoon: Rua de São Pedro and Beco do Carneiro into lower Alfama; the Sé (Romanesque, 1147, twin fortress towers, cloister €5). Cross into Mouraria by Rua dos Cavaleiros for Largo da Severa and the grocers of Rua do Benformoso, the least gentrified inner quarter.
itinerary.evening: Fado at Mesa de Frades, Rua dos Remédios 139A, a tiled former chapel; 20:00 sitting, book 3-5 days ahead, ~€45 with food. Cheaper walk-in alternative: Tasca do Chico, Rua do Diário de Notícias 39.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.8 km, 210 m ascent; bus 737; castle €15, opens 09:00; fado 20:00-21:00 starts.

itinerary.title: Belém: Manueline stone, modern riverfront
itinerary.morning: Tram 15E from Praça da Figueira (25 min). Mosteiro dos Jerónimos on a 09:30 slot (€18 combined with Torre de Belém; church nave free). The two-storey cloister and Castilho's south portal are the reason to come.
itinerary.afternoon: MAAT (€11), Levete's crouching pavilion plus the 1908 Central Tejo boiler hall, which is the better half. Torre de Belém from outside; the interior queue rarely repays 45 minutes.
itinerary.evening: Cervejaria Ramiro, Av. Almirante Reis 1, garlic prawns, then a prego as dessert. No bookings; take a ticket, expect 30-50 min, €35-45pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 6.2 km flat; tram 15E ~€1.66; Jerónimos 09:30-18:00, closed Mon; MAAT closed Tue.

itinerary.title: Príncipe Real, Estrela, Gulbenkian
itinerary.morning: Up through Praça das Flores to Praça do Príncipe Real and its 1863 cedar canopy; Embaixada inside the neo-Moorish Ribeiro da Cunha palace. On to Jardim da Estrela and the 1790 Basílica da Estrela dome.
itinerary.afternoon: Metro Blue Line to São Sebastião for the Calouste Gulbenkian (€14, Founder's + Modern; free Sun after 14:00). Two hours minimum, the Lalique room, the Rembrandt wall, and Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles's garden.
itinerary.evening: A Cevicheria, Rua Dom Pedro V 129 (no reservations, leave your name, drink pisco next door), or Cantinho do Avillez, Rua dos Duques de Bragança 7, booked a week out, €40-55pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.1 km, 170 m ascent; Metro Blue; Gulbenkian €14, 10:00-18:00, closed Tue.

itinerary.title: Sintra day trip
itinerary.morning: Rossio 08:11 train, 40 min, ~€2.40. Bus 434 up to Palácio da Pena for a 09:30-10:00 slot (park + palace €20), Ferdinand II's 1840s Romantic collage of Manueline quotation, Moorish tile and Bavarian battlement.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Castelo dos Mouros ramparts (€12), then the Palácio Nacional de Sintra with its conical kitchen chimneys (€13). In heavy fog, swap for Quinta da Regaleira (€15) and its initiation well.
itinerary.evening: Back by 19:00. Bistro 100 Maneiras, Largo da Trindade 9 (book 2 weeks, €70-90pp) or petiscos at Taberna Sal Grosso, Calçada do Forte 22.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.4 km incl. Sintra hills, 320 m ascent; ~€4.80 train return; Pena last entry 18:00.

itinerary.title: Azulejos east: Xabregas, Marvila, Beato
itinerary.morning: Bus 794 to the Museu Nacional do Azulejo in the Madre de Deus convent (€8, closed Mon). The 23-metre panorama of pre-earthquake Lisbon upstairs explains what 1755 erased better than any text.
itinerary.afternoon: North into Marvila/Beato: Dois Corvos taproom on Rua Capitão Leitão, the Fábrica Braço de Prata warehouse, Underdogs Gallery's wall on Rua Fernando Palha. Industrial Lisbon converting itself in real time.
itinerary.evening: Prado, Travessa das Pedras Negras 2, produce-led, book 2-3 weeks, €45-60pp. Late drink at Pensão Amor, Rua do Alecrim 19.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.6 km, flat; bus 794/210; Azulejo 10:00-13:00 & 14:00-18:00; taproom pints €4-5.

itinerary.title: Estuary morning and departure
itinerary.morning: Ferry Cais do Sodré → Cacilhas (10 min, ~€1.55) for the reverse skyline and lunch at Ponto Final, Rua do Ginjal 72, booked ahead. Or Elevador de Santa Justa at 08:30, before the queue.
itinerary.afternoon: Last pastéis at Manteigaria, Rua do Loreto 2 (€1.40, at the marble counter), then Metro Red Line to LIS from Alameda.
itinerary.evening: Flight out; a closing vermouth at Comida Independente, Rua Cais do Tojo 28, if the slot is late.
itinerary.dayStats: 4.5 km; ferry 10 min; airport 25 min from Baixa-Chiado with one change; allow 2 h before departure.

items.subject: Hamburg in a day
items.text: Hamburg in a day is a one day city sightseeing walk between the city's main sights in Germany. The route covers 5.1 km of walking between stops.

items.subject: Marble and Granite: A Pirin Hut-to-Hut Week from Bansko
items.text: Pirin changes underfoot halfway through the week. The north is white Triassic marble, bright, sharp, waterless, murder on boot rands, and the centre is grey granite that holds a hundred lakes in its hollows. In…

trip_data.title: Marble and Granite: A Pirin Hut-to-Hut Week from Bansko
trip_data.best_period: the second half of September, snow gone from Koncheto, huts half-empty, storm frequency dropping
trip_data.avoid: before mid-June (old snow on the Vihren north side and in the Kazana couloirs) and the 6 September and 22 September national holidays, when every hut fills with Bulgarian parties
trip_data.difficulty: Hard
trip_data.gateway: Sofia (SOF) airport, then a direct bus to Bansko from Sofia Central Bus Station (2 h 45-3 h 15) or the narrow-gauge Septemvri-Dobrinishte railway, the slowest and best-looking train in the Balkans. Plovdiv (PDV) is a 3 h 30 alternative.

itinerary.title: Bansko to the Bunderitsa
itinerary.morning: Arrive in Bansko (925 m), a town of stone-and-timber Revival houses with a ski resort bolted on. Draw hut cash at an ATM on Pirin Street, your last machine for six days, and eat at a mehana on the old square.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the Bansko gondola to Banderishka polyana, or share a jeep taxi up the Bunderitsa road from the gondola base, the road is rough, unsurfaced above Hizha Banderitsa, and driven by locals in vehicles you would not rent. Stop at Baikushev's Pine, a Bosnian pine (Pinus heldreichii) estimated at over 1,300 years old, standing in the forest just below Hizha Banderitsa.
itinerary.evening: Walk the last stretch to Hizha Vihren (1,950 m), the busiest hut in the range and the base for everything that follows. Confirm your onward beds by phone from the warden's desk while there is still signal.
itinerary.dayStats: 7 km / +330 m with mechanical assist

itinerary.title: Vihren, 2,914 m, by the Kazana cirque
itinerary.morning: Leave by 06:30. The red trail climbs to the Kazana ("the cauldron") cirque, a marble amphitheatre that holds snow into July, then zigzags to the summit ridge. Four to four and a half hours up.
itinerary.afternoon: Vihren, 2,914 m, Bulgaria's second-highest summit after Musala, with the Banski Suhodol wall one side and the granite south the other. Descend the same way; polished wet marble is treacherous.
itinerary.evening: Back at Hizha Vihren, walk twenty minutes to the Banderishki lakes, a granite-rimmed chain below Todorka, then bean soup and an early night.

itinerary.title: Kutelo, Koncheto and the long drop to Yavorov
itinerary.morning: The decision day. Up the red line to Premkata saddle and Kutelo (2,908 m), Bulgaria's third summit, in about three hours. Check the wind on the col; if it pushes you around, turn back.
itinerary.afternoon: Koncheto, the cabled knife-edge, then Banski Suhodol (2,884 m) and a long, loose, waterless descent to Hizha Yavorov (1,740 m). Allow eight to ten hours door to door and carry three litres.
itinerary.evening: Yavorov is small, wood-heated and cash-only, the Kutelo wall filling the window. No shop, no card machine.

itinerary.title: Down to Razlog, round to the Bunderitsa
itinerary.morning: The green trail down the Suhodol ridge to the Predel road, then a bus or shared transfer into Razlog, the honest way to reposition, because there is no low traverse under the marble wall.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus Razlog to Bansko (20 minutes), resupply at the Kaufland on the edge of town, then a jeep taxi back up the Bunderitsa road to Hizha Vihren.
itinerary.evening: A short day is not a wasted one. Wash socks, eat two dinners, and study the Vasilashki plateau on the hut's wall map, tomorrow is the longest stretch above 2,300 m.

itinerary.title: The classic high crossing to Tevno Ezero
itinerary.morning: Climb to the Banderishka porta under Todorka (2,746 m), then traverse south past the upper Banderishki lakes on granite slab. After yesterday's marble the change of rock is unmistakable underfoot.
itinerary.afternoon: Over the Todorina porta and down into the Vasilashki lakes, a basin of a dozen tarns, then the long rise to Hizha Tevno Ezero (2,510 m), sitting on the shore of its own black lake. Seven to eight hours.
itinerary.evening: Pirin's highest hut and its most spartan: bunks, blankets, a gas ring, no shower, sometimes no warden late in the season. Sunset over Dzhengal is the compensation.

itinerary.title: Popovo Lake and the granite south
itinerary.morning: Contour east under Dzhengal (2,730 m) on the red E4 line. If the weather has broken, escape south over the Mozgovishka porta to Hizha Pirin (Kamenitsa, 1,640 m) and the Sandanski road, know this before you need it.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop to Popovo Lake (2,234 m), the largest and deepest glacial lake in Pirin, then round the Dzhano shoulder and descend to Hizha Bezbog (2,236 m) in three to four hours.
itinerary.evening: Bezbog has electricity, a proper kitchen and a card machine, the first hot shower since Bansko.

itinerary.title: Bezbog Lake, then the chairlift out
itinerary.morning: A pre-breakfast lap to Bezbogsko Lake, then the 45-minute pull to Bezbog peak (2,645 m) for a last look north along the ridge you walked.
itinerary.afternoon: The Bezbog chairlift down to Hizha Gotse Delchev, then the shuttle road to Dobrinishte. If the lift is down, the forest path adds two hours.
itinerary.evening: Soak in Dobrinishte's mineral pools, eat kavarma with a grape rakia, then take the narrow-gauge train or a bus back to Sofia.
itinerary.dayStats: 7 km / +180 / −1,050 m with lift

items.subject: Torun, Poland
items.text: Gothic brick lanes, gingerbread and the house of Copernicus above the Vistula

source.text: Toruń (Kashubian: Torń, German: Thorn) is a beautiful, medieval city in North-Western Poland, situated on the Vistula River. Its architecture was not hit by bombs during World War II, and as such represents one of the few examples of true Gothic architecture in Poland.

On the way: the peak Flotsenberg (102 m), and the castles Kasteel Calmeyn and Kasteel van Beersel. It goes close to Manneken Peace and Brussels. Usually walkable all year.
