items.subject: Verbier and the 4 Vallées: Mont-Fort, Tortin and the Stairway to Heaven
items.text: A week in Verbier and the 4 Vallées built around Mont-Fort, the Stairway to Heaven and Tortin, with an honest read of where the lift interconnect actually breaks down.

trip_data.title: Verbier and the 4 Vallées: Mont-Fort, Tortin and the Stairway to Heaven
trip_data.gateway: Geneva (GVA)

itinerary.title: Arrival and gear check
itinerary.morning: Fly to Geneva; shuttle or train (Geneva-Martigny, then the Le Châble gondola) up to Verbier at 1,500 m.
itinerary.afternoon: Check into the base hotel and visit a rental shop for skis or a splitboard, boots and full avalanche kit, transceiver, probe, shovel. Register with La Fantastique or the Bureau des Guides de Verbier for the week's guided days.
itinerary.evening: Buy the 4 Vallées pass and check the Valais avalanche bulletin for the coming days.
itinerary.dayStats: 0 vertical metres skied · 0 sectors · 0 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Local orientation: Savoleyres and Lac des Vaux
itinerary.morning: Ride the Savoleyres gondola on Verbier's quieter, south-facing side, a good first day to read the group's ability on varied but non-glacial terrain.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to Lac des Vaux and the lower Attelas sector, working toward the base of the Mont-Fort lift chain to see current conditions and queue length before committing a full day to it.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner; tomorrow starts early to beat the Mont-Fort queue.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 3,000 m vertical · 2 sectors (Savoleyres, Lac des Vaux) · 4 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Mont-Fort and the Stairway to Heaven
itinerary.morning: Be at the Médran lift base in Verbier by 08:00. Ride up through Les Ruinettes to Attelas (2,727 m), then the Mont-Fort cable car to 3,330 m, the single access point to the glacier terrain and the most wind-sensitive lift in the network; it is the first thing to close in a storm and the reason this day is scheduled early in the week, not the last possible morning.
itinerary.afternoon: With a guide, ski the Stairway to Heaven: from the Mont-Fort glacier or Col des Gentianes, a long, roughly 2,000 m off-piste descent down the Combe de Tortin to the Tortin lift base. Crevasses on the upper glacier and variable snow on the lower combe make this a guided itinerary, run by La Fantastique or the Bureau des Guides de Verbier, not a solo line regardless of visible tracks.
itinerary.evening: Recovery dinner; this is the physically hardest day of the week.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,700 m vertical · 1 itinerary (Stairway to Heaven) · 3 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Tortin face and Siviez
itinerary.morning: Ride the Jumbo gondola from Le Châble/Verbier toward Attelas, then down into the Tortin sector via the Chassoure-Tortin cable car. The Tortin piste itself is one of the network's steepest marked runs, north-facing and mogul-prone by midday; ski it early while it is still firm rather than broken up.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue into Siviez and across toward Nendaz, sampling the interconnect's mid-mountain pistes, which are considerably gentler than the Verbier side.
itinerary.evening: Return via the same chain to Verbier.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,900 m vertical · 2 sectors (Tortin, Siviez/Nendaz) · 4.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: The full 4 Vallées traverse
itinerary.morning: A long point-to-point day linking Verbier through Siviez to Veysonnaz and on to Thyon, using the full chain of gondolas and chairlifts that gives the area its name. This is a logistics exercise as much as a ski day, plan lift closing times at each valley in advance, since missing the last connection strands you a taxi ride from Verbier.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the Thyon/Veysonnaz pistes, generally sunnier and lower-altitude than Mont-Fort, then begin the return traverse in good time.
itinerary.evening: Confirm the last uphill connection back over Attelas before it closes; if in doubt, descend to Le Châble by road transport rather than risk it.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 3,400 m vertical · 4 sectors (Verbier, Siviez, Veysonnaz, Thyon) · 5.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Second glacier day or La Tzoumaz bad-snow plan B
itinerary.morning: Check Mont-Fort's status before deciding: if it is running and the snowpack has stabilised, a second guided glacier itinerary off Col des Gentianes extends the week's off-piste tally. If the top chain is on wind hold or the lower slopes are worn thin by traffic and sun, switch to La Tzoumaz on the sunnier, more sheltered side of the valley, lower altitude but more forgiving and typically less crowded.
itinerary.afternoon: Either continuation of the glacier plan, or a relaxed tree-lined afternoon on La Tzoumaz's runs, a genuine fallback rather than a consolation prize.
itinerary.evening: Gear rinse and pack check ahead of the last day.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,200-2,700 m vertical · 1 sector (Mont-Fort or La Tzoumaz) · 4 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Final morning and departure
itinerary.morning: A short session on the Savoleyres side, the most reliable sector for a low-key last morning regardless of what the top of the mountain is doing.
itinerary.afternoon: Return gear, shuttle to Geneva.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 1,300 m vertical · 1 sector (Savoleyres) · 2 lift hours.

items.subject: Grazalema, Spain

source.text: Grazalema is a town of 2,050 people (2018) in the south-western Andalucia region of Spain. It is one of the largest 'white towns' (Spanish: pueblos blancos) of the Sierra la Grazalema national park, and is also Spain's wettest city.

items.subject: Durmitor Ridges
items.text: Durmitor is a compact, savage limestone massif with 48 peaks over 2,000 m packed into an area you can drive across in forty minutes, and Žabljak at 1,456 m is the highest town in the Balkans, which means you sleep at altitude and start every run from a car park rather than a valley. The rock is pale, fluted karst with almost no soil, so the running is fast on the grass shelves and genuinely sharp on the ridges. The week arcs from a lake-circuit warm-up through the two showpiece summits, Bobotov Kuk and Prutaš, into a two-day Škrčka lakes excursion with a hut night, then a recovery day on the Tara canyon rim and a fast finish on Savin Kuk. It suits runners who like empty mountains, do not need refuge comfort, and can carry their own water.

source.verified: Durmitor National Park entry is charged per person per day at approximately €5, with a Montenegro all-national-parks card around €13.50; the Bobotov Kuk out-and-back from Sedlo is about 9.9 km with roughly 939 m of ascent and the Sedlo trailhead is around a 25-minute drive from Žabljak on the P14; Montenegro uses the euro without being in the eurozone.

trip_data.title: Durmitor Ridges
trip_data.best_period: Mid-June-mid-July & early September-early October
trip_data.avoid: November-May (Sedlo pass road snow-blocked, high ridges unrunnable, Žabljak is a ski town); late July-August has the crowds and afternoon storms
trip_data.budget: €780 to €1,250 per person, excl. international flights
trip_data.difficulty: 4/5-1,000-1,400 m days on sharp karst with short exposed scrambles; no glacier, but very little forgiving ground
trip_data.gateway: TGD, Podgorica (2 h-2 h 30 drive to Žabljak via Nikšić or the Tara bridge); TIV, Tivat is 2 h 45

itinerary.title: Drive up from Podgorica, warm up at Crno jezero
itinerary.morning: Land at TGD, collect the car, drive north through the Moraća canyon and over to Žabljak (1,456 m), 2 h to 2 h 30 depending on route. Buy the national park ticket at the Crno jezero booth or the visitor centre.
itinerary.afternoon: Shake out on the Crno jezero (Black Lake) circuit, 3.6 km around both basins on flat forest track, then add the gentle climb to the Zminje jezero for another 4 km. Enough to feel the altitude, not enough to cost anything.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Žabljak, cicvara, kajmak and lamb ispod sača at one of the town's konobas; wash it down with a local Vranac.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km / 220 m D+ / T1 / 55 min-1 h 15; drive 2 h-2 h 30; NP entry ~€5.

itinerary.title: Prutaš, the slab mountain
itinerary.morning: Drive the P14 road to Sedlo pass (1,907 m), 25 minutes from Žabljak, and park at the col. Run the ridge south-west to Prutaš (2,393 m), grass shelves, then the famous banded limestone strata tilted like the pages of a book.
itinerary.afternoon: Return over Sedlo and add the short spur north toward Velika Previja for the first sight of the Škrka cirque and Bobotov's south face. Back to Žabljak by mid-afternoon.
itinerary.evening: Beer on the Žabljak main street; early dinner and a properly early night before tomorrow.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.2 km / 560 m D+ / T2-T3 / 1 h 30-2 h / high point 2,393 m / no water above Žabljak.

itinerary.title: Bobotov Kuk, 2,523 m
itinerary.morning: Leave Žabljak at 06:15 for Sedlo. Climb the scree gully and the traverse to Velika Previja, then the cabled, exposed final ridge onto Bobotov Kuk (2,523 m), the classic Durmitor summit, with the whole Tara canyon system on one side and Bosnian ranges on the other.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend by the same route to Sedlo, or, if fit, take the long variant down to Lokvice katun and out via Ivan Do to Žabljak, refilling at the katun spring and buying cheese from the shepherds.
itinerary.evening: Recovery meal in Žabljak; a soak in the hotel wellness if it has one.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.9 km / 940 m D+ (or 19 km / 1,450 m by Lokvice) / T3 with cables / 2 h 15-3 h / 2 L water minimum.

itinerary.title: Down into the Škrka cirque, hut night
itinerary.morning: Sedlo again, but this time run north-west over Velika Previja and drop into the Škrka cirque, a 500 m descent on loose karst steps into the most isolated bowl in the park, holding Veliko and Malo Škrčko jezero at about 1,686 m.
itinerary.afternoon: Easy exploration of the two lakes and the surrounding pastures, then check into the Škrka mountain hut, basic, bunk-bed, hot food, and the only building for hours in any direction.
itinerary.evening: Hut dinner and one of the darkest night skies in Europe; the cirque walls block every light source.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km in / 250 m up, 550 m down / T3 / 1 h 30-2 h / hut at ~1,700 m, ~€15 to €20.

itinerary.title: Climb out, then a genuine recovery afternoon on the Tara rim
itinerary.morning: Reverse the climb out of the cirque to Sedlo, 550 m up, taken slowly as the only hard effort of the day, and drive back to Žabljak.
itinerary.afternoon: True low day. An easy 7 km jog out to the Ćurevac viewpoint (1,625 m) on soft forest track for the head-on view 1,300 m down into the Tara canyon, the deepest in Europe. Then coffee and nothing else.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Žabljak; plan the last two days around the forecast.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km out / 550 m D+, then 7 km / 300 m D+ / total ~1 h 50 running / Tara canyon depth ~1,300 m.

itinerary.title: Savin Kuk and the Tara river
itinerary.morning: From Crno jezero, climb Savin Kuk (2,313 m) on the ski-area flank and the summit ridge, a shorter, less committing summit than Bobotov with an equally complete panorama over the Žabljak plateau and the Piva side.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to the Đurđevića Tara bridge and take a half-day raft on the Tara, cold, fast, green water at the bottom of the canyon you looked into yesterday. The best possible active recovery.
itinerary.evening: Grilled trout and rakija at a riverside restaurant near the bridge.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km / 900 m D+ / T2-T3 / 2 h-2 h 45; rafting €40 to €55 half-day; 35 min drive to the bridge.

itinerary.title: Katun loop and the drive out
itinerary.morning: Last run: the Ivan Do-Lokvice katun loop from Crno jezero, up through black pine to the shepherds' summer settlement at about 1,800 m and back on the Zminje side, the most characteristic Durmitor ground, all pasture, karst pavement and sheep bells.
itinerary.afternoon: Buy cheese and honey in Žabljak, then the drive south to Podgorica, ideally via the Tara bridge and the Piva canyon if the flight allows.
itinerary.evening: Departure from TGD.
itinerary.dayStats: 13 km / 700 m D+ / 2 h-2 h 30; drive to TGD 2 h-2 h 30.

items.subject: The GR54, Refuges of the Écrins Amphitheatre
items.text: A hut-to-hut week on the GR54 beneath La Meije, from the Vénéon valley's Refuge du Chatelleret to the Col d'Arsine above Villar-d'Arêne.

trip_data.title: The GR54, Refuges of the Écrins Amphitheatre
trip_data.gateway: Grenoble (GNB) or Lyon (LYS)

itinerary.title: Bourg-d'Oisans to La Bérarde
itinerary.morning: Bus from Bourg-d'Oisans up the Vénéon valley through Venosc, where the road narrows and the valley walls close in fast, this drive alone signals the scale of what's ahead.
itinerary.afternoon: From the roadhead at La Bérarde, an old mountaineering hamlet at 1,720 m with no through-road, walk the short but scenic path up to Refuge du Carrelet (1,908 m), sitting directly below the Barre des Écrins massif.
itinerary.evening: Book Refuge du Carrelet through the FFCAM refuges.info network or by direct phone; it is a small hut and fills on peak summer weekends.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km, 550 m ascent (bus-assisted approach to La Bérarde), 200 m descent, 2-3 hours walking. Grade T2, well-built valley path, no exposure.

itinerary.title: Refuge du Carrelet to Refuge du Chatelleret
itinerary.morning: Descend briefly to La Bérarde, then take the parallel valley path up toward the base of La Meije's north face, one of the great alpine walls, following the Étançons torrent.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb steadily to Refuge du Chatelleret (2,225 m), a small CAF hut with arguably the best amphitheatre view of any refuge in the Écrins, the Meije's glaciers hang directly overhead.
itinerary.evening: Book through refuges.info or by direct phone; this hut is popular with climbers acclimatising for the Meije's classic routes as well as GR54 walkers, so cross-reference dates early.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km, 650 m ascent, 350 m descent, 3.5-4 hours. Grade T3, rocky moraine path, moderate exposure near the glacier snout viewpoint.

itinerary.title: Refuge du Chatelleret to La Bérarde and transfer to Villar-d'Arêne
itinerary.morning: Descend from Chatelleret back to La Bérarde on the same valley path, taking the morning light on the Meije face from below.
itinerary.afternoon: Catch the bus from La Bérarde back down the Vénéon to Bourg-d'Oisans, then a connecting bus over the Col du Lautaret (2,058 m) to Villar-d'Arêne, a genuine change of massif and light in one road journey.
itinerary.evening: Overnight in Villar-d'Arêne, a small stone village that has served alpinists heading for the Meije's northern approaches for well over a century.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km walking, 350 m ascent, 650 m descent; remainder by bus. A deliberate rest-and-transfer day.

itinerary.title: Villar-d'Arêne to Refuge de l'Alpe du Villar-d'Arêne
itinerary.morning: Climb out of the village onto the Plateau d'Emparis approach path, following the GR54's red-and-white balisage up through alpine pasture grazed by mixed herds in summer.
itinerary.afternoon: The path steepens toward Refuge de l'Alpe du Villar-d'Arêne, a CAF hut set on an open shoulder with a wide panorama back over the Meije and forward toward the glaciated Arsine valley.
itinerary.evening: Book through refuges.info; this hut is smaller than Chatelleret and sells out on clear-forecast August weekends.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km, 900 m ascent, 100 m descent, 4.5-5 hours. Grade T2-T3, open pasture and moraine track, no significant exposure.

itinerary.title: Refuge de l'Alpe du Villar-d'Arêne over the Col d'Arsine to Refuge du Pigeonnier
itinerary.morning: Climb steadily along the true right bank of the Glacier d'Arsine's outwash to the Col d'Arsine (2,348 m), a broad, non-technical saddle with the glacier's tongue close on one side.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the far side into a quieter, less-visited valley, reaching Refuge du Pigeonnier by mid-afternoon, a small, simply-run hut that makes a deliberately restful stop after the col.
itinerary.evening: Book Refuge du Pigeonnier by direct phone; it is not always listed on the main online booking calendar and the warden prefers a call.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km, 650 m ascent, 550 m descent, 4.5-5.5 hours. Grade T3, glacier-adjacent moraine and scree, no fixed protection but genuine altitude exposure near the col.

itinerary.title: Refuge du Pigeonnier back over the Col d'Arsine and down to Villar-d'Arêne
itinerary.morning: Re-cross the Col d'Arsine, this time with the Meije and the Écrins skyline ahead rather than behind, worth doing even as a there-and-back for the reversed view.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend past the Refuge de l'Alpe du Villar-d'Arêne without stopping and continue down to the village, closing the loop on foot rather than by bus.
itinerary.evening: A last night in Villar-d'Arêne, with time to walk the village's small Romanesque church and watch the light change on the Meije.
itinerary.dayStats: 16 km, 400 m ascent, 1,650 m descent, 6-6.5 hours. Grade T3 at the col, easing to T1-T2 lower down.

itinerary.title: Villar-d'Arêne to Bourg-d'Oisans
itinerary.morning: A relaxed final morning; walk the short Plateau d'Emparis loop above the village for one last high view if legs allow, or simply pack and wait for the bus.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus back over the Col du Lautaret to Bourg-d'Oisans, with a stop possible at the Lautaret's alpine botanical garden if the timetable allows.
itinerary.evening: A final dinner in Bourg-d'Oisans, and onward transport to Grenoble.
itinerary.dayStats: 4-8 km optional walking, under 300 m ascent/descent; the day is primarily a transfer.

items.subject: Carp Country, Cycling the Třeboň Ponds and the Vltava
items.text: Flat dam-top gravel through a 700-year-old fishpond landscape, linked to the Vltava cycle path and the climb into Český Krumlov.

trip_data.title: Carp Country, Cycling the Třeboň Ponds and the Vltava
trip_data.gateway: Prague (PRG)

itinerary.title: Into the basin, around Svět
itinerary.morning: Train from Prague to České Budějovice, then the regional line east to Třeboň. ČD charges a bike ticket of roughly CZK 45-65 (approx €2.00-2.60), plus a compulsory bike seat reservation of about CZK 35 on express services with a marked bike wagon.
itinerary.afternoon: A gentle first loop around Svět, the pond that Třeboň sits on. The circuit is 12 km of packed dam-top gravel and asphalt, past the Schwarzenberg family tomb at Domanín, a neo-Gothic mausoleum in a wood, open in season for approx CZK 120.
itinerary.evening: Třeboň's Masarykovo náměstí is an unbroken Renaissance square with arcades on both sides. Eat carp: Šupina a Šupinka near the Svinenská gate has been serving pond fish for decades and does a fried carp and a carp soup that justify the trip.
itinerary.dayStats: 28 km, +90 m, half packed gravel dam-tops, half asphalt.

itinerary.title: Rožmberk, the largest pond in the country
itinerary.morning: North to the Rožmberk dam, built 1584-1590 by Jakub Krčín of Jelčany for the Rožmberk lords. It holds 489 hectares of water behind an earth wall planted with 400-year-old oaks. The dam top is a wide grass-and-gravel road, closed to cars.
itinerary.afternoon: Follow the Zlatá stoka, the Golden Canal, 45 km of hand-cut channel finished in 1520 and still feeding the whole system, to Stará Hlína, then back past the Nová řeka diversion canal. Reed beds, herons, eagles.
itinerary.evening: The Třeboň spa houses, Bertiny lázně and Lázně Aurora, both sell peat baths and swim access to non-residents. After 70 km on gravel, take the peat bath.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km, +140 m, roughly 40 km of crushed limestone and packed sand.

itinerary.title: Novohradské foothills and the Greenway
itinerary.morning: South on the Greenway Praha-Vídeň, the marked Prague-Vienna corridor, through Chlum u Třeboně and its glassworks village toward Nové Hrady. The land rises for the first time.
itinerary.afternoon: Nové Hrady has a Rožmberk castle, an Empire-period chateau and the Terčino údolí landscape park with its artificial waterfall. Return north on quiet asphalt through Borovany, whose Augustinian monastery has been restored as a cultural centre.
itinerary.evening: Last night in Třeboň. Walk the town walls and the Rožmberk brewery courtyard; the beer is Regent, brewed here since 1379.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km, +410 m, mostly asphalt with 8 km of forest gravel.

itinerary.title: West to České Budějovice via Hluboká
itinerary.morning: Leave Třeboň westward on quiet field roads through Lomnice nad Lužnicí and Veselí nad Lužnicí, then pick up the Vltava corridor. Bags go ahead: Top Bicycle and AVE Bicycle Tours both run luggage transfer across South Bohemia for roughly €12-18 per bag per stage.
itinerary.afternoon: Hluboká nad Vltavou is a Windsor-style neo-Gothic pile rebuilt by the Schwarzenbergs in the 1840s; approx CZK 350, tours timed, so buy the slot on arrival. The Alšova jihočeská galerie in the old riding school is quieter.
itinerary.evening: Roll into České Budějovice on the riverside path. Náměstí Přemysla Otakara II is one of the largest medieval squares in Central Europe, 133 metres a side.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km, +230 m, asphalt with 6 km crushed limestone along the Vltava.

itinerary.title: Holašovice and the Blanský les edge
itinerary.morning: West out of Budějovice through Dubné on lanes to Holašovice, a UNESCO-listed village of rural Baroque farmhouse gables around a green with two ponds. Twenty-two protected homesteads, still lived in.
itinerary.afternoon: Loop south under the Blanský les hills to Křemže and back along the Vltava. This is the first day with sustained rolling, and the return along the river is fast.
itinerary.evening: Budvar's brewery runs English tours at fixed times, approx CZK 250; the beer at source is noticeably softer. Otherwise the Masné krámy beer hall in the old butchers' arcade.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km, +480 m, asphalt with 5 km gravel.

itinerary.title: Up the Vltava to Český Krumlov
itinerary.morning: The Vltava cycle path south from Budějovice is the prettiest riding of the week: a mostly asphalt riverside route through Boršov and Zlatá Koruna, where the Cistercian abbey of 1263 keeps one of the best-preserved Gothic cloisters in Bohemia (approx CZK 180).
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Český Krumlov, arriving over the meander with the castle tower directly above. Push the last cobbled climb into the old town rather than riding it; the setts are polished and steep.
itinerary.evening: Krumlov after 18:00, when the day coaches have left, is a different place. The Baroque theatre in the castle is one of only a handful in the world with original stage machinery; tours are strictly limited and sell out.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km, +360 m, asphalt with cobbles in the old town.

itinerary.title: Lipno approach and the train home
itinerary.morning: Ride the Vltava upstream toward Zlatá Koruna's opposite bank or push on to Rožmberk nad Vltavou, a compact valley castle 25 km south. Turn where the legs say.
itinerary.afternoon: Return to Český Krumlov and take ČD line 194 north to České Budějovice. The line runs a bike wagon through the summer and it fills on Sunday afternoons, reserve, or take an earlier train.
itinerary.evening: Connect at České Budějovice for Prague. Bikes need a ticket and, on express services, a reserved bike slot.
itinerary.dayStats: 40 km, +320 m, asphalt with 4 km gravel.

items.subject: Hvar, Croatia
items.text: Glam Adriatic island

source.text: Hvar is an island off the coast of Croatia with a population of about 11,000 people (2011). Imposing fortifications hover above the fluid blend of grey stone and orange cascading roofs.

items.subject: Soroca, Moldova
items.text: Perfectly circular 15th-century fortress guarding the Dniester, plus the hilltop Candle of Gratitude

source.text: Soroca is a town in the northeastern part of Moldova.

items.subject: Underground Streets and Feteasca Neagră: A Week Through Codru and Ștefan Vodă
items.text: Moldova is the only wine country where you tour two of the cellars by car, windows down, headlights on, past street signs that read Cabernet and Feteasca. Above ground it is quieter than that sounds: low Codru…

trip_data.title: Underground Streets and Feteasca Neagră: A Week Through Codru and Ștefan Vodă
trip_data.best_period: the last ten days of September through the first weekend of October (harvest, then Ziua Națională a Vinului)
trip_data.avoid: July-early August (35 °C on the Bugeac steppe, cellars are the only cool place) and January-March (many small domains close their tasting rooms)
trip_data.difficulty: Easy
trip_data.gateway: Chișinău International (KIV), 13 km southeast of the centre; trolleybus 30 and bus 165 run into town, a taxi is €8 to €12 (150-230 MDL), there is no published airport tariff and meters are not reliably used, so hail through Yandex Go or Bolt and take the quoted fixed fare, which lands around 160 MDL for the 25-minute run; pre-booked private transfers start near €49 per car, which is money thrown away. Overland: Iași (Romania) is 3 h by road, Odesa 4 h. There is a slow overnight train from Bucharest to Chișinău.

itinerary.title: Chișinău, Landing and the First Glass
itinerary.morning: Land at KIV, drop bags, and orient on Bulevardul Ștefan cel Mare, the Arcul de Triumf, the Catedrala Nașterea Domnului with its free-standing belfry, the Ștefan cel Mare monument at the park gate. Twenty minutes fixes the city's grid in your head.
itinerary.afternoon: Piața Centrală for the food groundwork: barrels of must in season, sheep's brânză, walnuts, dried plums, and the divin counter. Then late plăcinte at La Plăcinte on Ștefan cel Mare.
itinerary.evening: A structured by-the-glass flight at Carpe Diem, the city's serious wine bar, ask for Viorica, then a Rara Neagră, then a Fetească Neagră, in that order. Dinner at Vatra Neamului for zeamă and mămăligă.
itinerary.dayStats: city walking, 4 km

itinerary.title: The Two Underground Cities
itinerary.morning: North to Cricova. The tour runs by electric train through galleries quarried for limestone and converted to wine storage in the 1950s; it holds 12-14 °C, so bring a jacket even in September. Finish in the tasting rooms on the traditional-method sparkling.
itinerary.afternoon: South through Chișinău to Mileștii Mici, driven along the underground avenues past the Golden Collection to a tasting hall; the scale, not the wine list, is the point. Allow an hour of city traffic between the two.
itinerary.evening: Eat lightly, Propaganda Cafe, or a bowl of zeamă near Parcul Catedralei. Two big lunches are coming.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km driving

itinerary.title: East to the Dniester: Bulboaca and Purcari
itinerary.morning: Out on the R30 to Castel Mimi at Bulboaca, 35 km east. Tour the restored 1893 cellar, then taste the Codru whites; with its garden, spa and restaurant this is the one stop here that works for a non-drinker.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue southeast to Château Purcari, 60 km on, for the Negru de Purcari vertical: Cabernet Sauvignon with Saperavi and Rara Neagră in French oak, and the 1878 Paris story told properly.
itinerary.evening: Stay at the Purcari Wine Resort, villas on the estate lake. Dinner is estate cooking with estate wine, which is exactly the point of driving this far.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km

itinerary.title: Ștefan Vodă Proper: Crocmaz and the Way Home
itinerary.morning: Walk the Purcari vineyard blocks before breakfast, the Dniester valley light at 07:30 is the photograph of the week. Then 20 km to Et Cetera at Crocmaz, the Luchianov brothers' domain: small, precise, and the best place in the country to understand Rara Neagră on its own.
itinerary.afternoon: Loop back northwest to Asconi at Puhăceni for a courtyard lunch, grilled meats, mămăligă, house Fetească Neagră, in the reconstructed village-street setting the estate built around its cellar.
itinerary.evening: Into Chișinău by early evening: sarmale and a glass of Fetească Regală somewhere unambitious. The week's second half is the harder driving.
itinerary.dayStats: 150 km

itinerary.title: Orheiul Vechi, the Non-Wine Day
itinerary.morning: North on the R14 to Orheiul Vechi, 55 km. Park at Butuceni and walk up the limestone promontory above the meander of the Răut to the cave monastery, a 13th-century hermitage cut into the cliff, with a bell tower on the ridge above and the church of the Ascension beside it. Cover shoulders; it is an active place of prayer.
itinerary.afternoon: Lunch in Butuceni, plăcinte, chicken zeamă, house wine from a plastic bottle, the honest other half of Moldovan wine culture. Then 18 km to Chateau Vartely above Orhei, tasting on the terrace.
itinerary.evening: Stay in a Butuceni guesthouse. No light pollution, and the promontory at dusk is worth walking twice.
itinerary.dayStats: 100 km

itinerary.title: South to Valul lui Traian: Tigheci and Cimișlia
itinerary.morning: The long day. Drive south from Chișinău through Hîncești and Leova toward the Tigheci hills for Fautor, the most convincing modern estate in the south, and the reference point for Moldovan Viorica and for late-harvest whites.
itinerary.afternoon: East across the Valul lui Traian earthwork toward Cimișlia for Gitana, whose reds are the broad, sun-driven counterweight to everything you drank in Codru. Ask to taste Rara Neagră from both zones back to back if the cellar will pour it.
itinerary.evening: Back in Chișinău around 19:00: a Bardar XO or Călărași divin, then an early night.
itinerary.dayStats: 280 km round trip

itinerary.title: Codru Garagistes and Wine Day
itinerary.morning: Small Codru producers within 40 km of the capital: Equinox, Novak, Atu Winery. Two of the three in a morning is realistic; all three is not. Here you meet the winemaker, not a guide.
itinerary.afternoon: If the trip is timed to the first weekend of October, this is Ziua Națională a Vinului, a hundred-odd producers pouring in Piața Marii Adunări Naționale. Buy the glass, walk the rows, find the four-hectare estates you will never see abroad.
itinerary.evening: Last supper at Gustar or back at Carpe Diem, then Piața Centrală in the morning for divin and walnuts to carry home. Duty-free allowances into the EU are two litres of wine and one of spirits per adult.

trip_data.title: Vilnius & Aukštaitija: Farmhouse Ale and Mead Road
trip_data.best_period: May to October. September-October for mushroom season, honey harvest and the beer festivals; June for cold soup season and Rasos midsummer
trip_data.budget: €940 to €1,755 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.

itinerary.title: Vilnius: the old town table
itinerary.morning: Arrive Vilnius. The old town is the largest surviving baroque old town in Eastern Europe, on the UNESCO list, and walkable end to end in forty minutes.
itinerary.afternoon: Halės Turgus, the covered market since 1906: rye bread, smoked meats, curd cheese, forest mushrooms and honey. Lunch here. Then Užupis, the self-declared artists' republic across the Vilnia river with its own constitution on a wall in thirty languages.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at one of the restaurants reinterpreting Lithuanian historical cuisine, the Grand Duchy's kitchen, with its game, rye and preserved fruit, is being seriously researched and cooked in Vilnius right now. `verify: true`

itinerary.title: Vilnius: beer bars and the modern kitchen
itinerary.morning: The Gediminas Tower and the Palace of the Grand Dukes for the context that explains the food: this was the capital of a state that stretched to the Black Sea.
itinerary.afternoon: Vilnius's farmhouse-beer bars are the point of this day. A handful of small bars in the old town and in Naujamiestis serve rotating kaimiškas alus from named village brewers, often unfiltered, low-carbonation, and unlike anything in the German or Belgian traditions.
itinerary.evening: Snack culture: smoked pig ears, kepta duona (fried garlic rye), curd cheese and salted peas, which exist specifically to be eaten with farmhouse ale.

itinerary.title: Trakai and the Karaim kitchen
itinerary.morning: Trakai, 30 minutes west: the island castle on Lake Galvė, red brick on water, rebuilt in the 20th century and unmistakable.
itinerary.afternoon: The Karaim community, a Turkic people brought here in the 14th century by Grand Duke Vytautas, still lives on the town's main street in three-windowed wooden houses. Their kibinai, a baked pastry of lamb and onion, is one of the region's great dishes and is made properly only here.
itinerary.evening: Return to Vilnius, or drive north to start the Aukštaitija leg.

itinerary.title: Aukštaitija: the farmhouse brewing heartland
itinerary.morning: Drive north toward Panevėžys and Pasvalys (about 2 h). This is flat, fertile, barley country and the last place in Europe where farmhouse brewing survived without a revival, it simply never stopped.
itinerary.afternoon: Visit an actual farm brewery. Jovarų Alus is the most famous, brewed by hand in a village with equipment that looks agricultural because it is. Arrangements must be made ahead and a Lithuanian-speaking guide helps enormously.
itinerary.evening: Biržai, the beer capital: a castle, a lake, and two large regional breweries in town alongside the farm producers. Dinner with local ale and skilandis.

itinerary.title: Biržai karst, Anykščiai and the fruit wines
itinerary.morning: The Kirkilai karst lakes outside Biržai, a landscape of sinkholes where the gypsum bedrock collapses, with a viewing tower over dozens of small water-filled craters.
itinerary.afternoon: South to Anykščiai for the fruit-wine tradition, Lithuania's berry and apple wines are a serious regional industry, plus the treetop walkway in the Anykščiai pine forest and the narrow-gauge railway.
itinerary.evening: Anykščiai or back toward Vilnius.

itinerary.title: Stakliškės mead and the Dzūkija forest
itinerary.morning: Stakliškės, south of Vilnius, is where Lithuanian mead is made to a documented traditional method, honey, water, hops and herbs, fermented and matured for months rather than fortified. The tasting explains why midus is closer to a wine than to the sweet mead most people expect.
itinerary.afternoon: Into Dzūkija National Park: pine forest, sand, and villages like Zervynos and Musteika, where the UNESCO-listed tree-beekeeping tradition is still practised, hives hollowed into living pines, worked with a rope and a climbing seat.
itinerary.evening: Mushrooms. Dzūkija is Lithuania's foraging heartland and in September the entire region is in the forest at dawn. A guesthouse dinner here will be built around what was picked that morning.

itinerary.title: Vilnius return and departure
itinerary.morning: Last market run at Halės or the Tymo market for honey, black bread, smoked cheese and a bottle of mead.
itinerary.afternoon: Vilnius airport is fifteen minutes from the old town.

items.subject: Andesite Milestones: A Gravel Week on the Via Transilvanica
items.text: A carved stone every kilometre, an orange T on a fence post, and 300 km of Transylvania that no road atlas makes look interesting. This is riding through hay meadows and oak forest between Saxon villages with…

trip_data.title: Andesite Milestones: A Gravel Week on the Via Transilvanica
trip_data.best_period: the first three weeks of September, hay cut, tracks dry, hills green, and the clay hard enough to ride
trip_data.avoid: any week after prolonged rain (the clay sections become unrideable) and mid-July-August heat
trip_data.difficulty: Moderate
trip_data.gateway: Fly into Sibiu (SBZ), Târgu Mureș (TGM) or Cluj (CLJ). CFR trains reach Sighișoara from Brașov (2 h 15), Cluj (3 h 30) and Bucharest (4 h 30-5 h). Finish on a train or flight out of Sibiu.

itinerary.title: Sighișoara and a shakedown
itinerary.morning: Arrive in Sighișoara, collect or build the bike, and walk the citadel, the Clock Tower, the Covered Stairway up to the Church on the Hill, and the last inhabited medieval citadel in Europe still functioning as a town.
itinerary.afternoon: A short loop east on the Via Transilvanica towards Hetiur and back, purely to find the orange T, meet your first milestone, and check that the gearing and tyre pressure suit 10% pasture ramps.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in the lower town. Set the bike up properly tonight: mud clearance, spare hanger, two tubes, and a chain that will survive clay.

itinerary.title: A taste of Terra Siculorum
itinerary.morning: Transfer or train north-east to Odorheiu Secuiesc, the Székely town at the heart of Terra Siculorum, Hungarian-speaking, with its own architecture and a completely different village pattern from the Saxon lands.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the Via Transilvanica back south-west out of Odorheiu through the Székely hill villages: long grassy doubletrack, oak woodland, and milestones set into hedgerows. This is the quietest riding of the week.
itinerary.evening: Finish at a guesthouse on the section end and eat kürtőskalács fresh off the spit. Székely cooking runs to gulyás and stuffed cabbage, order both.

itinerary.title: Saschiz, Criț and the clay
itinerary.morning: Back to Sighișoara and out west on the route to Saschiz, whose fortified church and hilltop citadel are UNESCO-listed as part of the Villages with Fortified Churches in Transylvania.
itinerary.afternoon: The section on to Criț is the first serious clay. Ridable and enjoyable dry; a shoulder-carry wet. Criț's church has a Saxon graveyard with almost no living German community left to fill it.
itinerary.evening: Down to Viscri. Guesthouse dinner, this village's houses were restored under the Mihai Eminescu Trust and the whole street is lime-washed in blues and greens.

itinerary.title: Viscri, Bunești and Rupea
itinerary.morning: The Viscri fortified church, UNESCO-listed, white-walled and unheated, plus the village blacksmith and the woollen-sock cooperative. Do this before riding; the coaches arrive at 11:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Out via Bunești, the junction village on the DN13, and the pasture climb to Rupea, where a huge basalt-hilltop citadel stands over the road, restored and open. The Rupea approach is the best descent of the week.
itinerary.evening: Guesthouse in Rupea or Homorod. Ciorbă, sarmale, palincă; ask the host to fill your bottles from the well rather than the tap.

itinerary.title: Homorod, Cața, Ungra
itinerary.morning: Homorod's Romanesque-cored fortified church, then a long forest-track section south, genuinely remote riding, with more roe deer than people.
itinerary.afternoon: Cața and Ungra, the two quietest Saxon villages on the route, on rolling clay and pasture. Ungra sits above the Olt; from the ridge the Făgăraș wall appears to the south, 2,500 m and usually with snow on it.
itinerary.evening: Guesthouse in the Făgăraș foothills. This is the day to check the forecast properly, everything from here west depends on whether the clay stays hard.

itinerary.title: North-west to Biertan and Richiș
itinerary.morning: Transfer or ride north-west to Biertan, whose fortified church, a triple ring of walls, the famous multi-locked sacristy door, was the seat of the Saxon Lutheran bishops and is the best-preserved of the lot.
itinerary.afternoon: The short, beautiful ride over the hill to Richiș, a village with a strikingly Gothic-Cistercian church and a slow trickle of returning Saxon descendants, then on towards Mediaș.
itinerary.evening: Mediaș: the leaning Trumpeters' Tower, a real town centre, and a proper restaurant meal after five days of guesthouse cooking.

itinerary.title: Into Sibiu
itinerary.morning: West out of Mediaș on the Terra Vinum ground, vineyards on the south-facing slopes, gravel between them, easier gradients than anything so far.
itinerary.afternoon: The long approach into Sibiu through Șura Mare, finishing in the Piața Mare. Wash the bike before you box it; Transylvanian clay sets like cement.
itinerary.evening: Sibiu. Eat on the Piața Mică under the Bridge of Lies, drink something local, and count how many andesite milestones you photographed.

items.subject: Faroe Islands Subsea Loop: Eighteen Islands, Six Tunnels
items.text: A seven-day road trips & scenic drive itinerary in Streymoy, Eysturoy, Norðoyar, Sandoy, Vágar, Faroe Islands.

trip_data.title: Faroe Islands Subsea Loop: Eighteen Islands, Six Tunnels
trip_data.best_period: May to September for open roads, ferries and puffins; late September for autumn light; winter driving is feasible but daylight is short and mountain roads close in gales
trip_data.budget: €1,605 to €2,630 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.

itinerary.title: Vágar: Gásadalur and the western edge
itinerary.morning: Land at Vágar, collect the car. Drive first to Bøur, a village of turf roofs facing the sea stacks of Tindhólmur.
itinerary.afternoon: Through the old single-lane tunnel, or the new one, to Gásadalur, a village of sixteen people that had no road access until 2004; the postman used to walk over the mountain three times a week. The Múlafossur waterfall drops straight off the cliff beside it into the Atlantic.
itinerary.evening: Sørvágur or Miðvágur for the night. Buy food; shops close early and are shut on Sundays.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km

itinerary.title: Streymoy: Saksun, Tjørnuvík and the old high road
itinerary.morning: Take the Oyggjarvegur, the old mountain road over Streymoy, rather than the tunnel, it climbs into cloud with the whole island beneath it.
itinerary.afternoon: Saksun: a turf-roofed church, a tidal lagoon that empties completely at low water, and a handful of farms in an amphitheatre of cliffs. Then across to Tjørnuvík on the north coast, facing the Risin og Kellingin sea stacks, the giant and the witch, petrified while trying to drag the Faroes to Iceland.
itinerary.evening: Drive to Tórshavn. Walk Tinganes, the peninsula of red turf-roofed government buildings where the Løgting has met since Viking times, arguably the oldest continuous parliamentary site in the world.
itinerary.dayStats: 90 km

itinerary.title: Eysturoy: Gjógv, Funningur and the pass
itinerary.morning: Through the Eysturoy subsea tunnel, past the illuminated undersea roundabout with its light installation and jellyfish sculpture. North to Funningur, said to be the first Norse settlement in the islands.
itinerary.afternoon: The Eiðisskarð pass beneath Slættaratindur (882 m, the highest point), then Gjógv, built around a 200 m natural sea gorge that served as its harbour.
itinerary.evening: Stay in Gjógv. There is one guesthouse, no restaurant, and complete silence.
itinerary.dayStats: 110 km

itinerary.title: Norðoyar: Klaksvík, Viðareiði and Kalsoy
itinerary.morning: The Norðoya tunnel to Klaksvík, the second town and the fishing capital, with the extraordinary Christianskirkjan, a modern church with a Viking longhouse form and a rowing boat hung from the ceiling.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to Viðareiði, the northernmost settlement, under Enniberg, one of the highest sea cliffs in Europe at 754 m. Alternatively take the small ferry from Klaksvík to Kalsoy and drive its chain of single-lane tunnels to Trøllanes for the Kallur lighthouse walk, the most photographed ridge in the Faroes. Ferry capacity is tiny; queue early. `verify: true`
itinerary.evening: Klaksvík. The town brewery is a national institution.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km + ferry

itinerary.title: Vestmanna bird cliffs and Sandoy
itinerary.morning: The Vestmanna sea-cliff boat trip: two hours through sea caves and under 600 m cliffs stacked with guillemots, fulmars and puffins. It cancels in swell, so treat it as first-choice-if-calm.
itinerary.afternoon: Through the new Sandoy tunnel to Sandoy, sand dunes, the village of Skopun, and Húsavík with its medieval ruins. Sandoy is where Faroese people go when they want to be somewhere quiet, which tells you something.
itinerary.evening: Back to Tórshavn.
itinerary.dayStats: 100 km + boat

itinerary.title: Tórshavn, Kirkjubøur and a home dinner
itinerary.morning: Kirkjubøur, the medieval episcopal seat: the roofless Gothic Magnus Cathedral begun around 1300, the small St Olav's church still in use, and Kirkjubøargarður, a farmhouse continuously inhabited for centuries.
itinerary.afternoon: Tórshavn properly, the National Museum, the Nordic House, the old town's black tarred houses with grass roofs, and the harbour.
itinerary.evening: Book a heimablídni: dinner in a Faroese family's home, several courses of lamb, fish and rhubarb, with the family eating alongside you. It is the single best thing you can do in the islands.
itinerary.dayStats: 40 km

itinerary.title: Trøllkonufingur, Sørvágsvatn or Mykines, then out
itinerary.morning: Depending on wind: the Mykines boat for puffins, or the short walk to the Trælanípa cliff over Sørvágsvatn.
itinerary.afternoon: Fly out from Vágar. Allow generous slack for weather.

items.subject: Andorra High Route: Comapedrosa, Juclà and the Madriu Valley
items.text: Andorra is 468 km² and nearly all of it is above 1,000 m, which makes it the densest walking country in the Pyrenees. This week takes its two defining landscapes: the granite bowl beneath Pic de Comapedrosa, 2,942 m, the country's high point, and the Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror, a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape covering nine per cent of the national territory with no road into it at all. Between them the route crosses the Sorteny and Juclà lake basins on the Coronallacs circuit. You sleep in a mixture of staffed refuges with cooked dinners and free unstaffed stone shelters. It suits confident hikers who like high, empty, lake-strewn granite country and do not need a village every night.

source.verified: Refugi del Comapedrosa at 2,260 m with 45 overnight places, open continuously from 1 June to 12 October with out-of-season bookings possible, reservations online at reserves.refugicomapedrosa.ad or by phone on +376 327 955 between 09:00 and 19:00, half board (bed, dinner, breakfast) at €55.80 and bed-only at €21.90, with the approach from Arinsal quoted as 2 h-2 h 30 min for 685 m of ascent. The existence of a Govern d'Andorra process approving public prices for the staffed Refugi de l'Illa, and the government's published network of staffed and unstaffed refuges and GR routes.

trip_data.title: Andorra High Route: Comapedrosa, Juclà and the Madriu Valley
trip_data.best_period: Late June-early October, with the staffed refuge window roughly 1 June-12 October
trip_data.avoid: November-May, the staffed refuges close, the high colls hold snow and the Madriu valley path ices in its lower gorge
trip_data.budget: €780 to €1,250 per person, excl. international flights
trip_data.difficulty: 4/5, a 2,942 m summit plus three consecutive days of 800-950 m ascent crossing colls above 2,700 m
trip_data.gateway: TLS Toulouse-Blagnac, 3 h to La Massana by bus or car; BCN Barcelona 3 h 15 min; LEU Andorra-La Seu d'Urgell 40 min

itinerary.title: La Massana, Ordino and the Sorteny valley
itinerary.morning: Arrive by coach from Toulouse or Barcelona (3 h-3 h 15 min) into Andorra la Vella, then the local bus up to La Massana, 1,230 m. Buy gas, maps and anything you forgot; Andorra's sports shops are duty-free and genuinely cheap.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive or bus to Ordino and walk into the Parc Natural de la Vall de Sorteny, an easy 8 km loop through the botanical meadows, over 700 plant species, to the Borda de Sorteny refuge at 1,970 m and back.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Borda Xixerella near Pal, a converted stone barn doing wood-grilled meats, trinxat and Andorran cheese, or at Molí dels Fanals in Sispony.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km / 450 m ascent / La Massana 1,230 m / Sorteny refuge 1,970 m / 3 h realistic / duty-free gas canisters available

itinerary.title: Arinsal to the Comapedrosa refuge
itinerary.morning: Start from Arinsal at 1,550 m, following the Riu de Comapedrosa past the Cascada de la Roca del Cabirol on a steadily steepening path through pine to the open cirque.
itinerary.afternoon: Reach the Refugi del Comapedrosa, 2,260 m, after 685 m of ascent, then spend the afternoon walking up to the Estany Negre and the Estanys de les Truites beneath the summit wall, good acclimatisation and the best light of the day on the granite.
itinerary.evening: Half board at the refuge (€55.80): soup, a stew, cheese, and a warden's briefing on tomorrow's snow and wind. Forty-five places, so it books out on August weekends.
itinerary.dayStats: 5.5 km / 710 m ascent / Arinsal 1,550 m / refuge 2,260 m / 2 h 45 min-3 h realistic / half board €55.80, bed only €21.90

itinerary.title: Pic de Comapedrosa, 2,942 m
itinerary.morning: Leave at 07:00 for the country's high point. Steep switchbacks to the Portella de Sanfons, then a stony ridge and a short easy scramble to the summit of Pic de Comapedrosa, 2,942 m, with France, Spain and the whole of Andorra laid out, the "roof of the Principality".
itinerary.afternoon: Descend by the Sanfons route or reverse the ascent, collect gear at the refuge, and continue down to Arinsal. Transfer across to Ordino or Canillo for the eastern half of the week.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Ordino's Plaça Major; Restaurant Armengol or the terrace at Coma. Andorran escudella and a Costers del Segre red.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km / 700 m ascent / 1,400 m descent / summit 2,942 m / 6 h 30 min-7 h 30 min realistic

itinerary.title: Sorteny to the Estanys de Juclà
itinerary.morning: Return to the Borda de Sorteny refuge, 1,970 m, and climb the Coronallacs stage east over the Collada dels Meners at roughly 2,713 m, a long grass-and-scree pull with old iron-mine workings near the top.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend into the Juclà basin and the Estanys de Juclà, the largest natural lake in Andorra, and check into the Refugi de Juclà at about 2,300 m on its shore.
itinerary.evening: Trout-coloured light on the lake at dusk, dinner in the refuge, and no phone signal to speak of. The Coronallacs stages are exactly this: one coll, one lake basin, one bed.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km / 900 m ascent / 550 m descent / Collada dels Meners approx. 2,713 m / 5 h 30 min-6 h 30 min realistic

itinerary.title: Vall d'Incles and the crossing to Refugi de l'Illa
itinerary.morning: South-west from Juclà, dropping toward the Vall d'Incles, a summer-shuttle-only valley of bordes and grazing, then climbing again past the Estanys de Cabana Sorda.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross the high ground around the Coll de Vall Civera (approx. 2,550 m) into the head of the Madriu and reach the Refugi de l'Illa, 2,488 m, a modern staffed refuge beside the Estany de l'Illa with the Riu Madriu starting at its door. It sits inside the UNESCO valley, whose tariffs are approved as public prices by the Andorran government.
itinerary.evening: The refuge's terrace faces east down the entire Madriu. Order tomorrow's packed lunch, it is a long, foodless day out.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km / 800 m ascent / 650 m descent / Coll de Vall Civera approx. 2,550 m / refuge 2,488 m / 6-7 h realistic

itinerary.title: The full Madriu: Perafita, Ràmio and Escaldes
itinerary.morning: Walk the length of the Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror, past the Pla de l'Ingla and the side turn to the free, unstaffed Refugi de Perafita, worth the detour to see how the unguarded system works: bunks, a table, a stove, nobody in charge.
itinerary.afternoon: The long stone-pitched descent past the bordes de Ràmio, the fangars charcoal platforms and the old irrigation channels, through a hanging beech gorge to Entremesaigües and out at Escaldes-Engordany, 1,100 m. There is no road the entire way, which is the point.
itinerary.evening: Caldea thermal spa in Escaldes (€45 to €55) is precisely engineered for legs that have just lost 1,400 m. Dinner afterwards at Can Manel in Andorra la Vella.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km / 250 m ascent / 1,400 m descent / Madriu valley 42 km², 9% of Andorra / 7-8 h realistic / no vehicle access anywhere in the valley

itinerary.title: Escaldes, the customs run and out
itinerary.morning: Walk the Madriu interpretation centre and the Romanesque església de Sant Miquel d'Engolasters above Escaldes, then the easy Rec del Solà balcony path over Andorra la Vella.
itinerary.afternoon: The duty-free shop before you leave is a national institution, but Andorra is outside the EU customs union and allowances are enforced at both the French and Spanish frontiers, typically around 1.5 litres of spirits, 300 cigarettes and a €900 goods value for adults. Do not over-buy.
itinerary.evening: Coach or drive out: 3 h 15 min to Barcelona, 3 h to Toulouse, or 40 minutes to the small La Seu d'Urgell airport.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km of town walking / Escaldes 1,100 m / customs allowance approx. €900 goods, 1.5 L spirits / BCN 3 h 15 min

items.subject: The Una's Green Water: Cabins, Travertine and Krajina Forest
items.text: The Una is a limestone river that builds its own bed: dissolved calcium precipitates out as travertine, forming stepped barriers, terraces and curtains that shift over decades, so the waterfalls here are alive rather than eroded. Una National Park, declared in 2008, protects 198 km² of that river plus the Unac tributary and the forest above. This week is deliberately low-mileage, a rafting day from Štrbački buk, a slow day of village bread and travertine at Martin Brod, a forest day toward Klekovača's old-growth beech and spruce, and evenings on a wooden deck with the water going past at walking pace. It suits people who want genuine quiet, low prices and a country that still surprises Western visitors, and who will take the landmine briefing seriously enough to stay on marked ground.

source.verified: Una National Park official price list, Štrbački buk/Lohovo zone 12 KM adult, 8 KM child 7-14, 4 KM senior 65+, free under 7; Lohovo entrance 4 KM; Martin Brod/Milančev buk 5 KM adult, 3.50 KM child; family packages 20 KM in April-May and October-November; rafting-section fees 15 KM (Štrbački buk-Lohovo) and 8 KM (Martin Brod-Kulen Vakuf); camping at Lučica 20 KM per person per day; tourist guide 100 KM up to 8 hours; fishing 50-60 KM daily and 120-140 KM for three days. BHMAC landmine contamination figures: over 820 km² still suspected, roughly 1.6% of territory, about 3,360 km² cleared of an original 4,180 km², clearance targeted at 75 km² a year.

trip_data.title: The Una's Green Water: Cabins, Travertine and Krajina Forest
trip_data.best_period: Late May-early July & September-mid-October
trip_data.avoid: December-March, riverside cabins close or run cold, forest tracks to Klekovača are snowbound, and the Una runs high and brown
trip_data.budget: €750 to €1,220 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.
trip_data.difficulty: 2/5, riverside walking, one 900 m forest ascent, and a rafting day; nothing technical
trip_data.gateway: ZAG Zagreb, 2 h 30 to Bihać via the Maljevac crossing; ZAD Zadar 2 h 45; SJJ Sarajevo 4 h 30

itinerary.title: Cross the border, land on the river at Bihać
itinerary.morning: Drive from Zagreb to the Maljevac or Ličko Petrovo Selo crossing, passports out, green card in the glovebox, and into Una-Sana canton. Change money and buy a local SIM in Bihać.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk Bihać's riverside: the Captain's Tower, the Fethija mosque (a Gothic church converted in the 16th century, unmistakable from its buttresses), and the Japodski otoci, a chain of wooded river islands linked by footbridges that the town uses as its swimming and picnic ground.
itinerary.evening: Grilled Una trout and a Bosnian coffee at a riverside restaurant on the Kostela cascade below town, with the falls audible over dinner.
itinerary.dayStats: 240 km / 2 h 30 plus border / BAM pegged at 1.95583 to €1 / local SIM roughly 10-20 KM / hospital in Bihać, the only one for 100 km

itinerary.title: Štrbački buk and the upper river
itinerary.morning: Drive to Orašac and take the forest spur to Štrbački buk, the Una's signature fall, a 24 m travertine drop into a green pool, viewed from wooden platforms that put you close enough to be soaked in spray. Buy the zone ticket at the entrance gate.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the riverside path downstream and swim in one of the flat reaches; the water sits around 12-14°C even in August, so this is a plunge, not a lounge. Cross into the Lohovo zone on the way back for the quieter Troslap and Dvoslap cascades.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Kulen Vakuf below the Ostrovica fortress, a 14th-century hilltop ruin above a village of 300 people.
itinerary.dayStats: NP zone ticket 12 KM adult (≈€6.10), 8 KM child, 4 KM senior / Lohovo entrance 4 KM / Štrbački buk 24 m / 12 km gravel spur from Orašac / water 12-14°C

itinerary.title: Rafting the Štrbački buk section
itinerary.morning: Raft the classic run from below Štrbački buk down to Lohovo, grade II-III at normal levels, with a few genuine drops over travertine steps and long green flat stretches between. Operators supply wetsuit, helmet and shuttle; the park charges a separate small water-use fee of 15 KM for this section.
itinerary.afternoon: Dry out at the take-out, eat the standard rafting lunch of grilled meat and bread, then do nothing for three hours. This is not a filler, the river week only works if you let some days empty out.
itinerary.evening: Back in Kulen Vakuf, walk up to the Ostrovica ruins for sunset over the Una's confluence with the Krušnica.
itinerary.dayStats: 15 km river / grade II-III / operator price typically €45 to €60 pp incl. equipment and shuttle / NP rafting fee 15 KM Štrbački buk-Lohovo / minimum age usually 12

itinerary.title: Martin Brod, Milančev buk and a slow village day
itinerary.morning: Drive south to Martin Brod, where the Unac joins the Una and the river disintegrates into a fan of travertine steps, Milančev buk and the Veliki and Mali buk, a hundred small falls rather than one big one. Buy the separate zone ticket.
itinerary.afternoon: Visit the 15th-century Rmanj Monastery at the confluence, then walk the village lanes past the old mills. Eat lunch where the sign is handwritten. In late September the road here smells of plum rakija being distilled in every second yard.
itinerary.evening: Nothing planned. Read on a deck. If you are here in late July, the Una Regatta, a mass descent of the river that has run since the 1990s and draws thousands of boats, turns this stretch into a festival and you should either join it or avoid the week entirely.
itinerary.dayStats: Martin Brod / Milančev buk zone ticket 5 KM adult, 3.50 KM child / 45 km from Kulen Vakuf / family package 20 KM in April-May and October-November

itinerary.title: Forest day toward Osječenica and Klekovača
itinerary.morning: With a park guide or a local driver, take the forest roads east toward Osječenica and the flanks of Klekovača (1,962 m), where some of the last old-growth beech and spruce in Bosnia stands in the Lom reserve. This is the one day that genuinely needs a 4x4 and genuinely needs someone who knows which side tracks are cleared ground.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk 8-10 km through the forest, looking for bear sign on the beech and listening for black woodpecker. Stay on the track. Mushroom season here is late September-early November and the ceps are extraordinary, within personal-use quantities and outside the park's strict zones.
itinerary.evening: Return to the valley for lamb slow-cooked under a sač (an iron bell buried in embers), order it in the morning, it takes four hours.
itinerary.dayStats: 40-50 km of forest road / Klekovača 1,962 m / guide 100 KM (≈€51) up to 8 h / zero mobile signal for 5 h / mine-marking signs mean stop, no exceptions

itinerary.title: Krušnica source, Ostrožac castle and the lower valley
itinerary.morning: Drive north to Bosanska Krupa and paddle or walk the Krušnica, a 5 km spring-fed tributary so clear it looks like the boats are floating on air. Canoe hire is cheap and the current is gentle.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Ostrožac, a fortress above the Una begun by the Habsburgs on a medieval base, half-ruined, half-restored, and virtually unvisited on a weekday.
itinerary.evening: Back to Bihać. Eat ćevapi in the old town, then coffee by the water while the swifts work the river.
itinerary.dayStats: 5 km Krušnica / canoe hire roughly 30-50 KM / Ostrožac 25 km from Bihać / river temperature 9-11°C at the Krušnica source

itinerary.title: Last morning on the water and out
itinerary.morning: Walk the Japodski otoci once more at 07:00, when the mist is still on the river and the town is empty, or fish a morning beat with a park permit, the Una's grayling and brown trout are the reason people fly here with rod tubes.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive north to the border and Zagreb, allowing an hour of contingency for the crossing on a summer weekend.
itinerary.evening: Zagreb, or straight to the airport.
itinerary.dayStats: Fishing permit 50-60 KM/day, 120-140 KM for three days / 240 km to ZAG / border queues of 1-2 h on July and August weekends

items.subject: Ski Arlberg, St. Anton, the Flexenbahn and the Valluga
items.text: A week based in St. Anton am Arlberg, using the Flexenbahn interconnect to ski Lech, Zürs and Warth, with a guided off-piste day and the Weisse Ring circuit.

trip_data.title: Ski Arlberg, St. Anton, the Flexenbahn and the Valluga
trip_data.gateway: Innsbruck (INN)

itinerary.title: Arrival and the Galzig shakedown
itinerary.morning: Land in Innsbruck, transfer by rail to St. Anton (1,304 m). The direct train from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof takes about an hour and drops you a five-minute walk from most central hotels.
itinerary.afternoon: Rent skis on the Dorfstrasse and buy the Ski Arlberg pass online in advance, a pre-loaded card saves the first-morning Galzigbahn queue. Ride the Galzigbahn gondola to 2,185 m for an easy recon lap back to the valley.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner and an early night. St. Anton's après-ski culture, centred on the Krazy Kanguruh at the base of the Galzig slope, runs loud from mid-afternoon; skip it on arrival day and save it for later in the week.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 600 m vertical · Galzig sector only · 2 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Rendl, the sunny side
itinerary.morning: Rendl is St. Anton's own separate sector, reached by a gondola from the southern edge of the village rather than through the main Galzig-Gampen lift chain. It faces south-east, so ski it on a cold, clear morning and avoid it by early afternoon in a hot spell, when the lower snow softens fast.
itinerary.afternoon: Rendl has the area's best lift-served, patrolled freeride-adjacent terrain: wide ridge bowls plus a dedicated freeride zone the ski patrol opens and closes by avalanche bulletin. Check the noticeboard at the Rendlbahn base before heading off-piste even within the marked zone, "open" here means avalanche-controlled, not risk-free.
itinerary.evening: Walk the short Dorfstrasse loop; St. Anton's old core is compact and everything is within ten minutes of the lifts.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 5,200 m vertical · Rendl sector · 5.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: The Weisse Ring
itinerary.morning: The Weisse Ring is a 22 km circular ski safari linking St. Anton, St. Christoph, Stuben and back, strung together on the Vallugabahn, Albonabahn and the Rendl/Gampen lift chains rather than one dedicated lift. Start at Galzig and ski clockwise via St. Christoph (1,800 m) to Stuben; a confident intermediate manages it in three to four hours.
itinerary.afternoon: From Stuben, the Albonabahn and Alberjoch chair carry you back to the St. Anton side, closing the loop past Rendl. The circuit's weak link is timing: the last connecting lift at Stuben closes earlier than the main Galzig lifts, and missing it means a bus back rather than a ski-back.
itinerary.evening: St. Christoph's small hamlet, one of the birthplaces of Austrian ski instruction, is worth a coffee stop if you have time before the last lift, otherwise save it for a future lap.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 22 km circuit, 4,300 m vertical · St. Anton-St. Christoph-Stuben sectors · 4 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Flexenbahn to Zürs and the Valluga
itinerary.morning: The Flexenbahn cable car, opened in 2016, is what actually makes "Ski Arlberg" one area rather than four resorts strung along a road. It runs from Alpe Rauz, above St. Anton, to Zürs in about six minutes, replacing an old bus transfer. Ride it early, wind holds are common above 2,000 m and the Flexenbahn is the first lift to suspend in a storm, splitting the interconnect in two.
itinerary.afternoon: From Zürs, ski across to Lech via the pistes and lifts around Zürsersee and the Rüfikopf. Lech is the quieter, more manicured half of the area, old wooden farmhouses, a slower pace than St. Anton. The Valluga cable car, the area's highest point at 2,811 m, is visible from most of Zürs; Valluga II, the upper stage, only carries skiers with a certified guide, because the descent is a narrow, exposed, glaciated ridge with real avalanche and fall exposure and no marked piste down.
itinerary.evening: Ride the Flexenbahn back to Alpe Rauz before the last car, check the posted last-departure time each morning, since it shifts with daylight and weather through the season, and bus or ski back into St. Anton.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 4,800 m vertical · Zürs-Lech sectors via Flexenbahn · 5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Guided off-piste day
itinerary.morning: Book a full day with a certified mountain guide through Piste to Powder, the town's established freeride and touring outfit, or the Skischule St. Anton's guided freeride programme. A guide is non-negotiable for the classic Arlberg lines off the back of Valluga and Kapall. Groups run four to six skiers; transceiver, probe and shovel are provided or checked on the spot.
itinerary.afternoon: A typical day runs a couloir or bowl off the Valluga or Schindlergrat, checking slope angle and aspect against the morning's avalanche bulletin, and finishes with a longer valley run toward St. Anton or St. Christoph. The guide reads the five-level European avalanche danger scale (1 Low to 5 Very High) posted daily and will change or cancel terrain choices on the spot, that flexibility is the point of paying for local knowledge.
itinerary.evening: A debrief drink is standard practice with these groups, worth staying for, since guides here often flag which slopes are worth another look later in the week.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 1,200-1,600 m vertical off-piste · Valluga/Schindlergrat/St. Christoph sectors · full guided day.

itinerary.title: Warth-Schröcken and the far end of the interconnect
itinerary.morning: Take the Flexenbahn again, continuing past Zürs and Lech to Warth-Schröcken, the interconnect's western end, joined to Lech only since a 2013 lift upgrade. Warth sits slightly higher and more sheltered than St. Anton's lower slopes, and in a thin-snow year is often the better sector by February.
itinerary.afternoon: Warth's terrain is broader and less crowded than St. Anton's, a good contrast day for tired legs. If the snowpack low down has been marginal, St. Anton's village-level runs sit at 1,304 m and suffer first in a warm spell, this is the bad-snow plan B for the week: stay high, on Warth-Schröcken and upper Zürs above 1,700 m, and treat any day below that as optional.
itinerary.evening: The return trip from Warth to St. Anton by lift needs a firm early-afternoon turnaround; missing the last Flexenbahn car means a long road transfer by bus around the valley, well over an hour.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 3,800 m vertical · Warth-Schröcken sector · 4.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Last laps and departure
itinerary.morning: A short final session on Gampen-Kapall, St. Anton's steep home sector above the village, suits those who want one more real run before packing.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop skis at the rental shop, shower, and train to Innsbruck. Build in a two-hour buffer, Sunday afternoon trains from the Arlberg run full with changeover traffic.
itinerary.evening: Flight home from Innsbruck.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 1,800 m vertical · Gampen-Kapall sector · 2 lift hours.

items.subject: The Vennbahn, Aachen to Troisvierges on a Borrowed Railway
items.text: A converted railway from Aachen to Luxembourg at railway gradients, crossing the High Fens, five German exclaves and three countries in 125 km.

trip_data.title: The Vennbahn, Aachen to Troisvierges on a Borrowed Railway
trip_data.gateway: Brussels (BRU)

itinerary.title: Aachen to Monschau through the exclaves
itinerary.morning: Pick up bikes in Aachen. Velocity Aachen on the Reichsweg hires trekking bikes and e-bikes and knows the Vennbahn well. Start at the Aachen Hauptbahnhof end of the trail and roll south through Kornelimünster, whose abbey and cobbled Benediktusplatz are worth ten minutes.
itinerary.afternoon: From Roetgen the trail turns strange. The trackbed is Belgian territory, so the German land east of it, Münsterbildchen, Roetgener Wald, Rückschlag, Mützenich, Ruitzhof, is cut off as five exclaves. Signposts change country every few kilometres. Asphalt, with crushed stone near Lammersdorf.
itinerary.evening: Drop off the plateau into Monschau, a half-timbered town wedged in the Rur gorge. The descent into town is steep and cobbled, walk it if the panniers are loaded.
itinerary.dayStats: 47 km, +390 m, asphalt with approx 4 km compacted crushed stone.

itinerary.title: The High Fens loop from Monschau
itinerary.morning: A luggage-free day onto the Hohes Venn. Ride via Kalterherberg and Sourbrodt to the Botrange Nature Centre and the Signal de Botrange, at 694 m the highest point in Belgium. The plateau boardwalks are for walkers only; bikes stay on the marked cycle routes and forest roads.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue past Baraque Michel and the Fagne de la Poleur, then descend the Hoëgne valley toward Sart before turning back east. This is the only day with real climbing, and the wind on the plateau does most of the damage.
itinerary.evening: Monschau's Senfmühle mustard mill and the glassblowers on the Marktplatz. Eat Rhenish, Sauerbraten, Reibekuchen, at one of the Rur-bank restaurants.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km, +620 m, mixed asphalt and gravel forest track.

itinerary.title: Down the Warche to Bütgenbach
itinerary.morning: Rejoin the Vennbahn southbound past Kalterherberg's oversized church and Küchelscheid, crossing into Belgium proper. The trail runs on embankments and through cuttings with the old station buildings still standing at Sourbrodt and Weywertz.
itinerary.afternoon: Detour west to the Robertville dam and Reinhardstein castle, then east along the Warche to the Bütgenbach lake. The dam-top road gives the classic view down the reservoir.
itinerary.evening: Worriken sits on the lake shore. Swim if it is August, otherwise walk the 8 km shoreline path at dusk.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km, +320 m, asphalt with approx 3 km gravel around the reservoirs.

itinerary.title: Elsenborn, Butgenbacher Heck and the Ourthe headwaters
itinerary.morning: A loop day. North-east across the Elsenborn ridge, open moorland, military training area boundaries clearly marked and to be respected, and down to Rocherath and Krinkelt.
itinerary.afternoon: Return via Bullingen and the Butgenbacher Heck woods on forestry gravel. This is the day to test a gravel bike or an e-MTB if you hired one; the surface is loose and the descents are fun rather than technical.
itinerary.evening: Ostbelgien's German-speaking Community has its own parliament in Eupen and its own beer culture. The Bütgenbach brewpubs pour local Ourdaller and Eifel beers.
itinerary.dayStats: 48 km, +540 m, roughly half compacted gravel.

itinerary.title: Bütgenbach to Sankt Vith
itinerary.morning: Straight down the Vennbahn through Weywertz and Born. This is textbook rail-trail: 1.5 per cent, cuttings, viaducts, and the occasional preserved goods shed. Surface is asphalt with a long crushed-limestone stretch approaching Sankt Vith.
itinerary.afternoon: Sankt Vith lost its railway and most of its old town in the Ardennes offensive of December 1944, and its history museum is direct about it. Short afternoon by design.
itinerary.evening: Sankt Vith eats better than a town of 9,000 has any right to. The dining room at Zur Post is the serious one in the German-speaking Community; book it before you leave home.
itinerary.dayStats: 36 km, +180 m, asphalt with approx 6 km crushed limestone.

itinerary.title: The Our valley and the three-country stone
itinerary.morning: South from Sankt Vith on the trail through Lommersweiler and Steinebrück into the Our valley, one of the prettiest and least visited river corridors in the Ardennes. Burg-Reuland's ruined keep sits directly above the path.
itinerary.afternoon: At Ouren the Our, the German border and the Luxembourg border meet. The Europadenkmal, three stones for the founding states, stands at the confluence. Cross the bridge, ride 300 metres, and you have been in three countries in five minutes. Then climb gently to Troisvierges over the Luxembourg border.
itinerary.evening: Troisvierges, Ëlwen in Luxembourgish, is the end of the Vennbahn and the northern terminus of CFL line 10. Modest, quiet, and the point where all your public transport becomes free.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km, +420 m, asphalt with approx 5 km gravel in the Our valley.

itinerary.title: Clervaux and the train home
itinerary.morning: Follow Luxembourg's national cycle network south from Troisvierges toward Clervaux, a short and steadily descending run through the Öslek forests.
itinerary.afternoon: Clervaux's castle holds The Family of Man, Edward Steichen's photographic exhibition and a UNESCO Memory of the World listing; entry approx €6. The Benedictine abbey above the town sings Vespers.
itinerary.evening: Board CFL at Clervaux for Luxembourg City, about an hour. Public transport in Luxembourg is free, bikes included where there is space, and no reservation exists to buy.
itinerary.dayStats: 26 km, −180 m net, asphalt.
