items.subject: Chamonix Freeride: Grands Montets, Vallée Blanche and the Off-Piste Circuit
items.text: A week of guided and self-directed freeride in Chamonix, built around the Vallée Blanche, Grands Montets and Le Tour, with avalanche and crevasse discipline throughout.

trip_data.title: Chamonix Freeride: Grands Montets, Vallée Blanche and the Off-Piste Circuit
trip_data.gateway: Geneva (GVA)

itinerary.title: Arrival and orientation
itinerary.morning: Fly into Geneva and take the shuttle or the Léman Express/Mont-Blanc Express rail combination to Chamonix. Check into the base hotel and rent skis or a splitboard, boots and an avalanche kit (transceiver, probe, shovel) from a rental shop on Rue Joseph Vallot or Rue du Docteur Paccard.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk to the Maison de la Montagne on Place de l'Église, home of the Compagnie des Guides de Chamonix and the Office de Haute Montagne (OHM), the free walk-in service where guides brief on snowpack, glacier conditions and the daily avalanche bulletin (Météo-France BRA). Buy the Chamonix Le Pass covering Brévent-Flégère, Grands Montets, Le Tour-Balme and Les Houches.
itinerary.evening: Group briefing with the guide if pre-booked, or a solo transceiver practice session in the search field most rental shops keep near their counters.
itinerary.dayStats: 0 vertical metres skied · 0 sectors · 0 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Brévent-Flégère, orientation day
itinerary.morning: Take the Téléphérique du Brévent from Chamonix centre up to 2,525 m. This south-facing sector catches the sun earliest and holds up best after fresh snow blows through the Grands Montets side, so it is the sensible opener while you read how the group skis together.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride across to La Flégère (1,877 m base, Index at 2,385 m) via the valley traverse, and ski the open bowls below the Refuge de Bellachat side of the ridge, staying inside the pisted boundary until the guide has assessed the day's danger rating on the European five-level scale.
itinerary.evening: Aprés-ski on Rue du Docteur Paccard; check tomorrow's Grands Montets lift status before dinner, the sector is wind-exposed and the Argentière side often closes above Lognan when the valley itself is calm.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 3,200 m vertical · 1 sector (Brévent-Flégère) · 4.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Grands Montets and the Argentière glacier
itinerary.morning: Bus to Argentière and ride the Télécabine de Plan-Joran. Note before you go: the historic cable car from Lognan to the Aiguille des Grands Montets summit (3,295 m) has been shut since a 2018 fire destroyed the mid-station, and the upper mountain has run on a reduced, rebuilt lift configuration since, check the current top station with the lift company before committing a day to this sector, the interconnect most likely to have changed since last season.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the accessible pistes and marked off-piste variants above Lognan, with views onto the Argentière glacier and the Aiguille Verte. With a guide, the Pas de Chèvre passage links this basin toward the Mer de Glace system for skiers planning ahead to the Vallée Blanche exit later in the week.
itinerary.evening: Early return to Chamonix; the Argentière-side buses thin out after 17:00.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,600 m vertical · 1 sector (Grands Montets) · 4 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Le Tour-Balme and the Vallée du Trient
itinerary.morning: Bus to Le Tour and ride the Télécabine de Charamillon to Col de Balme (2,270 m), the highest and most north-facing sector in the valley and the most snow-reliable when the lower mountain is thin.
itinerary.afternoon: With the Compagnie des Guides, this is the launch point for the Vallée du Trient ski tour: a short skin over the col into Switzerland, then a long glacier and forest descent past the Trient glacier toward Vallorcine, finishing at the train station. Crevasses on the upper glacier make this a roped, guided day only.
itinerary.evening: Train back from Vallorcine on the Mont-Blanc Express, a scenic 25-minute ride down the valley.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 1,900 m vertical (plus one uphill skin) · 1 sector (Le Tour-Balme) · 3 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Vallée Blanche, guided
itinerary.morning: Early start at the Aiguille du Midi téléphérique, arrive before 07:30 to beat the queue, since the ride to 3,842 m runs in two stages. Meet the Compagnie des Guides party at the top; the guide fits harnesses and rope for the exposed ridge walk off the summit station, the single most consequence-heavy few minutes of the week.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski or ride the Vallée Blanche itself: roughly 20 km and 2,700 m of descent down the Géant and Mer de Glace glaciers to Chamonix or, in low-snow years, to a shuttle pickup partway down. Crevasses are real and hidden by snow bridges; the route is skied roped and guided, never solo, regardless of how many tracks are already visible.
itinerary.evening: A long, satisfied dinner, this is the trip's centrepiece and most parties are tired by 18:00.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,700 m vertical · 1 itinerary (Vallée Blanche) · 1 lift ride (Aiguille du Midi).

itinerary.title: Second freeride day, weather-dependent
itinerary.morning: Check the Aiguille du Midi status before making plans, it is the valley's most wind-sensitive lift, with holds common above 60-70 km/h at altitude, so keep this day flexible. If it is running and conditions are stable, a second glacier tour (the Envers du Plan variant off the Vallée Blanche, or a return to Grands Montets) extends the week's off-piste mileage.
itinerary.afternoon: If the Midi is on hold, default to Grands Montets or Le Tour, both of which sit lower and are less exposed to wind than the Aiguille du Midi's summit ridge.
itinerary.evening: Gear rinse and dry, wet skins and rope need to dry overnight before packing.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,400 m vertical · 1 sector (weather-dependent) · 3.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Final morning and departure
itinerary.morning: A short session at Brévent-Flégère, the most forgiving last-morning sector, then return skis and boots by the shop's midday deadline.
itinerary.afternoon: Shuttle or train to Geneva for the flight home.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 1,200 m vertical · 1 sector (Brévent-Flégère) · 2 lift hours.

items.subject: Milos, Greece
items.text: Volcanic moonscape beaches

source.text: Milos is a volcanic Greek island in the Aegean Sea, just north of the Sea of Crete. Milos is the southwesternmost island in the Cyclades group. The island is famous for the Venus de Milo, a statue of Aphrodite, now in the Louvre.

items.subject: Kurzeme Slow Week: Kuldīga, Sabile & Talsi
items.text: A seven-day cozy towns trip itinerary in Kurzeme (Courland), western Latvia, Latvia.

trip_data.title: Kurzeme Slow Week: Kuldīga, Sabile & Talsi
trip_data.best_period: Mid-May to September. Late May for the lamprey and fish-jumping season at the Venta rapids; late July for the Sabile wine festival; September for mushrooms and empty guesthouses
trip_data.budget: €635 to €1,235 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.

itinerary.title: Riga to Kandava, into Courland
itinerary.morning: Collect a car in Riga and drive west (about 1 h 30). Stop at Tukums, a market town with a good regional museum.
itinerary.afternoon: Kandava: a tiny town of wooden houses on the Abava river, with a 19th-century stone bridge, the ruins of a Livonian Order castle mound, and a market square that has not changed in a century. Walk the Abava valley path.
itinerary.evening: Stay at a country guesthouse in the Abava valley. Dinner is whatever the hosts have cooked, ask when you book.

itinerary.title: Sabile: the northernmost vineyard
itinerary.morning: Sabile, population under a thousand, on a bend of the Abava. The Wine Hill (Vīna kalns) on the slope above the town has been cultivated since the Duchy of Courland in the 16th century and was long cited as the world's northernmost open-air commercial vineyard.
itinerary.afternoon: The town's small art house and the Sabile synagogue, restored as a cultural space commemorating the Jewish community murdered in 1941. Then the Pedvāle open-air art park across the river, 200 hectares of sculpture in a working farmed landscape.
itinerary.evening: If your week falls in late July, the Sabile Wine Festival takes over the town, a genuine village festival, not a marketing exercise. `verify: true`

itinerary.title: Kuldīga: the wooden town and Europe's widest waterfall
itinerary.morning: Drive to Kuldīga (about 50 minutes). Ventas rumba, the waterfall on the Venta, is only about 2 m high but 249 m wide, making it the widest in Europe. In spring and again in autumn, fish leap it, the Dukes of Courland had baskets set to catch them mid-air.
itinerary.afternoon: The old town: wooden and half-timbered 17th-19th century houses, the Alekšupīte stream running along the base of the buildings on Baznīcas iela, the "Venice of Kurzeme", and the 1874 red-brick road bridge, one of the longest of its kind in Europe.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at a restaurant built into the stream wall, with tables over the water. Kuldīga is the anchor of this itinerary; give it two nights.

itinerary.title: Kuldīga slow day: makers, market and Riežupe
itinerary.morning: The Saturday market if the day fits; otherwise the craft workshops, Kuldīga has an unusually strong ceramics and textile tradition and several working studios in the old town.
itinerary.afternoon: The Riežupe sand caves outside town, a 2 km network of hand-dug 19th-century tunnels in white sandstone, visited by lantern with a guide.
itinerary.evening: Kuldīga's town park and the old town at dusk, which is when the wooden facades and the stream are at their best. A concert in the church is likely; the town punches far above its size culturally.

itinerary.title: Talsi, the town of nine hills
itinerary.morning: Drive north to Talsi (about an hour). It is built around two lakes on nine hills, with wooden houses stacked on the slopes and a viewing point over the roofs from the castle mound.
itinerary.afternoon: The Talsi regional museum in a manor house, the lakeside promenade, and the small galleries. Then Dundaga's castle nearby, a Livonian Order fortress with a green crocodile statue in front, honouring a local emigrant said to have inspired Crocodile Dundee.
itinerary.evening: Stay in Talsi or at a manor guesthouse in the countryside around it.

itinerary.title: The coast: Ventspils and Pāvilosta
itinerary.morning: Drive to Ventspils, a port town that spent its oil money on parks, sculpture and a beach that has held Blue Flag status for years. The cow sculptures scattered through the town are a long-running civic joke.
itinerary.afternoon: South to Pāvilosta, a fishing village turned windsurfing town, with a boardwalk, a long empty beach, and Latvia's laid-back coastal end of the week.
itinerary.evening: Fresh fish at the Pāvilosta harbour, then a walk on the beach, the Baltic sunsets on this coast are the best in Latvia.

itinerary.title: Back to Riga via Jaunmoku or Rundāle
itinerary.morning: Slow drive east. Jaunmoku Palace near Tukums does an excellent lunch in a Tudor-revival hunting lodge.
itinerary.afternoon: If you can spare two hours, Rundāle Palace (an hour south of the direct route) is Rastrelli's Baroque masterpiece, the same architect as the Winter Palace, and is worth reshaping the drive for. Then Riga airport.

items.subject: Istria: The Parenzana & the Hilltowns
items.text: The Parenzana is an abandoned narrow-gauge railway that ran 123 km from Trieste to Poreč between 1902 and 1935, and its Croatian section is now the best-surfaced long gravel corridor in the northern Adriatic. This week uses it as a spine: hardpack embankments, unlit stone tunnels and viaducts through the Mirna valley, with detours climbing off it to Grožnjan, Motovun, Buje and Oprtalj, each a walled hilltown on its own knoll. Add a truffle lunch in Livade, two days of Malvazija tasting, an optional 1,401 m ascent of Vojak on Učka, and a finish on the Rovinj coast. It is the gentlest week in this collection on paper and the most tempting to overcook, because every hilltown demands a climb.

source.verified: The Parenzana's route Trieste/Muggia-Poreč and its promotion as a cross-border cycling trail; existence of Rental Center in Umag and CCT Bike Rental serving the Parenzana corridor; Bike Tours Istria running Parenzana packages; Croatia's euro adoption.

trip_data.title: Istria: The Parenzana & the Hilltowns
trip_data.best_period: Late April-mid-June & September-end October
trip_data.avoid: July-August, coastal roads saturated with Austrian and Italian holiday traffic, and the Mirna valley sits at 34°C with high humidity
trip_data.budget: €1,280 to €2,050 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.
trip_data.difficulty: 3/5, the rail-trail itself is graded at railway gradients, but the hilltown spurs and the optional Vojak day are genuinely hard
trip_data.gateway: TRS Trieste-Ronchi, 75 min to Buje; PUY Pula, 60 min to Motovun; LJU and VCE both around 2 h 30 min

itinerary.title: Buje, and the first tunnels
itinerary.morning: Transfer from Trieste to Buje and take delivery of the bike. Climb into Buje's old town for the loggia and the view over the Mirna basin, the whole week's terrain visible in one sweep.
itinerary.afternoon: Join the Parenzana north of Buje and ride the restored section toward Kostanjica, through the first stone tunnel and across the viaducts. Turn at Završje, a half-abandoned village with a leaning bell tower.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Morgan in Brtonigla, game, Istrian beef and one of the region's most serious wine lists, heavy on Teran and Malvazija.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km / 470 m ascent / 70% hardpack, 30% paved / two unlit tunnels

itinerary.title: Grožnjan, the artists' town on the ridge
itinerary.morning: Ride the Parenzana east and take the spur up to Grožnjan, 3.4 km at 6.8%. The town has been an artists' colony since the 1960s and its lanes are mostly galleries and studios; ride in early and it is silent.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to the trail and continue toward Livade through the longest tunnel section, then loop back on the valley road via Oprtalj's lower slopes.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Bastia in Grožnjan for fuži with truffle and a bottle of Kozlović Malvazija.
itinerary.dayStats: 54 km / 780 m ascent / 60% hardpack, 35% paved, 5% setts / Grožnjan summit 288 m

itinerary.title: Mirna valley, Livade truffles and up to Motovun
itinerary.morning: Follow the Parenzana into the Mirna valley floor and stop at the Parenzana Museum in Livade for the railway's history, rolling stock photographs and old timetables, €4, twenty minutes, worth it.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the valley flats to the Motovun forest, then the ramp: 1.6 km at 9.1%, setts for the final 400 m. Push if it is wet. Walk the Motovun town walls at golden hour.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Mondo just below the Motovun gate, the region's best-known truffle kitchen, small, book ahead. In autumn ask what the white truffle price is before ordering.
itinerary.dayStats: 47 km / 690 m ascent / 55% hardpack, 40% paved, 5% cobbles / Motovun 277 m, max 12%

itinerary.title: Oprtalj, Zavrsje and the Istrian interior
itinerary.morning: Climb north from Livade to Oprtalj (378 m), a 6.2 km ascent at 5.9% with continuous switchbacks and the finest single panorama in inland Istria.
itinerary.afternoon: A gravel loop through Sovinjak and Buzet's outskirts on farm hardpack, returning down the Mirna. Buzet is the truffle capital and its Subotina festival in September serves a giant truffle omelette in the square.
itinerary.evening: Restaurant Zigante in Livade, the truffle house that made the region's name. Expensive and unapologetic; the tasting menu runs €90 to €130.
itinerary.dayStats: 63 km / 1,120 m ascent / 45% hardpack, 55% paved / Oprtalj 6.2 km at 5.9%

itinerary.title: The Vojak day, or the Vižinada alternative
itinerary.morning: For the queen stage, van-transfer to Lovran and climb Učka: 22.6 km, 1,380 m, via Poklon at 922 m to Vojak at 1,401 m, with the Kvarner gulf and the Julian Alps from the summit tower. The Učka tunnel is closed to bikes, so this pass road is the only line.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the same way to Lovran, or continue to Opatija for the Lungomare. Riders skipping Vojak instead take the Parenzana west from Motovun to Vižinada and Baldaši, the loosest and least restored gravel on the route.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Batelina at Banjole near Pula if you have transport, a fish restaurant that treats offcuts and shark as seriously as sea bass. Otherwise Konoba Mondo again in Motovun.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km / 1,380 m ascent (Vojak option) or 52 km / 540 m (Vižinada option) / summit 1,401 m

itinerary.title: Parenzana to Poreč, then the coast to Rovinj
itinerary.morning: Complete the Parenzana to Poreč through Vižinada and Nova Vas, finishing at the sea. In Poreč, the Euphrasian Basilica's sixth-century apse mosaics are a UNESCO site and open all day.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride south on the coastal lanes via Funtana and Vrsar, skirting the Limski kanal, a drowned karst canyon rather than a fjord, whatever the signage says, into Rovinj.
itinerary.evening: Monte, just under the church of St Euphemia in Rovinj, holds a Michelin star; book weeks out. The cheaper move is grilled fish on the Rovinj waterfront.
itinerary.dayStats: 71 km / 640 m ascent / 50% hardpack, 50% paved / Parenzana Croatian section complete

itinerary.title: Rovinj, Bale and the ride out
itinerary.morning: A flat loop inland to Bale, a compact stone village with a Venetian palace, then back through the Kamenjak vineyards on white roads.
itinerary.afternoon: Return the bike at the operator's Rovinj or Poreč drop-off, then walk Rovinj's Grisia street up to St Euphemia and climb the 60 m bell tower.
itinerary.evening: Ice cream and a Malvazija on the Rovinj harbour before the Pula or Trieste transfer.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km / 380 m ascent / 65% paved, 35% white road / drop-off fee €40 to €70 outside the Parenzana corridor

items.subject: Bornholm Round: Granite Coast & Smokehouse Loop
items.text: A seven-day cycling trip itinerary in Bornholm, Baltic Sea, Denmark.

trip_data.title: Bornholm Round: Granite Coast & Smokehouse Loop
trip_data.best_period: Mid-May to mid-September; peak light and open smokehouses late June-August; quietest late May and first half of September
trip_data.budget: €1,035 to €1,690 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.
trip_data.difficulty: Easy-moderate. 105-135 km signposted loop split over 5 riding days; 300-450 m gain per day; no sustained climbs

itinerary.title: Arrival, Rønne and the west coast warm-up
itinerary.morning: Train from Copenhagen Central to Ystad in Sweden (about 1 h 40 with the through ticket), then the Bornholmslinjen fast ferry Ystad-Rønne, roughly 1 h 20. Collect bikes at a Rønne rental within walking distance of the terminal; ask for 32-38 mm tyres, they make the gravel sections painless.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the coastal path north to Hasle, an easy flat 12 km on asphalt with the Baltic on your left. Stop at Hasle Røgeri for your first sol over Gudhjem, smoked herring, raw egg yolk, radish, chives, rye.
itinerary.evening: Continue to Jons Kapel, a sea-cliff chapel formation reached by wooden stairs, then back to Rønne. Dinner at a harbourside table; early night, the ferry day is longer than it reads.
itinerary.dayStats: 24 km, asphalt

itinerary.title: Rønne to Allinge via Hammershus
itinerary.morning: North on the coast route through Sorthat-Muleby and Hasle, then onto the Ringebakkerne cliff section, this is the most dramatic asphalt on the island, quarried granite falling straight into the sea.
itinerary.afternoon: Hammershus, the largest medieval fortress ruin in Northern Europe, with the low-slung visitor centre built into the hillside opposite. Allow two hours. Push on over Hammerknuden past Hammer Fyr lighthouse and the flooded Opalsøen quarry.
itinerary.evening: Roll down into Sandvig and Allinge. Dinner at Nordlandet's restaurant if you want the design-hotel version of the island, or the harbour grill in Allinge for the honest one.
itinerary.dayStats: 36 km, 420 m gain

itinerary.title: Allinge to Gudhjem, round churches and Christiansø
itinerary.morning: Inland loop to Olsker and Østerlars round churches, Østerlars is the largest and oldest of the four, a whitewashed defensive drum from around 1160.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to Gudhjem, the steepest little town on Bornholm, and take the Christiansøfarten boat to Christiansø in the Ertholmene group, about an hour each way. No bikes, no cars, 90 residents, a 17th-century naval fortress and the country's easternmost point.
itinerary.evening: Back in Gudhjem, dinner at the harbour, then walk up Bokul rock for sunset over the roofs.
itinerary.dayStats: 28 km

itinerary.title: Gudhjem to Svaneke, the craft corridor
itinerary.morning: Coastal ride via Melsted and Listed. Stop at Bornholms Kunstmuseum on the Helligdomsklipperne cliffs, the building is worth the ticket on its own.
itinerary.afternoon: Svaneke, Denmark's best-preserved small town and the island's maker capital: Svaneke Bryghus for beer, Svaneke Chokoladeri, Pernille Bülow's glassblowing workshop, Bornholms Mosteri for apple must.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Svaneke; if you have booked far ahead, this is the night to drive or taxi to Kadeau Bornholm at Sømarken for the island tasting menu.
itinerary.dayStats: 26 km

itinerary.title: Svaneke to Dueodde and Aakirkeby
itinerary.morning: South through Nexø, then the long white sand of Dueodde, the finest-grained beach in Denmark, used historically for hourglasses. Lighthouse climb for the flat forest view.
itinerary.afternoon: Turn inland on the old railway grade (compacted gravel) toward Aakirkeby, passing Hallegård farm shop for smoked sausage.
itinerary.evening: Stay near Aakirkeby or Sømarken. Quiet interior night; stars are excellent here.
itinerary.dayStats: 34 km, mixed surface

itinerary.title: Almindingen forest and Ekkodalen
itinerary.morning: Into Almindingen, Denmark's third-largest forest. Ride the gravel through Ekkodalen, the echo valley, a rift with 20 m rock walls, and climb Rytterknægten (162 m), the island's high point, with the Kongemindet tower on top.
itinerary.afternoon: Paradisbakkerne on the eastern edge: granite hills, glacial erratics, marked walking trails if you want to leave the bike. Loop back west to Nylars round church, the best preserved of the four.
itinerary.evening: Return to Rønne. Dinner and a last harbour beer.
itinerary.dayStats: 30 km, 450 m gain

itinerary.title: Coastal spin and departure
itinerary.morning: Short flat spin south to Arnager and its long wooden pier, then back. Return bikes.
itinerary.afternoon: Ferry Rønne-Ystad, train to Copenhagen. If you have a late flight, the alternative is the Rønne-Køge overnight route (about 5.5 h) which takes bikes without fuss.

items.text: Dramatic Scottish island

source.text: Skye (Gaelic: An t-Eilean Sgitheanach) is the largest and most northerly of the Inner Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland, linked to the mainland by a toll-free bridge. It's a rugged mountainous island with spectacular scenery.

items.subject: Hemsedal & Hallingdal: Alpine and Nordic
items.text: A seven-day winter sports & skiing itinerary in Hallingdal, Viken, Hemsedal and Geilo, Norway.

trip_data.title: Hemsedal & Hallingdal: Alpine and Nordic
trip_data.best_period: Late November to early May. February to mid-April is the core: reliable base, returning light and the best ski-touring conditions. December and January are dark and very cold; late April brings spring corn snow
trip_data.budget: €1,980 to €3,320 per person for 7 days, the sum of the breakdown.

itinerary.title: Oslo to Hemsedal
itinerary.morning: Train from Oslo on the Bergen line to Gol (about 3 h), then bus or transfer 40 minutes to Hemsedal. Alternatively drive, roughly 3 h 30 on winter roads with studded tyres.
itinerary.afternoon: Collect the pass and hire gear. Ski a few laps on the lower mountain to find your feet on Norwegian snow, which is drier and faster than Alpine.
itinerary.evening: Hemsedal's base village is small and its après is the liveliest in Norway. Eat in the apartment; drink out, if the Norwegian bar prices do not stop you.

itinerary.title: The full mountain
itinerary.morning: Ride to the top sector. Hemsedal's vertical is over 800 m, which is Alpine-scale by Nordic standards, and the top-to-bottom runs are long enough to burn legs.
itinerary.afternoon: The black pitches under the summit lifts, and the long blues that wrap the fell. Wind is the constraint here: the highest lifts close in gales more often than snow ever stops play.
itinerary.evening: Sauna, then a proper dinner. Norwegian mountain restaurants do reindeer and Arctic char extremely well.

itinerary.title: Off-piste and the Hydalen valley
itinerary.morning: Book a guide. Hemsedal's off-piste, particularly the Hydalen valley behind the resort, is the reason experienced skiers come here, and it is avalanche terrain requiring transceiver, shovel and probe.
itinerary.afternoon: The guided day typically combines a short skin with lift-accessed lines. Norwegian guides are pragmatic and will change plans based on the avalanche bulletin without discussion.
itinerary.evening: Check varsom.no, Norway's national avalanche forecast, published in English, before every off-piste day. It is the standard reference and it is excellent.

itinerary.title: Nordic day on the Hemsedal and Golsfjellet tracks
itinerary.morning: Hallingdal has an enormous groomed cross-country network, and Norwegian Nordic culture is the deepest in the world. Hire classic skis and take the marked tracks out onto the plateau.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski to a koie or a mountain café and eat waffles with brown cheese, which is the entire point of Norwegian cross-country skiing.
itinerary.evening: An easy night. Norwegians go to bed early and get up at 08:00 to ski.

itinerary.title: Geilo and the Hallingskarvet
itinerary.morning: Drive or take the train an hour to Geilo, where Norwegian skiing effectively started in the 1930s. Two linked mountainsides, gentler than Hemsedal, with a village on the railway.
itinerary.afternoon: Geilo's Nordic terrain runs up onto Hallingskarvet National Park's plateau, a vast flat-topped massif and one of the great Nordic ski landscapes.
itinerary.evening: Geilo, or back to Hemsedal.

itinerary.title: Ski touring on Skogshorn or a resort day
itinerary.morning: Skogshorn (1,728 m) above Hemsedal is the classic local ski tour: a skinning ascent with a long open descent, guided in the right conditions. Alternatively spend a last full day on the lifts.
itinerary.afternoon: If the weather closes in, Hemsedal's lower mountain and tree runs keep working when the top is shut.
itinerary.evening: Last night. Norwegian après peaks on the final evening and the base bars have live music.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.morning: Half-day skiing if the pass allows, or an early Nordic loop.
itinerary.afternoon: Transfer to Gol and the Bergen-line train to Oslo, or continue west to Bergen, which is one of Europe's most spectacular rail journeys and takes about five hours from Gol.

items.subject: Enkhuizen, Netherlands
items.text: Preserved VOC port on the IJsselmeer whose open-air Zuiderzee Museum recreates vanished fishing life.

source.text: The small city of Enkhuizen is an old Dutch harbour town, and one of the most prominent ones of the Dutch Golden Age. It lost its trade position by the late 17th century, due to the wars with England, the silting of its waters and the rise of Amsterdam, but maintained much of its historic grandeur.

items.subject: Sofia in a day
items.text: Sofia in a day is a one day city sightseeing walk between the city main sights. This route is anchored in Sofia, BG and features 10 sightseeing stops.
